dervis-irab:1-5.t:
* Vocabulary:
(النَّجْوَى): secret talk; it is a noun from al-tanājī (confiding with one another), and it is only ever hidden. In al-Qāmūs: "It is a description by a maṣdar (verbal noun), in which singular and plural are alike; one says: هم نجوى (they are [people in] secret counsel)."
(أَضْغاثُ أَحْلامٍ): jumbled things one sees in sleep; its discussion has preceded.

* I'rab:
(اقْتَرَبَ لِلنَّاسِ حِسابُهُمْ وَهُمْ فِي غَفْلَةٍ مُعْرِضُونَ): اقترب is a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa; للناس is attached to (mutaʿalliq) اقترب. It may also be an emphasis of the ascription of the reckoning to them, as when you say أزف للحي رحيلهم ("their departure has drawn near for the tribe"); the original is أزف رحيل الحي, then أزف للحي الرحيل, then أزف للحي رحيلهم. حسابهم is the fāʿil (agent) of اقترب, because everything that is coming is near, however long the interval. The wāw is of the ḥāl (circumstantial); هم is a mubtadaʾ (subject), في غفلة is the khabar (predicate), and معرضون is a second khabar. (ما يَأْتِيهِمْ مِنْ ذِكْرٍ مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ مُحْدَثٍ إِلَّا اسْتَمَعُوهُ وَهُمْ يَلْعَبُونَ): the clause gives the cause of the preceding clause, so it has no grammatical position. ما is negative; يأتيهم is an imperfect verb, and the hāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); من is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition, because it is preceded by negation; ذكر is genitive in form and nominative in position as the fāʿil; من ربهم is an adjective (naʿt) of ذكر, and محدث is a second adjective. من ربهم may also be attached to يأتيهم, or to an omitted ḥāl of ذكر, since it is described by محدث. إلا is a particle of restriction, because the exception is emptied (mufarragh). The clause استمعوه is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl of the object of يأتيهم, with قد implied. وهم: the wāw is circumstantial, هم is a mubtadaʾ, and the clause يلعبون is the khabar of هم; the clause is accusative as a ḥāl of the fāʿil of استمعوه. Moreover, the description of the reminder (al-dhikr) as "new" (muḥdath) has been taken as proof that the Qur'an is originated (muḥdath), since the reminder here is the Qur'an. The answer given is that there is no dispute about the originatedness of what is composed of sounds and letters, since it is renewed in being sent down, so the meaning is "its sending down is new"; the dispute concerns only the inner speech (al-kalām al-nafsī).
(لاهِيَةً قُلُوبُهُمْ وَأَسَرُّوا النَّجْوَى الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا هَلْ هذا إِلَّا بَشَرٌ مِثْلُكُمْ): لاهية is likewise a ḥāl of the fāʿil of يلعبون, so it is an overlapping (mutadākhila) ḥāl; it may also be a ḥāl of the fāʿil of استمعوه, in which case the two ḥāls are consecutive (mutarādifa), since a ḥāl may be multiple. قلوبهم is the fāʿil of لاهية. أسروا is a verb and its fāʿil, and النجوى is the mafʿūl bihi. الذين is a badal (substitute) of the wāw of وأسروا النجوى, to indicate that they are the ones branded with the gross wrongdoing they committed; more on the parsing of this word will come in the section on benefits. The clause ظلموا is the ṣila (relative clause). هل is an interrogative particle, هذا is a mubtadaʾ, إلا is a particle of restriction, and بشر is the khabar; مثلكم is an adjective. The interrogative clause is in the position of accusative as a badal of النجوى, since it serves as its explanation. Al-Zamakhsharī allowed it to be in the position of accusative as the object of an omitted verb of saying; it may also be in the position of accusative as the reported content of النجوى, since that has the meaning of saying. I see nothing to prevent it [Translator's note: the source has «من أتكون», a misprint for «من أن تكون»] from being a clause with no grammatical position, because it is explicative. (أَفَتَأْتُونَ السِّحْرَ وَأَنْتُمْ تُبْصِرُونَ): the preceding views apply to this clause as well. The hamza is interrogative, and the fāʾ is a conjunction onto something implied; تأتون السحر is an imperfect verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi. The wāw is of the ḥāl; أنتم is a mubtadaʾ and the clause تبصرون is the khabar; the clause وأنتم تبصرون is a ḥāl of the fāʿil of تأتون, reinforcing the denial. (قالَ رَبِّي يَعْلَمُ الْقَوْلَ فِي السَّماءِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَهُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ): ربي is a mubtadaʾ and the clause يعلم القول is the khabar; the clause is the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl). في السماء والأرض is attached to an omitted ḥāl of القول, or to يعلم. وهو: the wāw is a conjunction, هو is a mubtadaʾ, and السميع العليم are two khabars of هو; what they are attached to is omitted because it is known, i.e. "the One who hears what they kept secret, and knows it".
(بَلْ قالُوا أَضْغاثُ أَحْلامٍ بَلِ افْتَراهُ بَلْ هُوَ شاعِرٌ): they turned away from their saying "it is magic" and said "it is jumbled dreams". So أضغاث أحلام is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, and the clause is in the position of accusative as the object of قالوا. بل افتراه: then they turned away from that and said "he invented it"; افتراه is a past verb, a latent (mustatir) fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi. Then they turned away again and said هو شاعر, a mubtadaʾ and a khabar. (فَلْيَأْتِنا بِآيَةٍ كَما أُرْسِلَ الْأَوَّلُونَ): the fāʾ is the faṣīḥa, because it discloses an implied condition, as though it were said: "and if it is not as we said, then let him bring us". The lām is the lām of command; يأت is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the lām of command, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the weak letter; the fāʿil is latent, its implied form being "he"; نا is an attached pronoun in the position of accusative as the mafʿūl bihi. The kāf [of كما] may be an adjective of آية, i.e. "being like the sign with which the former ones were sent", in which case ما is a relative noun; it may also be an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, with ما maṣdariyya, i.e. "let him bring us a sign, a bringing like the sending of the former ones". [Translator's note: the source says «كما يجوز في الكاف» ("as it is also permissible for the kāf"), though no preceding alternative for the kāf is given; translated as written.]

* Benefits:
The saying of the Exalted «وَأَسَرُّوا النَّجْوَى الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا». Abū al-Baqāʾ said:
"Regarding الذين ظلموا, there are three views on its position. The first: nominative, and in it there are four views:
a- That it is a badal of the wāw in وأسروا.
b- That it is the fāʿil, the wāw being a particle marking plurality, not a noun.
c- That it is a mubtadaʾ, its khabar being هل هذا, the implied sense being: 'they say: is this...?'
d- That it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. 'they are those who did wrong'.
The second: that it is accusative by an implied أعني ('I mean').
The third: that it is genitive as an adjective of الناس."
It is well known that the verb must remain in the singular form with its fāʿil, even if [the fāʿil] is dual or plural. Ibn Mālik said:
وجرد الفعل إذا ما أسندا ... لاثنين أو جمع كفاز الشهدا
(Strip the verb [of dual/plural markers] when it is ascribed to two or to a plural, as in فاز الشهدا "the martyrs have won".)
except in a weak dialect of some Arabs, in which the verb agrees with the fāʿil. The Basrans reported it from Ṭayyiʾ, and some reported it from Azd Shanūʾa [Translator's note: the source prints «ازدشنوءة»], e.g. ضربوني قومك ("your people struck me"), ضربنني نسوتك ("your women struck me") and ضرباني أخواك ("your two brothers struck me"). In the hadith: «أو مخرجيّ هم» ("Will they drive me out?"). And ʿAmr ibn Milqaṭ, the pre-Islamic poet, said:
ألفيتا عيناك عند القفا ... أولى فأولى لك ذا واقيه
(Your two eyes were found at the nape of your neck — woe upon woe to you, O you who seek protection!)
ألفيتا, in the passive, is a past verb and عيناك is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); so the verb received the dual marker even though it is ascribed to an overt noun, and the nāʾib fāʿil is like the fāʿil. عند is an adverb meaning "near", attached to ألفيتا. ذا واقية is a ḥāl of the muḍāf ilayhi, namely the kāf; واقية is a maṣdar meaning protection (wiqāya), like كاذبة, a maṣdar meaning lying. أولى فأولى لك is an imprecation, i.e. "may what will destroy you come near you". Al-ʿAynī said: "If you ask: what is the grammatical position of أولى? I say: it may be in the position of nominative as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being 'my prayer [against you] is أولى لك'; فأولى لك is conjoined to the first أولى, repeated for emphasis." Abū al-Baqāʾ said in parsing أولى لك فأولى: there are two views on it. One is that it is [on the pattern] faʿlā, its alif being for attachment (ilḥāq), not for the feminine; the other is that it is afʿal. On both views it is [non-tanwīned] here, and that is why it was not given tanwīn; this is indicated by what Abū Zayd reported in al-Nawādir: هي أولاة with tāʾ [Translator's note: the source prints «أولات»]. It is a diptote because it has become a proper name for the threat, like a man named Aḥmad. On this view أولى is a mubtadaʾ and لك the khabar. The second is that it is an indeclinable verbal noun (ism fiʿl), meaning "woe to you, evil after evil", with لك for clarification. In this verse he describes a man who, when the battle grows fierce, turns to look behind him for fear of being pursued, so that his eyes are found at the back of his neck from the intensity of turning. And Abū Firās said:
تنج الربيع محاسنا ... ألقحنها غر السحائب
(Spring brings forth beauties, which the bright clouds impregnated.) [Translator's note: the verb تنج, with the feminine plural agreement in ألقحنها, illustrates the same dialect; the source prints the line this way.]
Abū Firās is one of the post-classical poets (muwalladūn), and the purpose in [citing] his words is illustration, not evidentiary citation (istishhād).
Shaykh Muṣṭafā al-Ghalāyīnī held a fine opinion, and we shall cite his text: "Whatever of this occurs in eloquent speech, the overt noun is parsed as a badal of the pronoun — and on this basis is the saying of the Exalted (وَأَسَرُّوا النَّجْوَى الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا) — or the overt noun is parsed as a mubtadaʾ and the clause before it as a fronted khabar, or it is parsed as the fāʿil of an omitted verb, as though, after His saying وأسروا النجوى, it were asked: 'Who kept it secret?' and the reply were: 'Those who did wrong kept it secret.' This is the correct view, and it applies only where the context calls for implying an interrogative statement, as you see in the noble verse." We reckon that the matter has been discussed sufficiently, so what has preceded is enough for us.

dervis-irab:6-13.t:
* Vocabulary:
(قَصَمْنا): qaṣm is more intense than breaking (kasr). In al-Qāmūs: "qaṣama, of the pattern ṣaraba [Translator's note: so in the source, «صرب», evidently for ḍaraba «ضرب»], qaṣman al-shayʾ: he broke it; qaṣama al-rajul: he destroyed him; and one says: qaṣama Allāh ẓahr al-ẓālim, i.e. He brought calamity down upon him." The qāf together with the ṣād as the first and second radicals of a word holds a wonderful secret: they indicate breaking, effacing and destroying. Thus they say qaṣaba al-shāh, meaning he cut the sheep into pieces, limb by limb; from it the butcher is called al-qaṣṣāb, i.e. the slaughterer. Al-qaṣṣāba is the feminine of al-qaṣṣāb, and it has another meaning, namely what we today call "the nāy", i.e. a reed blown into for singing. From one of the Arabs: "I composed some verses, and Ḥakam al-Wādī sang them; by Allah, he did not move a qaṣṣāba with them but that I feared the Fire, so I gave up composing poetry" — and it is the string [Translator's note: so in the source]; and nafakha fī al-qaṣṣāba: in the pipe (mizmār). Aqṣadathu al-maniyya: death destroyed him; from it qaṣada al-rajul: he came to him and headed in his direction. Qaṣartuhu: I confined him; qaṣartu nafsī ʿalā hādhā al-amr when you do not aspire to anything else; qaṣartu ṭarfī: I did not raise my glance to what is improper; and hunna qāṣirāt al-ṭarf: they restrict it to their husbands. Qaṣṣa al-shaʿr wa-l-rīsh (he clipped hair and feathers) and qaṣṣaṣahu are well known, and a wing is maqṣūṣ and muqaṣṣaṣ. Qaṣaʿa al-ṣuʾāb bayna ẓufrayhi: he killed the nit between his two nails; qaṣaʿat al-raḥā al-ḥabb: the mill crushed the grain; and a ṣabī qaṣīʿ is a stunted boy who does not grow. Qaṣafa al-qanāt wa-l-ʿūd: he broke the spear-shaft and the stick; qaṣafa ẓahrahu, and a man is maqṣūf; the common people say to someone they curse "yā maqṣūf", and it is eloquent Arabic with nothing wrong in it. A wind blew and broke (qaṣafat) the ship; and a stick that is qaṣif: quick to break. Al-Ṭirimmāḥ said:
تميم تمنّى الحرب ما لم ألاقها ... وهم قصف العيدان في الحرب خورها
(Tamīm long for war as long as I have not met them, yet in war they are brittle sticks, feeble.)
Qaṣalahu: he cut it off quickly (qaṭʿan wa-ḥayyan); a sword is qāṣil, qaṣṣāl and miqṣal; qaṣala farasahu yaqṣiluhu: he fed his horse green fodder (al-qaṣīl); from it is al-miqṣala (the guillotine), an instrument of execution consisting of a blade that falls upon the head of the criminal and cuts it off. Qaṣā yaqṣū qaṣwan, quṣuwwan, qaṣan and qaṣāʾan al-rajul: he went far away; and in farness there is an allusion to destruction, because it too is a going far.
(أُتْرِفْتُمْ): you were given ease of a comfortable life and a soft condition; al-itrāf is to make one insolent through blessing.

* I'rab:
(ما آمَنَتْ قَبْلَهُمْ مِنْ قَرْيَةٍ أَهْلَكْناها أَفَهُمْ يُؤْمِنُونَ): ما is negative; آمنت is a past verb and the tāʾ is for the feminine; the clause is resumptive, brought to affirm their disbelief and to deem their believing far-fetched. قبلهم is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) آمنت; من is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition; قرية is genitive in form and in position the fāʿil (agent) of آمنت; the clause أهلكناها is an adjective (naʿt) of قرية. What is meant by the town is its people, as will come in the section on rhetoric. أفهم: the hamza is for the interrogative of denial, the fāʾ is a conjunction, هم is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause يؤمنون is the khabar (predicate). (وَما أَرْسَلْنا قَبْلَكَ إِلَّا رِجالًا نُوحِي إِلَيْهِمْ): the wāw is a conjunction, ما is negative, أرسلنا is a past verb and its fāʿil, إلا is a particle of restriction, رجالا is the object of أرسلنا, and the clause نوحي إليهم is an adjective of رجالا; the imperfect form is used to narrate a past state. (فَسْئَلُوا أَهْلَ الذِّكْرِ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ لا تَعْلَمُونَ): the fāʾ is the faṣīḥa (the fāʾ of an implied condition); اسألوا is an imperative verb and its fāʿil, and أهل الذكر is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object). إن is conditional; كنتم is a defective past verb in the position of jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), the tāʾ is its noun, and the clause لا تعلمون is its khabar; the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa. (وَما جَعَلْناهُمْ جَسَداً لا يَأْكُلُونَ الطَّعامَ وَما كانُوا خالِدِينَ): the wāw is a conjunction, ما is negative, جعلناهم is a verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi, and جسدا is a second object if جعل has the sense of "making into" (taṣyīr); if it has the sense of creating, then جسدا is a ḥāl (circumstantial) interpreted as a derived word, i.e. "taking nourishment". The clause لا يأكلون الطعام is in the position of accusative as an adjective of جسدا. جسد is singular but the plural is meant; it was made singular only to include the genus in general, because a body must have nourishment. The wāw is a conjunction, ما is negative, and كانوا خالدين is kāna, its noun and its khabar; the clause is conjoined to لا يأكلون. (ثُمَّ صَدَقْناهُمُ الْوَعْدَ فَأَنْجَيْناهُمْ وَمَنْ نَشاءُ وَأَهْلَكْنَا الْمُسْرِفِينَ): ثم is a conjunction; صدقناهم is a verb, its fāʿil and its object; الوعد is accusative by removal of the preposition, because صدق is transitive to two objects, to the second of them through a preposition, the original being في الوعد. فأنجيناهم is conjoined to صدقناهم; ومن نشاء is conjoined to the hāʾ, and the clause نشاء is the ṣila (relative clause); وأهلكنا المسرفين is conjoined to أنجيناهم, and المسرفين is the mafʿūl bihi. (لَقَدْ أَنْزَلْنا إِلَيْكُمْ كِتاباً فِيهِ ذِكْرُكُمْ أَفَلا تَعْقِلُونَ): the lām is in reply to an omitted oath; قد is a particle of verification; أنزلنا is a verb and its fāʿil; إليكم is attached to أنزلنا; كتابا is the mafʿūl bihi; فيه is a fronted khabar and ذكركم a postponed mubtadaʾ, and the clause is an adjective of كتابا. The meaning of فيه ذكركم will come in the section on benefits. The hamza is for the interrogative of denial and rebuke, and the fāʾ is a conjunction onto something implied that the speech extends over, i.e. "Do you not reflect, so that you understand nothing of the things mentioned to you?" (وَكَمْ قَصَمْنا مِنْ قَرْيَةٍ كانَتْ ظالِمَةً وَأَنْشَأْنا بَعْدَها قَوْماً آخَرِينَ): the wāw is a conjunction, or resumptive, brought to cite as an example the nations that perished before them. كم is the predicative (khabariyya) kam, a fronted mafʿūl bihi of قصمنا; من قرية is the tamyīz (specification) of the predicative kam, genitive by من, as has preceded. The clause كانت ظالمة is an adjective of قرية, the town meaning its people; كانت ظالمة is kāna, its latent (mustatir) noun and its khabar. أنشأنا is conjoined to قصمنا; بعدها is an adverb attached to أنشأنا; قوما is the mafʿūl bihi, and آخرين is an adjective of قوما. (فَلَمَّا أَحَسُّوا بَأْسَنا إِذا هُمْ مِنْها يَرْكُضُونَ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; لما is a temporal adverb meaning "when", or a linking [particle]; إذا is the إذا of surprise (al-fujāʾiyya), and the discussion of it and the disagreement over it have preceded in full. هم is a mubtadaʾ and the clause يركضون its khabar; منها is attached to يركضون. Some have taken this verse as proof that لما is a particle; Ibn Hishām called it "linking" (rābiṭa) because, if parsed as an adverb meaning "when", it would have nothing governing it. We hold that the meaning of surprise indicated by إذا is what governs it. More discussion of لما will come in the section on benefits.
(لا تَرْكُضُوا وَارْجِعُوا إِلى ما أُتْرِفْتُمْ فِيهِ وَمَساكِنِكُمْ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُسْئَلُونَ): لا is prohibitive; تركضوا is an imperfect verb, jussive by the prohibitive لا, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil. The clause لا تركضوا is the object of an omitted verb of saying. There is disagreement about who said it: it is said they were the angels, and it is said they were those of the believers who were present; this saying is, of course, by way of mocking them. ارجعوا is an imperative verb conjoined to لا تركضوا; إلى ما is attached to ارجعوا; the clause أترفتم is the ṣila, and فيه is attached to أترفتم; مساكنكم, in the genitive, is conjoined to ما. لعلكم تسألون: laʿalla, its noun and its khabar. The hope here is mockery of them and derision of what they used to think of themselves, that they were the expected source of generosity and the dawning-place of liberality. The meaning is: "Return to your luxury and your dwellings; perhaps you will be asked for something of your worldly goods, according to how you imagine yourselves to be people of bounty and giving, whom people ask in misfortunes and calamities, summon for grave matters and consult on difficult problems." More on this delightful discussion will come in the section on rhetoric.

* Rhetoric:
1- Synecdoche (al-majāz al-mursal) in His saying «قرية», since what is meant is its people; examples of this have preceded many times.
2- Derision (al-tahakkum) in His saying «وَارْجِعُوا إِلى ما أُتْرِفْتُمْ فِيهِ وَمَساكِنِكُمْ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُسْئَلُونَ». We have alluded to what is meant by this derision, and here we add two important possibilities arising from it:
a- That they were truly generous, bestowing gifts and stretching out their hands with presents, but they did so to be seen by people and to gain fame and praise. In that there is what pain and anguish there is, since they see that what they spent and gave was nothing but an increase in their torment and a deepening of their punishment.
b- That they were misers who hated giving and turned away whoever came seeking rain from the clouds of their palms and trying to milk the udders of their bounty; so this was said to them to add pain upon pain and anguish upon anguish.

* Benefits:
1- His saying «كِتاباً فِيهِ ذِكْرُكُمْ»:
i.e. in it is what calls for praise of you, since it was sent down in your language, in your midst, and upon a messenger from among you. It is also said: in it is what you seek of good repute, far-reaching fame and fine report. It is also said: in it is admonition for you and guidance to what benefits you in your religion and your worldly life. All of that is possible.

2- A discussion of لما:
لما occurs in Arabic in three ways:

The first:
That it is specific to the imperfect verb, making it jussive, negating it and turning it to the past, like «لم», except that it differs from it in five matters:
1- It is not joined to a conditional particle; one does not say إن لما تقم, but one says إن لم تقم.
2- What it negates remains negated continuously up to the present, whereas what لم negates may be either continuous or discontinued, as in «لَمْ يَكُنْ شَيْئاً مَذْكُوراً». For this reason you may say لم يكن ثم كان ("it was not, then it was"), but you may not say لما يكن ثم كان.
3- What لما negates is usually close to the present, unlike what لم negates.
4- What لما negates is expected to come about, unlike what لم negates.
5- What لما negates may be omitted when there is an indication, as in the saying «فجئت قبورهم بدءا ولما» ("I came to their graves a chief, though I was not yet"), i.e. ولما أكن بدءا قبل ذلك, "and I had not been a chief (بدء) before that", i.e. a lord. But it is not permissible to say «وصلت إلى حمص ولم», meaning "and I did not enter it".

The second:
That it is specific to the past verb, requiring two clauses, the second of which came about upon the existence of the first, e.g. لما جاءني أكرمته ("when he came to me, I honoured him"). It is called a particle of existence due to existence; some say of necessity due to necessity. It is also said to be an adverb for an act that occurred because of the occurrence of another; and a group said it is an adverb meaning "when" (ḥīn).

The third:
That it is a particle of exception meaning إلا; it then enters upon the nominal clause, e.g. «إِنْ كُلُّ نَفْسٍ لَمَّا عَلَيْها حافِظٌ», according to those who read the mīm with shadda; and upon a verb that is past in form but not in meaning, e.g. أنشدك الله لما فعلت ("I adjure you by Allah, do it"), i.e. "I ask of you nothing but your doing it".

dervis-irab:14-23.t:
* Vocabulary:
(حَصِيداً): faʿīl in the sense of mafʿūl (passive participle), in which the singular and others are alike; its rule will come in the section on benefits. It is harvested crops.
(خامِدِينَ): one says khamadat al-nār and hamadat, each of them of the pattern dakhala; but the first denotes the dying down of its flame while the embers remain, and the second denotes its going out completely.
(لَهْواً): in al-Miṣbāḥ: "Lahw is well known. The people of Najd say lahawtu ʿanhu alhū luhiyyan, the original being on the pattern fuʿūl, of the pattern qaʿada; and the people of al-ʿĀliya say lahītu ʿanhu alhā, of the pattern taʿiba, and its meaning is forgetting and leaving. Lahawtu bihi lahwan, of the pattern qatala: I became fond of it, too. Al-Ṭurṭūshī said: the root meaning of lahw is relieving the soul with what wisdom does not require. Alhānī al-shayʾ, with the alif: the thing occupied me." End quote.
In al-Qāmūs and al-Tāj: "Lahā lahwan: he played, like iltahā; alhāhu dhālika (that distracted him); al-malāhī are its instruments (of amusement); talāhā bi-dhāka; al-uhlūwa, al-uhliyya and al-tilhiya are what one amuses oneself with. Lahat al-marʾa ilā ḥadīthihi lahwan and luhuwwan: she took pleasure in his talk and it pleased her. Al-lahwa is the woman one amuses oneself with, like al-lahw. With ḍamma and fatḥa [al-luhwa/al-lahwa]: what you throw into the mouth of the millstone; and a gift, or the best and most abundant of gifts, like al-luhya; and a handful of wealth, or a thousand dīnārs or dirhams, nothing else. Lahiya bihi, like raḍiya: he loved it; and [lahiya] ʿanhu: he forgot it, was heedless of it and ceased mentioning it — all of these like daʿā, lahyan and lahayānan." The commentator on al-Qāmūs said: "His saying 'lahā lahwan: he played' implies that the two are identical, but a group distinguished between them. It is said that they share in being occupation with what is of no concern, whether forbidden or not; and it is said that lahw is absolutely more general, so listening to musical instruments is lahw but not laʿib (play)." Al-Jawharī said: lahw is sometimes used as a euphemism for intercourse, and this is indicated by the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays:
ألا زعمت بسباسة اليوم أنني ... كبرت وان لا يحسن اللهو أمثالي
(Basbāsa claimed today that I have grown old, and that men like me are no good at dalliance.)
(فَيَدْمَغُهُ): so it does away with it; its pattern is qaṭaʿa. In al-Qāmūs: damaghahu: he overpowered it; damagha al-ḥaqq bi-l-bāṭil [Translator's note: so in the source; the sense required is "the truth crushed falsehood"]: it nullified and effaced it. Details of that will come in the section on rhetoric.
(يَسْتَحْسِرُونَ): they grow weary and tired. One says istaḥsara al-baʿīr, i.e. the camel grew weary and tired; and one says ḥasara al-baʿīr and ḥasartuhu (I wearied it), so it is both intransitive and transitive; and also aḥsartuhu, so faʿala and afʿala have one meaning. More explanation of al-istiḥsār will come in the section on rhetoric.

* I'rab:
(قالُوا يا وَيْلَنا إِنَّا كُنَّا ظالِمِينَ): يا is a vocative particle and ويلنا is the one addressed in the vocative (munādā), a muḍāf. They call upon woe and ruin, because this is its time. It is also possible that يا is for drawing attention and ويلنا is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of an omitted verb. The clause is the object of their speech (maqūl al-qawl). إنّ and its noun, and the clause كنا ظالمين is its khabar (predicate); [كنا is] kāna and its noun, and ظالمين is its khabar. (فَما زالَتْ تِلْكَ دَعْواهُمْ حَتَّى جَعَلْناهُمْ حَصِيداً خامِدِينَ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; ما زالت is a defective past verb and the tāʾ is the sign of the feminine; تلك, a demonstrative, is its noun, in the position of nominative; دعواهم is its khabar, accusative (manṣūb) with an implied (muqaddar) fatḥa on the alif; the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi, and the mīm is a particle indicating the masculine plural. What is meant by the "cry" is those words, namely «يا وَيْلَنا إِنَّا كُنَّا ظالِمِينَ». حتى is a particle of limit and a preposition; جعلناهم is a verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); حصيدا خامدين is the second mafʿūl bihi, because the two together are treated as one, since the meaning of جعلناهم حصيدا خامدين is "We made them combine likeness to harvested crops and extinction". An example of that is your saying جعلته حلوا حامضا ("I made it sweet-sour"), i.e. combining the two flavours [Translator's note: the source prints «للطعين», evidently for «للطعمين»], i.e. tart. You may also make خامدين an adjective (naʿt) of حصيدا. (وَما خَلَقْنَا السَّماءَ وَالْأَرْضَ وَما بَيْنَهُما لاعِبِينَ): the wāw is a conjunction or resumptive; the clause is resumptive, brought to present the marvels and wonders contained in the creation of the heavens and the earth and what is in them, for admonition, and to be occasions for taking heed and an incentive to reflection and inference. ما is negative; خلقنا is a verb and its fāʿil; السماء is the mafʿūl bihi; الأرض is conjoined to السماء; ما is conjoined to السماء and الأرض; بينهما is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; and لاعبين is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil of خلقنا. (لَوْ أَرَدْنا أَنْ نَتَّخِذَ لَهْواً لَاتَّخَذْناهُ مِنْ لَدُنَّا إِنْ كُنَّا فاعِلِينَ): لو is a conditional particle of non-occurrence; أردنا is a verb and its fāʿil; أن and what follows it are interpreted as a maṣdar (interpreted maṣdar), the object of أردنا; the fāʿil of نتخذ is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "we"; لهوا is the mafʿūl bihi. لاتخذناه: the lām occurs in the apodosis of لو, and اتخذناه is a verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi; من لدنا is attached to an omitted second object of اتخذ. إن may be negative, meaning ما, and كنا فاعلين is kāna, its noun and its khabar; the clause is a ḥāl of the fāʿil of اتخذناه, i.e. "while We are not doers [of that]". It is also possible that إن is conditional, its apodosis omitted and indicated by the apodosis of لو; perhaps this is preferable and the closer of the two views to the way of Arabic. (بَلْ نَقْذِفُ بِالْحَقِّ عَلَى الْباطِلِ فَيَدْمَغُهُ فَإِذا هُوَ زاهِقٌ وَلَكُمُ الْوَيْلُ مِمَّا تَصِفُونَ): بل is a turning away (iḍrāb) from taking amusement and play, and a declaration of His transcendence above it, exalted be He in Himself. نقذف is an imperfect verb and its fāʿil is latent, its implied form being "we"; بالحق, a preposition and its genitive noun, is attached to نقذف; على الباطل is attached to an omitted ḥāl, i.e. "rising above falsehood". فيدمغه is conjoined to نقذف. فإذا: the fāʾ is a conjunction and إذا is of surprise (fujāʾiyya), mentioned before; هو is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and زاهق its khabar. ولكم: the wāw is resumptive; لكم is a fronted khabar and الويل a postponed mubtadaʾ; مما is attached to the "settledness" (al-istiqrār) to which the khabar is attached, namely مما [Translator's note: so in the source; the khabar is لكم], i.e. "woe is settled for you from all that you describe". ما [in مما] may be relative or maṣdariyya, and in either case the clause تصفون has no grammatical position. (وَلَهُ مَنْ فِي السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ): the wāw is a conjunction; له is a fronted khabar and من a postponed mubtadaʾ; في السموات والأرض is the ṣila. (وَمَنْ عِنْدَهُ لا يَسْتَكْبِرُونَ عَنْ عِبادَتِهِ وَلا يَسْتَحْسِرُونَ): the wāw is a conjunction; من is conjoined to the first من; عنده is an adverb attached to an omitted ṣila; the clause لا يستكبرون is a ḥāl of the first من; عن عبادته is attached to يستكبرون; and the clause لا يستحسرون is conjoined to the clause لا يستكبرون. It is also possible that the wāw is resumptive and ومن عنده, i.e. the angels, is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is the clause لا يستكبرون, the clause being resumptive. (يُسَبِّحُونَ اللَّيْلَ وَالنَّهارَ لا يَفْتُرُونَ): a resumptive clause, brought to affirm what those who are with Allah do in their worship. يسبحون is an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; the clause may also be a ḥāl. الليل and النهار are two adverbs attached to يسبحون, and the clause لا يفترون is a ḥāl of the fāʿil of يسبحون. (أَمِ اتَّخَذُوا آلِهَةً مِنَ الْأَرْضِ هُمْ يُنْشِرُونَ): أم is the disconnected (munqaṭiʿa) one, a conjunction conveying denial; اتخذوا is a verb and its fāʿil; آلهة is the mafʿūl bihi, and من الأرض is an adjective; هم is a mubtadaʾ and the clause ينشرون is the khabar; the clause هم ينشرون is an adjective of آلهة. The object of ينشرون is omitted, i.e. "they bring the dead to life". It may also be made a resumptive clause. They did not claim for their gods that they raise the dead, but by merely claiming their divinity they are bound to claim implicitly that they raise the dead. More discussion of the pronoun «هم» will come in the section on rhetoric. (لَوْ كانَ فِيهِما آلِهَةٌ إِلَّا اللَّهُ لَفَسَدَتا فَسُبْحانَ اللَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَرْشِ عَمَّا يَصِفُونَ): لو is a conditional particle of non-occurrence; كان is a defective past verb; فيهما is the fronted khabar of كان and آلهة its postponed noun; إلا, meaning غير ("other than"), is an adjective of آلهة whose case-ending appears on what follows it. It cannot be an exceptive particle, because the implication of the exception is corrupt here: its upshot would be that if there were in them gods from whom Allah was not excepted, they would not be ruined — and that is not so, for the mere multiplicity of gods necessarily entails ruin absolutely. A fuller exposition of this important discussion will come. لفسدتا: the lām occurs in the apodosis of لو, and the clause فسدتا has no grammatical position. فسبحان الله: the fāʾ is a conjunction, ordering what follows it upon what precedes it, namely the establishment of oneness by demonstration; سبحان is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb, and the Name of Majesty is muḍāf ilayhi; رب العرش is a badal (substitute) or an adjective of the Name of Majesty; عما is attached to سبحان; and the clause يصفون has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of ما; ما may also be maṣdariyya. (لا يُسْئَلُ عَمَّا يَفْعَلُ وَهُمْ يُسْئَلُونَ): the clause is resumptive, brought to show that He, glory be to Him, is alone in sovereignty, such that no one asks Him about what He does. لا is negative; يسأل is an imperfect verb in the passive, and its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent, its implied form being "He"; عما is attached to يسأل. وهم: the wāw is a conjunction or circumstantial; هم is a mubtadaʾ and the clause يسألون is the khabar.

* Rhetoric:
In these verses there are numerous devices, the first of which:
1- Metaphor (istiʿāra) in their saying «يا ويلنا»: they addressed woe, which is destruction, as though it were a living person whom they call upon to save them from what they are in.
2- The eloquent simile (al-tashbīh al-balīgh) in His saying «جَعَلْناهُمْ حَصِيداً خامِدِينَ».
After the punishment had befallen them, He likened them first to حصيد, which is harvested crops, the point of resemblance between the likened and that to which it is likened being uprooting from the places of growth. Then He likened them secondly to an extinguished fire of which nothing remains but dead embers, with no benefit in them and no capacity for any benefit from them; so you see nothing but scattered remains and dispersed parts, stretched out and overcome by decay [Translator's note: the source prints «وقدران», evidently for «وقد ران»].
3- Implied metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-makniyya) in His saying «بل نقذف بالحق على الباطل فيدمغه فإذا هو زاهق»: He likened truth and falsehood, which are abstract, to two material, perceptible things that are hurled and pushed; then He omitted these two things and borrowed what belongs to them, namely hurling and crushing (al-damgh), to embody the overthrow of falsehood and the truth's rising above it, and to depict its nullification, annulment and effacement, as though it were a hard body such as a rock or something like it in strength and hardness, hurled upon a soft, hollow body and crushing its brain. It is a metaphor of the perceptible for the intelligible. A detailed discussion of that, with a complete account of the kinds of metaphor in relation to the two terms of the simile, has preceded.
4- Strength of wording for strength of meaning: this device has been discussed before. We mean by it moving a word from one pattern to another, longer pattern, so that it contains more of the meaning it indicates than it contained at first; for words are indicators of meanings and models for expressing them, so when the words are increased, the division requires an increase in meanings. This kind of increase is used only in contexts of hyperbole, and here it is in the saying of the Exalted «وَلا يَسْتَحْسِرُونَ». He turned from the triliteral, ḥasara, to the six-letter form, istaḥsara. The apparent form of the speech would have been to say يحسرون, i.e. "they grow weary and tired", since even the slightest boredom or weariness is inconceivable on the part of the angels with respect to their worship of Allah, glory be to Him. But He turned away from that for a secret hidden to a first, superficial glance: namely that their absorption in worship and their total devotion to it would call for the utmost and extreme degree of weariness.
5- Making the pronoun explicit: this is in His saying «هم ينشرون». It would have sufficed to say ينشرون, but He turned from that to making the pronoun explicit, first to convey the meaning of exclusivity, as though they had said "there is no one here able to raise the dead except them", and secondly to record their being bound to claim divine attributes for their gods. Allah nullified this claim in the verse following this one by the proof of mutual hindrance (dalīl al-tamānuʿ), drawn from the sea of this verse, namely «لَوْ كانَ فِيهِما آلِهَةٌ إِلَّا اللَّهُ لَفَسَدَتا», as will be clarified in the i'rab [Translator's note: so in the source]. This is of the essence and pure substance of speech.
6- The dialectical method (al-madhhab al-kalāmī): this is in His saying «لَوْ كانَ فِيهِما آلِهَةٌ إِلَّا اللَّهُ لَفَسَدَتا». Ibn al-Muʿtazz mentioned that the one who gave it this name was al-Jāḥiẓ, and the Noble Book is filled with it. Its definition is that the speaker argues for what he wants to establish with a proof that silences his opponent, in the manner of the theologians (arbāb al-kalām). It has numerous ways; al-Rummānī, in his commentary called al-Nukat fī Iʿjāz al-Qur'an, brought them to five kinds. Among them is casting the speech in the form of doubt, for the sake of utmost fairness. The entailment of His saying «لَوْ كانَ فِيهِما آلِهَةٌ إِلَّا اللَّهُ لَفَسَدَتا» is that they have not been ruined, so there are no gods in them except Allah. The explanation of that is that the proof of mutual hindrance is that if another god existed alongside Allah [Translator's note: the sentence is incomplete in the source] — they might say: if we suppose the existence of two gods, then either both are described by the attributes of perfection, which include the power to give life to the dead and raise them and other possible things, or neither of them has them, or one of them has them and not the other; and then the subjects would be ruined by the management of the two kings, because of the mutual struggle for dominance, mutual rejection and disagreement that would arise between them. It is reported that ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Marwān, when he killed ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd al-Ashdaq, said: "By Allah, he was dearer to me than the blood of my eye, but two stallions do not come together in one herd of she-camels." The theologians have wide-ranging excursions on the method of mutual hindrance, which are to be found in their proper places, and its clarification will come in the section on benefits.

* Benefits:
«إلا» in the sense of «غير»:
The basic function of «إلا» is exception, and of «غير» description; then one may be treated like the other, so that إلا is used for description and غير for exception. If إلا is in the sense of غير, it and what follows it occur as an adjective of what precedes it. That is where exception is not intended by it, but rather the description of what precedes it as being other than what follows it, as in the saying of the Exalted «لَوْ كانَ فِيهِما آلِهَةٌ إِلَّا اللَّهُ لَفَسَدَتا». إلا and what follows it are an adjective of آلهة, because what is meant is the negation of multiple gods and the affirmation of the one, single God. The exception with the accusative is not valid, because the meaning would then be: "If there were in them gods among whom Allah was not, they would be ruined", which implies that if there were in them gods among whom Allah was, they would not be ruined — and this is evidently corrupt. May Allah forgive Ibn Yaʿīsh, the commentator on al-Zamakhsharī's al-Mufaṣṣal, for he permitted the accusative as an exception in the noble verse without appreciating the corruption that follows from the accusative. Ibn Yaʿīsh's wording is: "Allah the Exalted said: لو كان فيهما آلهة إلا الله لفسدتا, and what is meant is 'other than Allah'; so this can only be a description. It cannot be a badal intended as exception, because it would then amount to 'if there were in them [none] but Allah, they would be ruined', and that is corrupt, because لو is a condition regarding the past, so it is like إن regarding the future; and if you said إن أتاني إلا زيد it would not be valid, because the condition is treated as affirmative, so just as أتاني إلا زيد is not valid, so إن أتاني إلا زيد is not valid. But if it were made accusative as an exception, and you said 'لو كان فيهما إلا الله', it would be permissible." [Translator's note: the quoted sentence appears thus in the source; the example given still lacks the excepted-from noun.] Further, the Name of Majesty cannot be parsed as a badal of آلهة either, because where exception is not valid, substitution is not valid. Moreover, the statement is affirmative, so substitution would not be permissible even if exception were valid, because the accusative is obligatory in a complete affirmative statement. Also, if you made it a badal, the implied sense would be: "if there were in them [none] but Allah, they would be ruined", since the badal is on the intention of discarding the substituted-for, as is known. Because exception is invalid here and substitution impermissible, it is determined that إلا is in the sense of غير.
To complete this subtle discussion, we quote the delightful section that the erudite Ibn Hishām set out in Mughnī al-Labīb, with his rebuttal of al-Mubarrad, with suitable comments, so that the subject may receive its due. Ibn Hishām said, after mentioning that إلا has four uses:
"The second is that it is an adjective like غير, so that with it and what follows it an indefinite plural or something resembling it is described. An example of the indefinite plural: «لَوْ كانَ فِيهِما آلِهَةٌ إِلَّا اللَّهُ لَفَسَدَتا». This إلا cannot be for exception, from the point of view of meaning, since the implied sense would then be 'if there were in them gods among whom Allah was not, they would be ruined', and that implies by its contrary sense that if there were in them gods among whom Allah was, they would not be ruined — and that is not what is meant; nor from the point of view of wording, because آلهة is an indefinite plural in an affirmative statement, so it has no generality, and exception from it is not valid; if you said قام رجال إلا زيدا ('men stood except Zayd'), it would not be valid, by agreement. Al-Mubarrad claimed that إلا in the verse is for exception and that what follows it is a badal, arguing that لو indicates non-occurrence, and the non-occurrence of a thing is its negation; and he claimed that the emptied construction (tafrīgh) after it is permissible, and that something like لو كان معنا إلا زيد ('if there were with us [none] but Zayd') is the finest speech. He is refuted by the fact that they do not say لو جاءني ديّار أكرمته ('if anyone at all came to me, I would honour him'), nor لو جاءني من أحد أكرمته; if it were like a negator, that would be permissible, just as ما فيها ديار ('there is no one at all in it') and ما جاءني من أحد ('no one came to me') are permissible. Since that is not permissible, it shows that the correct view is that of Sībawayh: إلا and what follows it are an adjective." Until he says:
"Ibn al-Ḥājib made it a condition for إلا occurring as an adjective that exception be impossible, and he counted as anomalous the saying of Ḥaḍramī ibn ʿĀmir the Companion — and it is said, ʿAmr ibn Maʿdīkarib:
وكل أخ مفارقه أخوه ... لعمر أبيك إلا الفرقدان
(Every brother will be parted from by his brother — by your father's life — except the two Farqad stars.)"
The meaning of the anomaly in it is that it is not an exception, since it was not made accusative after a complete affirmative statement, so it is determined to be an adjective; yet exception was not impossible, so it is anomalous, since he could have said إلا الفرقدين. We reckon that the discussion has grown long, so what has preceded is enough for us.

dervis-irab:24-29.t:
* I'rab:
(أَمِ اتَّخَذُوا مِنْ دُونِهِ آلِهَةً): أم is a conjunction of turning away (iḍrāb) and of moving on to show the falsity of what they took as gods, despite these being devoid of the characteristics of divinity. اتخذوا is a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); من دونه is in the position of accusative as the second mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of اتخذوا, and آلهة is the first object. (قُلْ هاتُوا بُرْهانَكُمْ): هاتوا is an imperative verb, always indeclinable (mabnī) on the kasra except with the wāw of the plural, where it takes ḍamma; the wāw of the plural is the fāʿil, and برهانكم is the mafʿūl bihi. (هذا ذِكْرُ مَنْ مَعِيَ وَذِكْرُ مَنْ قَبْلِي): هذا is a mubtadaʾ (subject), the reference being to the Qur'an and all the heavenly scriptures; ذكر is the khabar (predicate) and من is muḍāf ilayhi; معي is an adverb of place attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; ذكر is conjoined to the first ذكر, من is muḍāf ilayhi, and the adverb is the ṣila. The clause is resumptive.
(بَلْ أَكْثَرُهُمْ لا يَعْلَمُونَ الْحَقَّ فَهُمْ مُعْرِضُونَ): بل is a particle of turning away; أكثرهم is a mubtadaʾ and the clause لا يعلمون is the khabar, the wāw being the fāʿil and الحق the mafʿūl bihi. فهم: the fāʾ is causal; هم is a mubtadaʾ and معرضون the khabar. (وَما أَرْسَلْنا مِنْ قَبْلِكَ مِنْ رَسُولٍ إِلَّا نُوحِي إِلَيْهِ أَنَّهُ لا إِلهَ إِلَّا أَنَا فَاعْبُدُونِ): the wāw is resumptive; ما is negative; أرسلنا is a verb and its fāʿil; من قبلك is a ḥāl (circumstantial); من is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition, and رسول is genitive in form and accusative in position as the mafʿūl bihi; إلا is a particle of restriction; نوحي is a verb and its fāʿil, and إليه is attached to نوحي. The parsing of لا إله إلا أنا has preceded many times. The fāʾ is the faṣīḥa (the fāʾ of an implied condition); اعبدوني is an imperative verb, the wāw is the fāʿil, and the yāʾ, omitted in accordance with the script of the Muṣḥaf, is the mafʿūl bihi. The clause is resumptive, affirming the oneness of Allah summarized earlier, as the heavenly scriptures declared, by way of inference from the requirements of reason and logic. (وَقالُوا اتَّخَذَ الرَّحْمنُ وَلَداً، سُبْحانَهُ، بَلْ عِبادٌ مُكْرَمُونَ): another resumptive clause, brought to relate the sayings of certain Arab tribes who said:
"The angels are the daughters of Allah"; it is said they were Banū Khuzāʿa, Banū Juhayna, Banū Salima and Banū Mulayḥ. The clause اتخذ الرحمن ولدا is the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl); سبحانه is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of an omitted verb, as has passed, and the clause is parenthetical. بل is a particle of turning away; عباد is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, and مكرمون is an adjective (naʿt). He has described the angels with seven attributes, the first of which has preceded. (لا يَسْبِقُونَهُ بِالْقَوْلِ وَهُمْ بِأَمْرِهِ يَعْمَلُونَ): these are a second [and a third] attribute [Translator's note: the source says «صفتان ثانيتان», "two second attributes"]: the first is the clause لا يسبقونه بالقول and the second is the clause هم بأمره يعملون; بأمره is attached to يعملون, and the clause يعملون is their khabar.
(يَعْلَمُ ما بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَما خَلْفَهُمْ): this is the fourth attribute. ما is a relative noun, the mafʿūl bihi; بين is an adverb attached to an omitted ṣila of the relative noun, and أيديهم is muḍāf ilayhi; وما خلفهم is conjoined to ما بين أيديهم. (وَلا يَشْفَعُونَ إِلَّا لِمَنِ ارْتَضى وَهُمْ مِنْ خَشْيَتِهِ مُشْفِقُونَ): these are two further attributes. يشفعون is an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; إلا is a particle of restriction; لمن is attached to يشفعون, and ارتضى is the ṣila of the relative noun. هم is a mubtadaʾ; من خشيته, a preposition and its genitive noun, is attached to مشفقون, and مشفقون is their khabar. (وَمَنْ يَقُلْ مِنْهُمْ إِنِّي إِلهٌ مِنْ دُونِهِ فَذلِكَ نَجْزِيهِ جَهَنَّمَ كَذلِكَ نَجْزِي الظَّالِمِينَ): this is the seventh and last attribute. من is conditional, a mubtadaʾ; يقل is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), jussive (majzūm); منهم is a ḥāl; إنّ and its noun, and إله its khabar. The fāʾ links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), because it is a nominal clause; ذلك, a demonstrative, is a mubtadaʾ and the clause نجزيه is the khabar; the hāʾ is the object of نجزي and جهنم the second object of نجزي; the clause is the apodosis, and the protasis together with its apodosis is the khabar of ذلك [Translator's note: so in the source; the conditional من is the mubtadaʾ whose khabar this would be]. كذلك نجزي الظالمين: the kāf is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "We recompense the wrongdoers with a recompense like that".

dervis-irab:30-33.t:
* Vocabulary:
(رَتْقاً): in al-Mukhtār: "Al-ratq is the opposite of al-fatq (splitting). Rataqtu al-fatq, of the pattern naṣara: I closed it, so it irtataqa, i.e. was joined; and from it is the saying of the Exalted: كانتا رتقا ففتقناهما. Al-rataq, with two fatḥas, is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of your saying imraʾa ratqāʾ, i.e. a woman with whom intercourse is not possible because that place in her is closed up." In al-Asās: "He closed (rataqa) the split until it was closed. It was read كانتا رتقا and رتقا [Translator's note: the source shows both forms identically, presumably ratqan and rataqan]. From Ibn al-Kalbī: they were ratqāwayn (two closed masses), so Allah split the sky with water and split the earth with vegetation. A woman ratqāʾ, of evident rataq, when she has no opening except the urinary one."
(رَواسِيَ): plural of rāsiya, from rasā al-shayʾ when it is firm and well established. In al-Mukhtār: "Al-rawāsī of the mountains are the firm ones; the singular is rāsiya." In al-Miṣbāḥ: "Rasā al-shayʾ yarsū raswan and rusuwwan: it became firm, so it is rāsin; and mountains are rāsiya, rāsiyāt and rawāsin."
(تَمِيدَ): in al-Miṣbāḥ: "Māda yamīdu maydan, of the pattern bāʿa, and mayadānan with fatḥa on the yāʾ: it moved." In al-Asās: "A māʾid branch is a leaning one; māda yamīdu mayadānan. Among figurative usages: the woman swayed (mādat and māsat, tamayyadat and tamayyasat); the earth swayed with him (mādat bihi al-arḍ): it spun round; a man is māʾid: dizzy (yudāru bihi); and the one pierced sways (yamīdu) on the spear."
(فِجاجاً): in al-Mukhtār: "Al-fajj, with fatḥa: the wide road between two mountains; the plural is fijāj, with kasra, like sahm and sihām. Al-fijj, with kasra: the Syrian melon; and anything of melons and fruits that has not ripened is fijj, with kasra." In al-Qāmūs: al-fajj, plural fijāj; and al-fijāj: the wide road between two mountains.

* I'rab:
(أَوَلَمْ يَرَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا أَنَّ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضَ كانَتا رَتْقاً فَفَتَقْناهُما): the hamza is for the interrogative of denial; the wāw is a conjunction onto something implied; لم is a particle of negation, conversion [to the past] and jussive; الذين is the fāʿil (agent), and the clause كفروا is the ṣila (relative clause). أنّ and what follows it stand in place of the two objects of رأى, because the seeing is mental (qalbiyya). أنّ and its noun, and the clause كانتا is its khabar (predicate); the alif is the noun of كان and رتقا its khabar. Regarding predicating with it [a maṣdar], there applies what has preceded concerning زيد عدل ("Zayd is justice"), i.e. the sun [Translator's note: so in the source, «الشمس», evidently for «السموات», the heavens] and the earth were closure itself. ففتقناهما: the fāʾ is a conjunction; فتقناهما is a verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is conjoined to كانتا; the mīm and alif are two letters indicating the dual. Al-Akhfash said: He said كانتا only because they are two categories, i.e. the group of the heavens and the group of the earths, as the Glorified said: «إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُمْسِكُ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضَ أَنْ تَزُولا». Al-Zajjāj said: He said كانتا only because the heavens are expressed with a singular word, since the heavens were one sky, and likewise the earths. (وَجَعَلْنا مِنَ الْماءِ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ حَيٍّ أَفَلا يُؤْمِنُونَ): وجعلنا is conjoined to what precedes; جعلنا is a verb and its fāʿil, in the sense of "created". من الماء is attached to (mutaʿalliq) جعلنا, since it means "We created", or to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of كل شيء, because it was originally an adjective of it, and when it was placed before it, it became accusative as a ḥāl. You may also take جعلنا in the sense of "made into" (ṣayyara), transitive to two objects, in which case من الماء is in the position of accusative as the second object and كل شيء the first object. أفلا: the hamza is for the interrogative of denial, the fāʾ is a conjunction onto something omitted, لا is negative, and يؤمنون is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is the fāʿil.
(وَجَعَلْنا فِي الْأَرْضِ رَواسِيَ أَنْ تَمِيدَ بِهِمْ): وجعلنا is conjoined to جعلنا. في الأرض is either the second object, with رواسي the first object, or it is attached to جعلنا or to an omitted ḥāl, with رواسي the mafʿūl bihi. أن and what falls within its scope are in the position of accusative as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e. "out of dislike that it should sway", or "lest it sway"; بهم is attached to تميد.
(وَجَعَلْنا فِيها فِجاجاً سُبُلًا لَعَلَّهُمْ يَهْتَدُونَ): وجعلنا is conjoined to what precedes; فيها is the second object or attached to جعلنا; فجاجا is a ḥāl, because it was an adjective of سبلا and was placed before it; سبلا is the mafʿūl bihi; laʿalla and its noun, and the clause يهتدون is its khabar.
(وَجَعَلْنَا السَّماءَ سَقْفاً مَحْفُوظاً وَهُمْ عَنْ آياتِها مُعْرِضُونَ): وجعلنا السماء is a verb, its fāʿil and its first mafʿūl bihi, and سقفا is the second mafʿūl bihi. هم is a mubtadaʾ (subject); عن آياتها is attached to معرضون, and معرضون is their khabar; the clause is circumstantial or resumptive.
(وَهُوَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ اللَّيْلَ وَالنَّهارَ وَالشَّمْسَ وَالْقَمَرَ كُلٌّ فِي فَلَكٍ يَسْبَحُونَ): the wāw is a conjunction; هو is a mubtadaʾ and الذي the khabar; the clause خلق is the ṣila, and the fāʿil of خلق is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "He"; الليل is the mafʿūl bihi and what follows it is conjoined to it. كل is a mubtadaʾ; beginning with it is permissible because of the meaning of generality in it; في فلك is attached to يسبحون, and the clause يسبحون is the khabar of كل. The clause كل في فلك يسبحون is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl of the sun and the moon. He made the pronoun the wāw of rational beings only because of the description with an act that is characteristic of rational beings, namely swimming; its like has preceded in His saying «رَأَيْتُهُمْ لِي ساجِدِينَ».

* Benefits:
1- A delightful discussion on the mafʿūl li-ajlihi:
This is a curious discussion to which Sībawayh devoted a special chapter in his Kitāb. It concerns the interpreted (muʾawwal) mafʿūl li-ajlihi, and here it is in His saying «وَجَعَلْنا فِي الْأَرْضِ رَواسِيَ أَنْ تَمِيدَ بِهِمْ». He said, in summary: it is of the same kind as their saying أعددت هذه الخشبة أن يميل الحائط فأدعمه ("I prepared this beam in case the wall leans, so that I may prop it up"). He said its meaning is "that I may prop up the wall if it leans"; the leaning was mentioned first only out of concern for it, and also because it is the cause of the propping [Translator's note: the source prints «الإدغام», evidently for «الادعام», propping], and propping is the cause of preparing the beam; so the cause of the cause was treated as the cause. On this basis the saying of the Exalted «أَنْ تَضِلَّ إِحْداهُما فَتُذَكِّرَ إِحْداهُمَا الْأُخْرى» was interpreted. Likewise, in what we are dealing with, the original is "and We placed in the earth firm mountains in order that they make it firm if it sways with them"; so He made the swaying the cause, just as the leaning was made the cause in the example mentioned, and the speech became "and We placed in the earth firm mountains in case it sways, so that they make it firm"; then "so that they make it firm" was omitted, since there is no danger of confusion, for brevity and concision. By my life, this is preferable to what we followed in the i'rab, because what we mentioned, and what most grammarians and commentators mentioned, requires that the earth not sway with its inhabitants, since Allah disliked that, and it is impossible for what Allah the Exalted dislikes to occur, just as what He wills must occur; yet what is observed is contrary to that, for how many earthquakes have made the earth sway and almost turned it upside down! On Sībawayh's account, however, what is meant is that Allah the Exalted makes the earth firm with the mountains when it sways, and this does not exclude the occurrence of swaying. This is a sublime discussion that few notice except after this detailed account; reflect on it and you will see lawful magic — and indeed some eloquence is magic.
2- Sībawayh and the majority held that the words كل and بعض are definite by virtue of an intended annexation (iḍāfa); for this reason a ḥāl can come from them, as in their saying مررت بكل قائما ("I passed by all [of them] standing") and ببعض جالسا ("by some sitting"), and the basic rule for the owner of the ḥāl is definiteness. Al-Fārisī held that they are indefinite, and bound those who say they are definite to say that نصف, سدس, ثلث, ربع and the like are definite, because in meaning they are annexed — whereas they are indefinite by consensus. This was answered by saying that the Arabs omit the muḍāf while intending it, and sometimes do not intend it, and the occurrence of a ḥāl after كل and بعض shows that it is intended. One question remains here: why did He use the plural form when they [the sun and the moon] are two? The answer is that the pronoun refers to them together with the night and the day, because the night and the day also swim: the night is the shadow of the earth, and it revolves around the circumference of the globe of the earth according to the earth's rotation; likewise the day also revolves, because it succeeds the night around the circumference.

dervis-irab:34-40.t:
* I'rab:
(وَما جَعَلْنا لِبَشَرٍ مِنْ قَبْلِكَ الْخُلْدَ أَفَإِنْ مِتَّ فَهُمُ الْخالِدُونَ): the clause is resumptive, brought to affirm that human beings are not immortal, in reply to their saying that Muḥammad would die. ما is negative; جعلنا is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); لبشر is in the position of accusative as the second object; من قبلك is an adjective (naʿt) of بشر; الخلد is the first object of جعلنا. The hamza is for the interrogative of denial, the fāʾ is a conjunction, إن is conditional, and مت is a past verb and its fāʿil, in the position of jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ). The fāʾ is linking; هم is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and الخالدون the khabar (predicate); the clause is in the position of jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and it is intended as fronted, since the original form of the speech is "Are they the immortal ones, if you die?" Al-Farrāʾ said: He brought the fāʾ to indicate the condition, because it is a reply to their saying "he will die"; he said that omitting the fāʾ and implying it is permissible. The meaning is: "If you die, they too will die, so there is no [room for] gloating over death." (كُلُّ نَفْسٍ ذائِقَةُ الْمَوْتِ): كل is a mubtadaʾ, نفس is muḍāf ilayhi, and ذائقة الموت is the khabar; the clause is resumptive, brought to prove that there is no immortality, so there is no room for gloating. May Allah have mercy on the one who said:
فقل للشامتين بنا أفيقوا ... سيلقى الشامتون كما لقينا
(Say to those who gloat over us: wake up! The gloaters will meet what we have met.)
(وَنَبْلُوكُمْ بِالشَّرِّ وَالْخَيْرِ فِتْنَةً وَإِلَيْنا تُرْجَعُونَ): the wāw is also resumptive; نبلوكم is an imperfect verb with a latent (mustatir) fāʿil, its implied form being "we", and the kāf is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); بالشر is attached to (mutaʿalliq) نبلوكم and الخير is conjoined to الشر, i.e. "We test you with what requires patience and with what requires gratitude". فتنة is a maṣdar (verbal noun) emphasizing نبلوكم though not of its own root, because testing is trial, so it is as though it were said "We try you with a trial". It may also be parsed as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), or as accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil of نبلوكم, i.e. "trying you". إلينا is attached to ترجعون; ترجعون is an imperfect verb in the passive, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is conjoined to نبلوكم or circumstantial. (وَإِذا رَآكَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا إِنْ يَتَّخِذُونَكَ إِلَّا هُزُواً): you may make the wāw resumptive, so that the clause is resumptive, brought to state their attitude toward the Prophet Muḥammad ﷺ, or make it a conjunction, so that the clause is conjoined to His earlier saying «وَأَسَرُّوا النَّجْوَى». إذا is an adverb of future time, and the clause رآك is the one to which the adverb is annexed; the fāʿil of رآك is الذين, the kāf is the mafʿūl bihi, and the clause كفروا is the ṣila (relative clause). إن is negative; يتخذونك is an imperfect verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi; the negative إن and what falls within its scope are the apodosis of إذا; the reason why the apodosis is not joined with the fāʾ will be mentioned in the section on benefits. إلا is a particle of restriction, and هزوا is the second mafʿūl bihi, either by way of describing with a maṣdar for hyperbole — its parallels have passed — or by omission of a muḍāf. Moreover, the negative إن and what follows it may be a parenthetical clause, in which case the apodosis is His following saying:
(أَهذَا الَّذِي يَذْكُرُ آلِهَتَكُمْ وَهُمْ بِذِكْرِ الرَّحْمنِ هُمْ كافِرُونَ): the hamza is interrogative, and the interrogative means mockery. The clause is either the apodosis of إذا, as preceded, or the object of an omitted verb of saying, i.e. "some of them say to others, by way of mockery and derision: is this...?" هذا is a mubtadaʾ and الذي its khabar; the clause يذكر is the ṣila, and آلهتكم is the mafʿūl bihi. The wāw is circumstantial; هم is a mubtadaʾ; بذكر is attached to كافرون and الرحمن is muḍāf ilayhi; هم is a verbal tawkīd (emphasis) of the first هم, and كافرون is the khabar of هم. The clause is a ḥāl either of the fāʿil of يتخذونك or of the fāʿil of the implied verb of saying, as we said before. The object of يذكر is omitted; its discussion will come in the section on rhetoric.
(خُلِقَ الْإِنْسانُ مِنْ عَجَلٍ سَأُرِيكُمْ آياتِي فَلا تَسْتَعْجِلُونِ): the clause is resumptive, brought to reply to their seeking to hasten the punishment. خلق is a past verb in the passive and الإنسان is the nāʾib fāʿil; من عجل is attached to خلق or to an omitted ḥāl. The meaning of this construction will come in the section on rhetoric. سأريكم: the sīn is for the future; أريكم is an imperfect verb with a latent fāʿil, its implied form being "I"; the kāf is the first mafʿūl bihi and آياتي the second mafʿūl bihi. The fāʾ is a conjunction; لا is prohibitive; تستعجلون is an imperfect verb, jussive by the prohibitive لا, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil, and the yāʾ, omitted for the script, is the mafʿūl bihi. The clause سأريكم is also resumptive, brought to emphasize haste and its consequence, which is seeing the punishment. (وَيَقُولُونَ مَتى هذَا الْوَعْدُ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صادِقِينَ): the wāw is resumptive, and the clause is resumptive, brought to present one kind of their blameworthy haste. يقولون is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is the fāʿil. متى is an interrogative noun in the position of accusative as an adverb, attached to an omitted fronted khabar; هذا is a postponed mubtadaʾ and الوعد a badal (substitute). إن is conditional; كنتم is kāna and its noun, in the position of jussive as the protasis, and صادقين is the khabar of كنتم. The apodosis of إن is omitted, its implied form being "then specify its appointed time". Their address is to the Prophet and his Companions.
(لَوْ يَعْلَمُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا حِينَ لا يَكُفُّونَ عَنْ وُجُوهِهِمُ النَّارَ وَلا عَنْ ظُهُورِهِمْ وَلا هُمْ يُنْصَرُونَ): لو is conditional; يعلم is an imperfect verb, الذين is the fāʿil, and the clause كفروا is the ṣila. حين may be the object of يعلم, i.e. "the time which they seek to hasten by their saying 'when is this promise?'" — and it is a hard, straitened time, in which the Fire surrounds them from every side, since they were in that state of disbelief; the apodosis of لو is then omitted, as has been pointed out many times. It is also possible that يعلم is left without any object, meaning "if they had knowledge and were not ignorant, they would not be hasty", and حين is accusative by an implied [verb], i.e. "at the time when they cannot ward off the Fire from their faces, they will know that they were upon falsehood". The most likely view is that the object of يعلم is omitted because what precedes indicates it, i.e. "if those who disbelieve knew the coming of the promised thing about which they asked and which they thought slow", and حين is accusative by the object, which is "coming" (majīʾ). The clause لا يكفون is annexed to the adverb; عن وجوههم is attached to يكفون and النار is the mafʿūl bihi; ولا عن ظهورهم is conjoined. The wāw is a conjunction; لا is negative; هم is a mubtadaʾ and the clause ينصرون is the khabar; ينصرون is an imperfect verb in the passive and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil. (بَلْ تَأْتِيهِمْ بَغْتَةً فَتَبْهَتُهُمْ فَلا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ رَدَّها وَلا هُمْ يُنْظَرُونَ): بل is a particle of turning away (iḍrāb) and conjunction; تأتيهم is an imperfect verb with a latent fāʿil referring to the Fire; بغتة is a ḥāl that came as a maṣdar, and it is said to be a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); more discussion of it will come in the section on benefits. فتبهتهم is conjoined to تأتيهم; فلا يستطيعون is also conjoined, and ردها is the object of يستطيعون; ولا هم ينظرون is also conjoined; هم is a mubtadaʾ and the clause ينظرون is the khabar — [i.e. they will not be granted respite] as they were granted respite and delay before.

* Rhetoric:
1- Tailing (al-tadhyīl): in the saying of the Exalted «وَما جَعَلْنا لِبَشَرٍ مِنْ قَبْلِكَ الْخُلْدَ أَفَإِنْ مِتَّ فَهُمُ الْخالِدُونَ. كُلُّ نَفْسٍ ذائِقَةُ الْمَوْتِ» there is a curious rhetorical device to which the scholars of rhetoric gave the name "tadhyīl". They defined it as appending to speech, after it is complete and could well end there, a clause that confirms the preceding speech, adds emphasis to it and casts it in the form of a current proverb, so that the speech spreads after circulating on people's tongues. If the addition does not convey that, it is not called tadhyīl; some call it tadhyīl in that case too, but say that it is faulty — and how fitting it is that what is faulty be excluded from the devices of rhetoric rather than included among them! It is common in the Noble Qur'an, and many examples of it will come. As for the verse we are dealing with, the meaning is complete in the statement that He, glory be to Him, did not grant immortality to any human before His Prophet; then He appended to that statement something cast in the form of feigned ignorance (tajāhul al-ʿārif), namely His saying «أَفَإِنْ مِتَّ فَهُمُ الْخالِدُونَ»; then He appended to this tailing something cast in the form of a current proverb, saying: «كُلُّ نَفْسٍ ذائِقَةُ الْمَوْتِ».
Among the most splendid examples of tadhyīl in poetry is the saying of the poet of immortality, Abū al-Ṭayyib:
تمسي الأماني صرعى دون مبلغه ... فما يقول لشيء ليت ذلك لي
(Wishes lie felled short of his station, so he never says of anything: would that it were mine.)
Abū al-Ṭayyib says: wishes do not reach his heart so as to sway it, nor his tongue so as to run upon it, because he has no need to wish for anything without already having something better, or that thing has already become his. So wishes fall short of reaching his worth and fall short of the majesty of his affair; they lie felled short of attaining his glory, so he wishes for no more loftiness than he has already reached. Sayf al-Dawla never ceased to repeat this verse, extolling it, praising it and acknowledging that it cannot be overtaken in excellence and that no one has come, in its kind of hyperbole, with the like of what he brought.
And Ibn Nubāta al-Saʿdī said, and said it well:
لم يبق جودك لي شيئا أؤمله ... تركتني أصحب الدنيا بلا أمل
(Your generosity left me nothing to hope for; you have left me to keep company with the world without a hope.)
He fulfilled all his hopes and desires for him, so he no longer had anything to hope for; and even supposing he yearned for something, he was confident it would be at hand, so he became without hopes.
2- Concision by omission (al-ījāz bi-l-ḥadhf): this is in the omission of the object of يذكر in the saying of the Exalted:
«أَهذَا الَّذِي يَذْكُرُ آلِهَتَكُمْ». Mention may be good or bad; when the situation indicates one of them, it is left unqualified and unrestricted, as when you say to a man "I heard so-and-so mentioning you": if the one mentioning is a friend, it is praise, and if an enemy, it is censure. From another angle, they did not say "Is this the one who mentions your gods with every evil?" because they found it too abominable to relate what the Prophet said in disparagement of their gods — charging that they neither hear nor see, neither benefit nor harm — and they held them too high [Translator's note: the source prints «ورئبوا», evidently for «وربئوا»] for their censure to be reported in detail and explicitly; so they reported it summarily and by hint, rather they gestured to it with the reference mentioned, just as a believer avoids relating a word of disbelief, even if the one who said it is not a disbeliever, and gestures to it with an expression that conveys what is intended by way of allusion. Glory be to the One who led them so astray that they showed good manners toward idols and ill manners toward the Most Merciful!
3- Implied metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-makniyya) in His saying «خُلِقَ الْإِنْسانُ مِنْ عَجَلٍ»: He likened the haste with which a person is imprinted, and which has become like his innate disposition, to the origin of his substance, namely clay; then He omitted that to which it is likened and alluded to it with something belonging to it, namely His saying «خلق». It is also said that there is no metaphor in it, but rather that it is of the kind of inversion (qalb), the original being "haste was created from man", because of how intensely it issues from him and clings to him; inversion is found frequently in their speech, and it has been pointed out before. The first is preferable and more firmly grounded in rhetoric. Among the oddities of the commentaries is their saying that ʿajal is clay in the language of Ḥimyar; their poet said:
النبع في الصخرة الصماء منبته ... والنخل ينبت بين الماء والعجل
(The nabʿ tree has its growth in the solid rock, while the palm grows between water and clay.)
He says: the nabʿ — a tree from which bows are made — has its growing place in the solid, hard rock and nowhere else, while the palm grows in soft, well-watered ground, so it is between water and ʿajal, i.e. clay; and this, as was said, is the language of Ḥimyar. It appears that the first hemistich is a likeness of the difficult, miserly man and the second of the easy, generous man; or the first of the brave and the second of the coward, because of the hardness of the first and the softness of the second. In any case, this meaning does not apply in the noble verse, because the context rejects it: they are seeking to hasten, and Allah, glory be to Him, is censuring them for their haste.
In this verse [Translator's note: so in the source; the phrase belongs to verse 35] there is also an implied metaphor in His saying «ذائقة الموت». Death is not something tasted, but He likened it to food that is neither wholesome nor palatable; yet because of the inevitability of its occurrence and its being something unavoidable, it became as though wholesome and palatable, so no soul has escape from tasting it. Parallels of this metaphor have preceded.

* Benefits:
1- The apodosis of «إذا»:
«إذا» differs from all the conditional particles: for whenever the conditional particles are answered with the negative إن or the negative ما, the fāʾ must be brought, as in this verse [Translator's note: so in the source; in this verse إذا is answered by إن without the fāʾ, which is the point of contrast], and as in the saying of the Exalted also: «وَإِذا تُتْلى عَلَيْهِمْ آياتُنا بَيِّناتٍ ما كانَ حُجَّتَهُمْ إِلَّا أَنْ قالُوا».
2- The maṣdar occurring as a ḥāl:
Maṣdars parsed as ḥāls occur frequently among indefinite nouns, as in طلع زيد بغتة ("Zayd appeared suddenly"), جاء ركضا ("he came running") and قتلته صبرا ("I killed him in confinement") — which is that you keep him confined alive, then he is shot at until he is killed. All of that, frequent as it is, is interpreted as a descriptive: بغتة is interpreted as the descriptive of باغت, since it means "surprise", i.e. "taking by surprise" (mubāghitan); ركضا is interpreted as the active participle of ركض, i.e. "running" (rākiḍan); and صبرا is interpreted as the passive participle of صبر, i.e. "confined" (maṣbūran, maḥbūsan). Despite its frequent occurrence, Sībawayh said: it is not to be extended by analogy at all; some extended it by analogy, in ways that may be consulted in the lengthy works.
We return to بغتة: some have affirmed that it may be made a mafʿūl muṭlaq, and the same is said of the preceding examples, since they are a kind of [the action of] what governs them, so they are like رجع القهقرى ("he went back retreating").
What results from what the grammarians mentioned is that there are three views on the accusative maṣdar here:
1- The view of Sībawayh: the maṣdar is the ḥāl, and that is the basic view.
2- The view of al-Mubarrad and al-Akhfash: it is a mafʿūl muṭlaq, not made accusative by the governing word before it, but rather by an omitted governing word from its own root, and that omitted [verb] is the ḥāl. This is a fine view, as you see.
3- The view of the Kufans: it is a mafʿūl muṭlaq made accusative by the governing word before it, and it is not in the position of a ḥāl.
Among what comes up in this context is the parsing of «أسفا» in the saying of Abū al-Ṭayyib:
أبلى الهوى أسفا يوم النوى بدني ... وفرق الهجر بين الجفن والوسن
(Love wasted my body with grief on the day of parting, and separation parted eyelid from slumber.)
روح تردّد في مثل الخلال إذا ... أطارت الريح عنه الثوب لم يبن
(A spirit wavering in [a body] like a toothpick; when the wind blows the garment off it, it cannot be seen.)
كفى بجسمي نحولا إنني رجل ... لولا مخاطبتي إياك لم ترني
(It is enough of thinness for my body that I am a man whom, were it not for my speaking to you, you would not see.)
The ḥāl does not apply here, because the meaning rejects it; the mafʿūl li-ajlihi is not valid, because the agent differs; so nothing remains but the absolute object, the implied sense being "I grieved a grieving" (asiftu asafan); what preceded it indicates its verb, because love's wasting his body indicates his grief, as though he said "I grieved a grieving". Ibn Hishām strained himself and tried to justify its accusative as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi, saying: For whoever does not require the agent to be the same, there is no problem (the one who holds this is Ibn Kharūf); as for whoever requires it, it is by dropping the lām of cause by way of extension, as in His saying «يَبْغُونَها عِوَجاً» (i.e. they seek crookedness for it); or the identity [of agent] exists by implication, either on the basis that the verb given a cause is an omitted reflexive (muṭāwiʿ) of أبلى, i.e. "so I wasted away with grief" — and you should not imply "so my body wasted away", because the difference [of agent] would then exist, since grief is an act of the soul, not of the body — or because love, having come about by his causing it, is as though he said "I wasted my body with love". There is nothing of value beneath these strained interpretations.

dervis-irab:41-47.t:
* Vocabulary:
(يَكْلَؤُكُمْ): in al-Miṣbāḥ: "Kalaʾahu Allāh yaklaʾuhu, with hamza and two fatḥas, of the pattern qaṭaʿa, kilāʾatan with kasra and the long vowel: He guarded him. Lightening [the hamza] is permissible, so one says kalaytuhu aklāhu; and kaliʾtuhu aklaʾuhu, of the pattern taʿiba, is a dialect of Quraysh; but they said maklūw, with wāw, more than maklīy, with yāʾ." In al-Qāmūs: "Kalaʾa yaklaʾu, with fatḥa, kalʾan, kilāʾatan and kilāʾan, with kasra on the kāf: Allah guarded so-and-so and protected him; kalaʾahu bi-l-sawṭ: he struck him with the whip; kalaʾa baṣarahu fī al-shayʾ: he let his eye linger over the thing; kalaʾa al-najm matā yaṭluʿu: he watched for when the star would rise." In al-Asās: "Allah guards you (yaklaʾuka); Allah overtook him with His protection (kilāʾa); iktalaʾtu minhu: I was on my guard against it. Kaʿb ibn Zuhayr said:
أنخت قلوصي واكتلأت بعينها ... وآمرت نفسي أيّ أمري أفعل
(I made my young she-camel kneel and kept watch by her eye, and consulted myself as to which of my two courses I should take.)
i.e. I was on my guard by her eye, because when she sees something she takes fright. Kalaʾa daynuhu kulūʾan: his debt was deferred, so it is kāliʾ; and 'the sale of the deferred for the deferred' (bayʿ al-kāliʾ bi-l-kāliʾ) was forbidden. I deferred it (kallaʾtuhu) takliʾatan; istaklaʾtu kulʾatan and takallaʾtu: I took an advance (salaf). And you say: 'The pastures (al-kalaʾ) melt the fat of the kidneys (al-kulā)' [Translator's note: the source prints «الكلى» for both words; the reading here follows the sense of the saying] — plural of kalʾa."
(خَرْدَلٍ): mustard (khardal): a plant with very small, black, pungent seeds; the singular is khardala. One says khardala al-ṭaʿām: he ate the best of the food; khardala al-laḥm: he cut it into pieces; and al-kharādil are the pieces of meat.

* I'rab:
(وَلَقَدِ اسْتُهْزِئَ بِرُسُلٍ مِنْ قَبْلِكَ): the wāw is resumptive, and the clause is resumptive, brought to console the Prophet ﷺ and comfort him. The lām is in reply to an omitted oath; قد is a particle of verification; استهزئ is a past verb in the passive; برسل stands in place of the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); and من قبلك is an adjective (naʿt) of رسل.
(فَحاقَ بِالَّذِينَ سَخِرُوا مِنْهُمْ ما كانُوا بِهِ يَسْتَهْزِؤُنَ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; حاق is a past verb and بالذين is attached to (mutaʿalliq) حاق; the clause سخروا has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; منهم is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of سخروا. ما is the fāʿil of حاق, and the clause كانوا is the ṣila of the relative noun; [كانوا is] kāna and its noun; به is attached to His saying يستهزئون, and يستهزئون is a verbal clause in the position of accusative as the khabar (predicate) of كانوا. (قُلْ مَنْ يَكْلَؤُكُمْ بِاللَّيْلِ وَالنَّهارِ مِنَ الرَّحْمنِ): من is an interrogative noun in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause يكلؤكم is the khabar; the clause is the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl). بالليل is attached to يكلؤكم and النهار is conjoined to الليل; من الرحمن means "from His punishment and His command", and it is attached to يكلؤكم. (بَلْ هُمْ عَنْ ذِكْرِ رَبِّهِمْ مُعْرِضُونَ): بل is a particle of turning away (iḍrāb); هم is a mubtadaʾ; عن ذكر ربهم is attached to معرضون, and معرضون is the khabar of هم. It is a turning away from the negation the speech contains, the implied sense being: "they have no guardian and no protector other than the Most Merciful, yet they do not even let Him cross their minds, let alone fear His might and His punishment." (أَمْ لَهُمْ آلِهَةٌ تَمْنَعُهُمْ مِنْ دُونِنا): أم is a particle of conjunction and turning away, so it has the meaning of بل; لهم is a fronted khabar and آلهة a postponed mubtadaʾ; the interrogative hamza is implied, the implied sense being "Do they have gods that protect them?" The clause تمنعهم is an adjective of آلهة, and من دوننا is also an adjective of آلهة.
