(لا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ نَصْرَ أَنْفُسِهِمْ وَلا هُمْ مِنَّا يُصْحَبُونَ): a resumptive clause, brought to establish that whoever is not able to help and protect himself, and is not accompanied by Allah with help and support — how can he protect and help someone else? لا is negative; يستطيعون is an imperfect verb and its fāʿil, and نصر أنفسهم is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ولا: the wāw is a conjunction and لا is negative; هم is a mubtadaʾ; منا is attached to يصحبون; يصحبون is an imperfect verb in the passive and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil; the clause يصحبون is their khabar. The Arabs say أنا لك صاحب من فلان, i.e. "I am your protector against so-and-so", and they also say صحبك الله, i.e. "may Allah guard you and protect you". (بَلْ مَتَّعْنا هؤُلاءِ وَآباءَهُمْ حَتَّى طالَ عَلَيْهِمُ الْعُمُرُ): بل is a particle of transitional turning away; متعنا is a verb and its fāʿil; هؤلاء is a demonstrative, indeclinable (mabnī) on the kasra, in the position of accusative as the mafʿūl bihi; آباءهم is conjoined to هؤلاء. حتى is a particle of limit and a preposition; طال is a past verb, عليهم is attached to طال, and العمر is the fāʿil of طال.
(أَفَلا يَرَوْنَ أَنَّا نَأْتِي الْأَرْضَ نَنْقُصُها مِنْ أَطْرافِها أَفَهُمُ الْغالِبُونَ): the hamza is for the interrogative of denial and the fāʾ is a conjunction onto something implied; this expression has been repeated so often that there is no longer any need to repeat it. لا is negative; يرون is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is the fāʿil. أنّ and what falls within its scope stand in place of the two objects of يرون, because the seeing here is cognitive; it may also be visual. أنّ and its noun, and the clause نأتي الأرض is its khabar; the clause ننقصها من أطرافها is a ḥāl of the fāʿil of نأتي or of its object, i.e. "We conquer it land after land, by what is diminished from the outlying regions of the polytheists and added to the outlying regions of the believers". An extensive and detailed treatment of this has preceded in Sūrat al-Raʿd, so renew your acquaintance with it. The secret of His ascribing the act to Himself will come in the section on rhetoric. His saying أفهم: the hamza is for the interrogative of denial and reproach, the fāʾ is a conjunction onto something implied, هم is a mubtadaʾ and الغالبون the khabar. (قُلْ إِنَّما أُنْذِرُكُمْ بِالْوَحْيِ وَلا يَسْمَعُ الصُّمُّ الدُّعاءَ إِذا ما يُنْذَرُونَ): إنما is [إنّ] restraining and restrained (kāffa wa-makfūfa); أنذركم is an imperfect verb, its fāʿil is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "I", and the kāf is the mafʿūl bihi; بالوحي is attached to أنذركم. ولا يسمع: the wāw is a conjunction, and it may also be circumstantial; لا is negative; يسمع الصم الدعاء is an imperfect verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi. إذا is an adverb of future time, here for mere adverbial use, attached to يسمع, i.e. "at the time of their being warned"; ما is redundant (zāʾida); ينذرون is an imperfect verb in the passive and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil; the clause ينذرون is in the position of genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it. A detailed account of this verse will come in the section on rhetoric.
(وَلَئِنْ مَسَّتْهُمْ نَفْحَةٌ مِنْ عَذابِ رَبِّكَ لَيَقُولُنَّ يا وَيْلَنا إِنَّا كُنَّا ظالِمِينَ): the wāw is a conjunction; the lām prepares for the oath (muwaṭṭiʾa); إن is conditional; مستهم is a past verb in the position of jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), the hāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi, and نفحة is the fāʿil. What is meant by the "breath" (nafḥa) is a small amount, taken from the wafting (nafḥ) of musk — so said Ibn Kaysān — and from it is the saying of al-Nuʿmān ibn Bashīr:
وعمرة من سروات النسا ... ء تنفح بالمسك أردانها
(And ʿAmra is among the noblest of women; her sleeves waft with musk.)
Al-Mubarrad said: al-nafḥa is a portion of a thing short of its bulk; one says nafaḥahu nafḥatan bi-l-sayf when he strikes him a light blow with the sword. It is said: it is a share; and it is said: it is an extremity. The meaning is close, i.e. "if the least thing of the punishment touched them". من عذاب ربك is an adjective of نفحة. ليقولن: the lām occurs in the reply to the oath, because it came first; يقولنّ is an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, which has been dropped because of the succession of like letters; the wāw, dropped because of the meeting of two sukūns, is the fāʿil, and the nūn is for emphasis. يا ويلنا is either a calling upon woe to come, for this is its time, or يا is for drawing attention and ويلنا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb. إنا: inna and its noun, and the clause كنا is its khabar; نا is the noun of كان and ظالمين its khabar. (وَنَضَعُ الْمَوازِينَ الْقِسْطَ لِيَوْمِ الْقِيامَةِ فَلا تُظْلَمُ نَفْسٌ شَيْئاً): a resumptive clause, brought to show what will happen when what they were warned of comes. نضع is an imperfect verb and its fāʿil is latent, its implied form being "we"; الموازين is the mafʿūl bihi, and القسط is a description of الموازين: they are described with the maṣdar (verbal noun) itself, for hyperbole, from qasaṭa when he acted justly [Translator's note: so in the source; the common derivation is from aqsaṭa, "to act justly", qasaṭa usually meaning "to deviate"]. ليوم القيامة is attached to نضع, and the lām is in the sense of «في» ("in"), as in their saying مضى لسبيله ("he went his way"); it is also said to be in the sense of "at" (ʿinda) [Translator's note: the source prints «يمعنى», a misprint for «بمعنى»]. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is like it in your saying جئته لخمس خلون من الشهر ('I came to him when five [nights] of the month had passed'), and from it is the verse of al-Nābigha:
توسمت آيات لها فعرفتها ... لستة أعوام وذا العام سابع
(I scanned her traces and recognized them after six years — and this year is the seventh.)"
Its meaning is: I followed up its vestiges and traces and recognized them, i.e. in those places mentioned in the verse before it. His saying لستة أعوام means upon the completion of six years that had passed since [I was last] acquainted with it, and this present year in which we are is the seventh. Had he said لسبعة أعوام, it would have conveyed that all seven had passed, and that is not what is intended. So the claim of some that it would have sufficed him to say لسبعة أعوام, and that he was unable to complete [the verse] and so filled it out with something meaningless, has no basis except lack of insight. فلا: the fāʾ is a conjunction; تظلم is an imperfect verb in the passive and نفس is the nāʾib fāʿil; شيئا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq or a second object of تظلم.
(وَإِنْ كانَ مِثْقالَ حَبَّةٍ مِنْ خَرْدَلٍ أَتَيْنا بِها وَكَفى بِنا حاسِبِينَ): the wāw is a conjunction; إن is conditional; كان is a defective past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis, and its noun is latent, its implied form being "it", referring to the deed; مثقال حبة is the khabar of كان, and من خردل is an adjective of حبة. أتينا بها is in the position of jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). وكفى: the wāw is a conjunction; كفى is a past verb; the bāʾ is a redundant preposition; and حاسبين is a tamyīz (specification) or a ḥāl. The pronoun referring to the weight (al-mithqāl) was made feminine because it is annexed to الحبة; its rule has passed.

* Rhetoric:
1- Putting the overt noun in place of the pronoun: in the saying of the Exalted «قُلْ إِنَّما أُنْذِرُكُمْ بِالْوَحْيِ وَلا يَسْمَعُ الصُّمُّ الدُّعاءَ إِذا ما يُنْذَرُونَ» there is a subtle device that may be called putting the overt noun in place of the pronoun, and its benefit is to record [the charge] against them. The context required Him to say ولا يسمعون ("and they do not hear"), but He stated "the deaf" explicitly and passed over the pronoun to the overt noun, to indicate their feigning deafness and blocking their hearing when they are warned, and to indicate that strong disapproval, great anger and wonder issue at their hearing's shying away from the revelation, their not listening to what benefits them, and their persistence in riding error and blundering in the mazes of misguidance. This is a wonderful device by which the Noble Qur'an is distinguished, and many specimens of it will come before you.
2- Ascribing the pronoun to Allah the Exalted in the saying of the Exalted «أَفَلا يَرَوْنَ أَنَّا نَأْتِي الْأَرْضَ نَنْقُصُها مِنْ أَطْرافِها»: the Glorified ascribed the pronoun to Himself to honour the Muslims at whose hands He brought about the great victory and the conquest of lands and cities, their armies and detachments raiding the land of the polytheists, coming upon it as victors and diminishing it from its outlying regions. Its original sense is "the armies of the Muslims come", but He ascribed the coming to Himself in commendation of the worth of the mujāhidūn and in honour of the great deeds they accomplished. And what of one who does a deed that Allah ascribes to Himself — is it not fitting that he be the confirmation of His saying in His hadith: «كنت سمعه الذي يسمع به وبصره الذي يبصر به ويده التي يبطش بها» ("I become his hearing with which he hears, his sight with which he sees and his hand with which he strikes") — to the end of the ḥadīth qudsī.
3- Three hyperboles:
In the saying of the Exalted «وَلَئِنْ مَسَّتْهُمْ نَفْحَةٌ مِنْ عَذابِ رَبِّكَ لَيَقُولُنَّ يا وَيْلَنا» there are three hyperboles:
a- The mention of touching (al-mass), which is the least thing — indeed a very gentle thing; so what do you think if it poured down upon them? That is, it suffices to show their abasement, the lowliness of their affair and the weakness of their resolve that the slightest touch is enough for them to submit, humble themselves, and declare their abasement and submission and confess against themselves that they feigned deafness and turned away. Al-Mutanabbī aimed at the heights of this hyperbole when he said, describing a cowardly people:
وضاقت الأرض حتى كاد هاربهم ... إذا رأى غير شيء ظنه رجلا
(The earth grew so narrow that their fugitive, when he saw nothing at all, almost took it for a man.)
b- The meaning of smallness and scantiness in "nafḥa": one says nafaḥathu al-dābba (the animal kicked him lightly) and nafaḥahu bi-ʿaṭiyya (he gave him a small gift).
c- The use of the noun of a single instance (al-marra) from nafḥ: the maṣdar of single instance comes on the pattern faʿla, i.e. a single breath, with no second, suffices to scatter their affair, weaken their being and crack their ranks — so what if it were reinforced by a second or a third?

* Benefits:
The maṣdars of single instance and of manner:
The maṣdar of single instance (maṣdar al-marra) is what is mentioned to show the number of times the act occurs. From the bare triliteral it is formed on the pattern faʿla, with fatḥa on the fāʾ and sukūn on the ʿayn, e.g. وقفت وقفة ووقفتين ووقفات ("I stopped once, twice, several times"). If the verb has more than three letters, the tāʾ is attached to its maṣdar, e.g. أكرمته إكرامة, فرّحته تفريحة, تدحرج تدحرجة — unless the maṣdar already originally has the tāʾ, in which case something indicating the number is mentioned after it, e.g. رحمته رحمة واحدة ("I had mercy on him once"), أقمت إقامة واحدة and استقمت استقامة واحدة.
As for the maṣdar of kind or manner (maṣdar al-nawʿ or al-hayʾa), it is what is mentioned to show the kind and quality of the act, e.g. وقفت وقفة [Translator's note: so in the source; the manner pattern would be وِقفة, with kasra]. From the bare triliteral it is formed on the pattern fiʿla, with kasra on the fāʾ, e.g. عاش عيشة حسنة ("he lived a good life"), مات ميتة سيئة ("he died an evil death"), فلان حسن الجلسة ("so-and-so has a fine manner of sitting") and فلانة هادئة المشية ("so-and-so has a calm gait"). If the verb has more than three letters, its maṣdar becomes a maṣdar of kind by description, e.g. أكرمته إكراما عظيما ("I honoured him with a great honouring").
Here there is an important caution pointed out by Shaykh Abū Ḥayyān: this tāʾ indicating a single instance does not enter upon every maṣdar, but upon maṣdars issuing from the limbs and perceptible by the senses, such as قومة, ضربة, قعدة and أكلة. As for the maṣdars of inward acts and of great, fixed qualities, such as elegance, beauty, cowardice and knowledge, one does not say of them علمته علمة, nor فهمته فهمة, nor صبرته صبرة.

dervis-irab:76-82.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الْحَرْثِ): crops; the verb's pattern is naṣara or kataba, as in al-Mukhtār. In al-Qāmūs: "al-ḥarth is a verbal noun, and (also) the land that is made to produce by seed, date-stones and planting." Ibn ʿAbbās and most of the exegetes said that the ḥarth was a vineyard whose bunches of grapes were hanging low; it was also said to have been a sown field.
(نَفَشَتْ): scattered and spread out in it, so that they grazed it and ruined it. In al-Mukhtār: "nafashat al-ghanam wa-l-ibil means that they grazed at night without a herdsman, from the pattern jalasa ... and al-nafash, with two fatḥas, is the noun from it, and from it comes the saying of the Exalted «إِذْ نَفَشَتْ فِيهِ غَنَمُ الْقَوْمِ»; nafash occurs only at night." Nafasha al-ṣūf wa-l-quṭn (he fluffed wool and cotton) is from the pattern naṣara, and al-nafsh is the separating out of a thing with your fingers until it spreads.
(لَبُوسٍ): al-labūs is clothing (libās). He said: "Wear for every situation its own garment (labūs)." What is meant is the coat of mail. Qatāda said: they were plates; the first to link them into rings and shape them was Dāwūd, so they combined lightness with protection, and this is what is called the coat of mail (dirʿ). The word dirʿ, as in al-Mukhtār, is feminine; Abū ʿUbayda said it is used both as feminine and masculine.

* I'rab:
(وَنُوحاً إِذْ نادى مِنْ قَبْلُ فَاسْتَجَبْنا لَهُ فَنَجَّيْناهُ وَأَهْلَهُ مِنَ الْكَرْبِ الْعَظِيمِ) «ونوحا» is conjoined (ʿaṭf) to «لوطا», so it shares with it the governing verb, which is «آتينا» explained by the overt «آتينا»; likewise «داود» and «سليمان». The implied sense is: "and Nūḥ We gave him judgment, and Dāwūd and Sulaymān We gave them both judgment." «إذ» is a badal ishtimāl (inclusive substitute) from «نوحا» and «داود» and «سليمان». You may also parse it as a direct object (mafʿūl bihi) of an omitted verb, i.e. "and remember Nūḥ and Dāwūd and Sulaymān", meaning: remember their account and story; in that case «إذ» is accusative by the implied muḍāf itself, i.e. "their account that occurred at such-and-such a time". The clause «نادى» is the genitive complement (muḍāf ilayhi) of it. «ومن قبل» is attached to «نادى». «فاستجبنا» is conjoined to «نادى». «وله» is attached to «استجبنا». «فنجيناه» is conjoined to «استجبنا». «ومن الكرب» is attached to «نجيناه», and «العظيم» is an adjective (naʿt).
(وَنَصَرْناهُ مِنَ الْقَوْمِ الَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا بِآياتِنا إِنَّهُمْ كانُوا قَوْمَ سَوْءٍ فَأَغْرَقْناهُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ)
«ونصرناه»: verb, agent and direct object. «ومن القوم» is attached to «نصرناه». «والذين» is an adjective of «القوم». The clause «كذبوا بآياتنا» is the ṣila (relative clause). «إن» and its noun; and the clause «كانوا» is its predicate. The clause «إنهم» is a causal clause with no grammatical position. «قوم سوء» is the predicate of «كانوا». «فأغرقناهم» is conjoined to what precedes, and «أجمعين» is tawkīd (emphasis) for the hāʾ.
(وَداوُدَ وَسُلَيْمانَ إِذْ يَحْكُمانِ فِي الْحَرْثِ إِذْ نَفَشَتْ فِيهِ غَنَمُ الْقَوْمِ وَكُنَّا لِحُكْمِهِمْ شاهِدِينَ) «وداود وسليمان»: their parsing has already been given. «وإذ» is an adverb, a badal from the omitted muḍāf, i.e. "remember the story of Dāwūd and Sulaymān". The clause «يحكمان» is its genitive complement. «وفي الحرث» is attached to «يحكمان». «وإذ» is an adverb attached to the badal of the omitted muḍāf. The clause «نفشت» is its genitive complement. «وفيه» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «نفشت». «وغنم القوم» is the agent (fāʿil). A summary of the story will come in the section on Benefits. «وكنا»: the wāw is a conjunction; kāna and its noun; «وشاهدين» is its predicate; «ولحكمهم» is attached to «شاهدين». The pronoun is plural because He intended the two of them together with those who brought their dispute to them; or because it is a pronoun by which the dual is meant, the plural having been put in the place of the dual figuratively; or because the dual is a plural, the minimum of a plural being two. What indicates that the dual is meant is the reading of Ibn ʿAbbās, «لحكمهما», in dual form.
(فَفَهَّمْناها سُلَيْمانَ وَكُلًّا آتَيْنا حُكْماً وَعِلْماً) «ففهمناها» is conjoined to «يحكمان» because it has the sense of the past, i.e. "We made him understand the right answer in it". «فهمناها»: verb, agent and direct object; «سليمان» is the second direct object. «وكلا» is the first direct object, fronted, of «آتينا», and «حكما وعلما» are the second direct object of «آتينا».
(وَسَخَّرْنا مَعَ داوُدَ الْجِبالَ يُسَبِّحْنَ وَالطَّيْرَ وَكُنَّا فاعِلِينَ) «وسخرنا»: verb and agent. «ومع» is an adverb of place attached to «سخرنا». «وداود» is a muḍāf ilayhi. «والجبال» is the direct object. The clause «يسبحن» is a ḥāl clause from «الجبال», i.e. "glorifying"; it may also be resumptive. «والطير» is conjoined to «الجبال», or is an object of accompaniment (mafʿūl maʿahu). «وكنا»: the wāw is a conjunction; kāna and its noun; «وفاعلين» is its predicate.
(وَعَلَّمْناهُ صَنْعَةَ لَبُوسٍ لَكُمْ لِتُحْصِنَكُمْ مِنْ بَأْسِكُمْ فَهَلْ أَنْتُمْ شاكِرُونَ) «وعلمناه» is conjoined to what precedes; «علمناه»: verb, agent and direct object. «وصنعة» is the second object of «علمناه»; «ولبوس» is a muḍāf ilayhi. «ولكم» may be attached to an omitted element serving as an adjective of «لبوس», in which case the lām is for possession (tamlīk); or it may be attached to «علمناه», in which case the lām is causal (taʿlīl), and on this view the phrase «لتحصنكم» is a badal with the lām repeated, i.e. "for you and for your protection"; on the first view the phrase «لتحصنكم» is attached to «علمنا». «ولتحصنكم»: the lām is causal; «تحصنكم» is an imperfect verb made accusative by an implied «أن» after the lām of cause; the agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "she (hiya)"; the kāf is the direct object; «ومن بأسكم» is attached to «تحصنكم». The fāʾ is resumptive; «وأنتم» is the mubtadaʾ and «وشاكرون» is the khabar.
(وَلِسُلَيْمانَ الرِّيحَ عاصِفَةً تَجْرِي بِأَمْرِهِ إِلى الْأَرْضِ الَّتِي بارَكْنا فِيها) The wāw is a conjunction; «ولسليمان» is attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being «سخرنا»; «والريح» is the direct object of the omitted verb understood from His saying «وَسَخَّرْنا مَعَ داوُدَ الْجِبالَ»; «وعاصفة» is a ḥāl; the clause «تجري بأمره» is a second ḥāl; «والى الأرض» is attached to «تجري»; «والتي» is an adjective; the clause «باركنا فيها» is the ṣila.
(وَكُنَّا بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عالِمِينَ) The wāw is a conjunction; «وكنا»: kāna and its noun; «وبكل شيء» is attached to «عالمين», and «وعالمين» is its predicate.
(وَمِنَ الشَّياطِينِ مَنْ يَغُوصُونَ لَهُ) «ومن الشياطين» is a fronted predicate; «ومن» may be a relative noun or an indefinite (mawṣūf) noun, as a postponed mubtadaʾ; and you may conjoin it, as a coordinate, to «الريح». The clause «يغوصون» is a ṣila or an adjective. The pronoun is plural by taking «من» according to its meaning, and what made this fine is that a plural has preceded it. «وله» is attached to «يغوصون».
(وَيَعْمَلُونَ عَمَلًا دُونَ ذلِكَ وَكُنَّا لَهُمْ حافِظِينَ) «ويعملون» is conjoined to «يغوصون»; «وعملا» is a direct object or an absolute object (mafʿūl muṭlaq); «ودون» is an adverb attached to an omitted element serving as an adjective; «وذلك» is a muḍāf ilayhi; «وكنا»: kāna and its noun; «وحافظين» is the predicate; «ولهم» is attached to «حافظين».

* Rhetoric:
In His saying: «وَداوُدَ وَسُلَيْمانَ إِذْ يَحْكُمانِ فِي الْحَرْثِ» etc. there is the figure "combining the differing and the harmonious" (jamʿ al-mukhtalif wa-l-muʾtalif). It means that the speaker wishes to put two praised persons on an equal footing, so he brings harmonious meanings in praise of both, and then wishes to give one of them preference over the other by an added merit which does not diminish the praise of the other; for the sake of that preference he brings meanings that differ from the meanings of equality. Before we speak of the verse, we cite verses by al-Khansāʾ that make this figure plain; she composed them on her brother Ṣakhr, wishing to make him equal in merit to his father, while respecting the father's right by an added merit that does not diminish the praise of the son. She said:
جارى أباه فأقبلا وهما ... يتعاوران ملاءة الحضر
وهما وقد برزا كأنهما ... صقران قد حطّا إلى وكر
حتى إذا نزت القلوب وقد ... لزت هناك العذر بالعذر
وعلا هتاف الناس أيهما ... قال المجيب هناك: لا أدري
برقت صحيفة وجه والده ... ومضى على غلوائه يجري
أولى فأولى أن يساويه ... لولا جلال السن والكبر
(He raced his father, and the two came on, taking turns in wearing the wrap of the race. / The two of them, when they came out into the open, were like two falcons swooping down to a nest. / Until hearts leapt, and the cheek-straps were pressed tight against one another there. / The shouting of the people rose, "Which of them?"; the one asked there said, "I do not know." / The page of his father's face shone, and he went on running in his headlong course. / Closer and closer it was to his equalling him, were it not for the venerability of age and years.)
Let us now speak about the verse and the verses together, so that the reality of this wondrous figure becomes clear to you. In the verse, the beginning put Dāwūd and Sulaymān, peace be upon them, on an equal footing in their fitness for judgment; then its end gave preference to Sulaymān, where He says «فَفَهَّمْناها سُلَيْمانَ». Then a turn (iltifāt) took place toward respecting (the father's right), so He brought what stands in the place of that surplus by which Sulaymān was preferred, to guide to equality in merit, so that the merit of age and what it brings with it of abundant experience and life's seasoning stands in the place of the surplus by which Sulaymān was preferred in judgment. As for the meaning of al-Khansāʾ's poetry: after her saying about equality:
وهما وقد برزا كأنهما ... صقران قد حطا إلى وكر
(The two of them, when they came out into the open, were like two falcons swooping down to a nest.)
and after her saying in the same vein:
حتى إذا نزت القلوب وقد ... لزت هناك العذر بالعذر
(Until hearts leapt, and the cheek-straps were pressed tight against one another there.)
she means that the straps of the bridles were pressed one against another (al-ʿudhur is the plural of ʿidhār, the strap that lies on the animal's cheek from the bridle), and this indicates equality in running. Then she said, in giving preference to the father:
برقت صحيفة وجه والده ... ومضى على غلوائه يجري
(The page of his father's face shone, and he went on running in his headlong course.)
She means that his face emerged from the dust ahead of the face of his rival, by outstripping him. Then she said, in joining the son to the father in merit:
أولى فأولى أن يساويه ... لولا جلال السن والكبر
(Closer and closer it was to his equalling him, were it not for the venerability of age and years.)
She means that the son was able to equal the father were it not for the courtesy he had bound himself to out of dutifulness to his father and knowledge of his right; so he held back his rein and lowered the wing of his merit, in order to prefer his father to himself in merit.
The noble verse put Dāwūd and Sulaymān on an equal footing in their fitness for judgment and made them partners in it where it says «إِذْ يَحْكُمانِ فِي الْحَرْثِ»; and it informed that Allah the Exalted made Sulaymān understand the correct judgment, so he excelled his father in that after the equality. Then the Exalted turned toward respecting the father's right and said: «وَكُلًّا آتَيْنا حُكْماً وَعِلْماً», so the two returned by that to equality after the preference of Sulaymān, so that the son might know thereby the dutifulness due to the father and recognise the right the father has over him. Thus when a reflective reader considers this speech and says, "From where did equality in judgment and knowledge come, after the report that Sulaymān understood of the judgment what his father did not understand?", he will know that the right of fatherhood stood in the place of that merit, so equality was achieved. And in this speech there is achieved, beyond the meaning of al-Khansāʾ, after their sharing in "combining the differing and the harmonious", another kind of beauty called iltifāt (turning), namely in His saying within it «وَكُنَّا لِحُكْمِهِمْ شاهِدِينَ». And there is embedded in this iltifāt another kind of beauty called tankīt (the pointed remark): for the point for whose sake the pronoun was made plural, though it should have been dual, is the indication that this judgment is to be followed and must be taken as a model, because it is the very truth and the essence of justice. And how could it not be so, when the Exalted has informed that He is a witness to it, that is, it is watched over by His very sight, the Mighty and Majestic. It is also possible that the pronoun to which "judgment" is added was made plural because judgment necessarily involves a judge, the one judged in favour of and the one judged against, so the pronoun was made plural for that reason.
Now among the charming things said on combining the harmonious and the differing is the saying of al-Khubz Arzī, whose name was Naṣr Allāh b. Aḥmad al-Baṣrī; he was unlettered, baked rice bread in Basra and recited love poems. He said:
رأيت الهلال ووجه الحبيب ... فكانا هلالين عند النظر
فلم أدر من حيرتي فيهما ... هلال السما من هلال البشر
ولولا التورد في الوجنتين ... وما لاح لي من خلال الشعر
لكنت أظن الهلال الحبيب ... وكنت أظن الحبيب القمر
(I saw the crescent and the face of the beloved, and to the eye they were two crescents. / In my bewilderment about them I did not know the crescent of the sky from the crescent of humankind. / Were it not for the blush of the two cheeks and what showed to me through the hair, / I would have thought the crescent the beloved, and I would have thought the beloved the moon.)
Here he first made them equal, then went back and preferred the beloved over the crescent.
[Translator's note: in the source the lines of this poem are run together and the word «خلال» is split across a line break; the verses are given above in their evident order.]

* Benefits:
The story of the judgment of Dāwūd and Sulaymān concerning the crop:
We shall summarise the story of the judgment of Dāwūd and Sulaymān concerning the crop, on account of the charm it contains, so that it may spur the pens of story-writers to render it in the manner of the story of the People of the Cave. History has related that two men came to Dāwūd, peace be upon him, one the owner of a crop and the other the owner of sheep. The owner of the crop said: "This man's sheep broke loose and fell upon my crop and ruined it, leaving nothing of it." So Dāwūd gave him the sheep themselves in compensation for the crop. They went out and passed by Sulaymān, who was eleven years old, and he said: "How did he judge between you?" They told him, and Sulaymān said: "Had I been in charge of your affair, I would have judged otherwise." It is related that he said: "Other than this is kinder to both parties." Dāwūd was told of that and summoned him and said: "How would you judge?" It is related that he said: "By the right of prophethood and fatherhood, tell me what is kinder to both parties." He said (Sulaymān):
"I would give the sheep to the owner of the crop to benefit from their milk, their offspring and their wool, and the owner of the sheep would sow for the owner of the crop the like of his crop; when the crop has become as it was, it is handed back to its owner, and the owner of the sheep takes his sheep." Dāwūd said: "The judgment is what you have judged," as the Exalted said: «فَفَهَّمْناها سُلَيْمانَ», that is, We taught him the case. It is also related that Sulaymān said: "I think the sheep should be given to the owners of the crop, who benefit from their milk, their young and their wool, and the crop to the owners of the sheep, who tend it until it returns to the state it was in on the day it was ruined; then they exchange back." He (Dāwūd) said: "The judgment is what you have judged," and he carried out the ruling accordingly.

The ruling under Islamic law:
As for the ruling of this case in Islamic law, al-Zamakhsharī asked about it in his Kashshāf and said: "If you say: if this incident occurred in our sharia, what would its ruling be? I say: Abū Ḥanīfa and his companions, may Allah be pleased with them, hold that there is no liability, whether by night or by day, unless the animal has a driver or a leader with it; and al-Shāfiʿī, may Allah be pleased with him, makes liability obligatory by night."
One question remains here: why was a plural pronoun used for two in His saying «وَكُنَّا لِحُكْمِهِمْ شاهِدِينَ»?
There are two answers. The first is that the dual is meant even though the pronoun is plural, because the dual is the minimum of the plural. The second is that the verbal noun, being annexed, is annexed to the two judges, Dāwūd and Sulaymān, and the one judged against; these then are a group. But on this view the verbal noun is annexed to its agent and its object at one and the same time, whereas it is annexed to only one of them, and it involves combining the literal and the figurative, for the literal is the annexation of the verbal noun to its agent and the figurative is its annexation to its object.
Among the marvels of Sulaymān's judgment is what Muslim related in the ḥadīth of Abū Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet ﷺ: "While two women were there, each with her son, the wolf came and carried off one of them. This one said: 'It was only your son it carried off,' and the other said: 'It was only your son it carried off.' They took their dispute to Dāwūd, peace be upon him, who judged the child for the elder. They passed by Sulaymān and told him, and he said: 'Bring me a knife so that I may split him between you.' The younger said: 'No, may Allah have mercy on you!' So he judged the child for the younger." Abū Hurayra said:
"By Allah, though I had heard of the word sikkīn before that, I used to say only mudya."
He said in al-Qāmūs: "al-sikkīn is feminine, like al-sakīna, and its maker is called sakkān and sakākīnī." This said, Dāwūd was famed for making coats of mail, breastplates and the like, and Abū al-Ṭayyib al-Mutanabbī looked toward the sky of this craft when he said, describing his bedding and clothing in boasting of himself:
مفرشي صهوة الحصان ولكنّ ... قميصي مسرودة من حديد
لأمة فاضة أهناة دلاص ... أحكمت نسجها يدا داود
(My bedding is the saddle of the steed, and my shirt is a linked coat of iron. / A close-fitting, ample, smooth mail, whose weaving the hands of Dāwūd made firm.)
He says: I am brave and never leave the horse's back, and what I wear is the coat of mail, and my shirt is a lāʾma, that is, one whose workmanship is closely joined and whose weave is firm, made by Dāwūd, who was the first to make the coat of mail.
Another question: how is the wind subjected to Sulaymān described as "violent" (ʿāṣif), and elsewhere described as "gentle" (rukhāʾ), so that it is described at one time by violence and at another by gentleness? Al-Zamakhsharī answered this question with rare brilliance, saying: "In itself it was gentle and pleasant like a breeze, but when it passed by his throne it bore it far in a short time, as He said «غدوها شهر ورواحها شهر» (its morning course a month and its evening course a month). So its combining the two things, being gentle in itself and violent in its effect, while obeying Sulaymān and blowing as he willed and commanded, is a sign upon a sign and a miracle upon a miracle. It was also said that at one time it was gentle and at another violent, blowing according to the dictates of his will."
I say: Similar to this description is the description of Mūsā's staff, at one time as a jānn and at another as a thuʿbān; the jānn is the slender kind of snake and the thuʿbān the large, coarse kind. The reason is that it combined the two descriptions: in its lightness and speed of movement it was like the jānn, and in the greatness of its build like the thuʿbān. Poets have looked toward the sky of this meaning and described the union of two opposites in one described thing. Ibn al-Rūmī said, describing the singer Waḥīd:
خلقت فتنة غناء وحسنا ... ما لها فيهما جميعا نديد
فهي نعمى يميد منها كبير ... وهي بلوى يشيب منها الوليد
(She was created a temptation of song and beauty, with no equal to her in both together. / She is a blessing at which a grown man sways with delight, and a trial at which a newborn turns grey.)
He described her as a blessing at which the elder sways with delight, and then as a trial at which the young turns grey: if she keeps in touch, she gives life, and if she deserts, she kills. And he said in this delightful ode, which I would like you to consult in his Dīwān:
ما تزالين نظرة منك موت ... لي مميت ونظرة تخليد
نتلاقى فلحظة منك وعد ... بوصال ولحظة تهديد
(You never cease: one glance of yours is a death that kills me, and one glance an immortalising. / We meet, and one look from you is a promise of union, and another look a threat.)
This is plentiful in poetry, and we content ourselves with this example.
[Translator's note: in the source Ibn al-Rūmī's second line is glossed as "the young turns grey" for «الوليد»; "newborn" is the literal sense of the word.]

dervis-irab:48-55.t:
* Vocabulary:
(التَّماثِيلُ): plural of timthāl (with kasra on the tāʾ), that is, the fashioned image, or what one makes and depicts in imitation of Allah's creation of living beings and forms. This pattern has two additional letters, one before the fāʾ and the other before the lām, and it has occurred as both a noun and an adjective. The noun is timthāl for the image, pluralised as tamāthīl. They also said tajfāf and tibyān: tajfāf is the singular of tajāfīf al-faras, which is what is put on [the horse] for war and for adornment; and tibyān has the meaning of bayān, and some make it a maṣdar of the irregular kind, because maṣdars come on the pattern tafʿāl with fatḥa, such as al-talʿāb and al-tihdār, and none came with kasra except tibyān and tilqāʾ; Sībawayh makes both of them nouns that were put in the place of maṣdars, like al-ghāra, which was put in the place of al-ighāra. More than one of the scholars of the language said: al-timthāl is the image made of marble, copper or wood resembling the creation of the human being.

* I'rab:
(وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنا مُوسى وَهارُونَ الْفُرْقانَ وَضِياءً وَذِكْراً لِلْمُتَّقِينَ): the wāw is resumptive, and the clause is resumptive, introduced to begin the stories of the prophets, upon them be peace, as consolation for His Messenger ﷺ regarding what he endures from his people, to strengthen his heart and urge him to continue in delivering the message; ten stories of them are mentioned in this sura and they will come. The lām is the response to an omitted oath, qad is a particle of verification, ātaynā is a verb and agent, Mūsā is the direct object, Hārūna is conjoined to Mūsā, al-Furqāna is a second direct object, ḍiyāʾan is conjoined to al-Furqāna and dhikran is conjoined to ḍiyāʾan, and lil-muttaqīna, the two are attached to ḍiyāʾan. Conjoining attributes is permissible, so this is of that kind. Al-Zamakhsharī preferred that it be parsed as a ḥāl whose governor is omitted, indicated by what precedes, and he implied: "and We gave through it a light". As for what some thought, that the wāw is redundant and ḍiyāʾan a ḥāl from al-Furqān, that is mere arbitrariness which we do not hesitate to reject.
(الَّذِينَ يَخْشَوْنَ رَبَّهُمْ بِالْغَيْبِ وَهُمْ مِنَ السَّاعَةِ مُشْفِقُونَ): alladhīna is a relative noun in the position of genitive as an adjective of al-muttaqīna, and you may parse it as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, that is, "hum alladhīna"; the clause yakhshawna is the ṣila, the wāw is the agent, rabbahum is the direct object, and bil-ghaybi is a ḥāl from the agent in yakhshawna; wa-hum: the wāw is a conjunction or a ḥāl wāw, hum is a mubtadaʾ, min al-sāʿati, the preposition and its genitive noun, are attached to mushfiqūna, and mushfiqūna is their khabar. The secret of the use of the nominal form will come in the chapter on Rhetoric. (وَهذا ذِكْرٌ مُبارَكٌ أَنْزَلْناهُ أَفَأَنْتُمْ لَهُ مُنْكِرُونَ): the wāw is resumptive and the clause is resumptive, to address the people of Mecca and converse with them about the Noble Qur'an that was sent down in their tongue. Hādhā is a mubtadaʾ, dhikrun a khabar, mubārakun an adjective, and the clause anzalnāhu an adjective of dhikr, being a verb, agent and direct object; the hamza is for a reproachful question, because it addresses the Arabs, who are the people of the Arabic tongue and the mines of eloquence, so how fit they are to fathom the secrets of the Qur'an and grasp its eloquence. The fāʾ is conjoined to an omitted element, antum is a mubtadaʾ, lahu, the two are attached to munkirūna, and munkirūna is the khabar of antum. (وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنا إِبْراهِيمَ رُشْدَهُ مِنْ قَبْلُ وَكُنَّا بِهِ عالِمِينَ): the wāw is a conjunction, the lām is the response to an omitted oath, qad is a particle of verification, ātaynā is a verb and agent, Ibrāhīma is the first direct object and rushdahu the second direct object, and min qablu is a ḥāl, that is, before Mūsā and Hārūn. Wa-kunnā: the wāw is a conjunction, kāna and its noun; bihi, the two are attached to ʿālimīna, and ʿālimīna is the khabar of kunnā. (إِذْ قالَ لِأَبِيهِ وَقَوْمِهِ ما هذِهِ التَّماثِيلُ الَّتِي أَنْتُمْ لَها عاكِفُونَ؟): the adverb is attached to an omitted verb, that is, "udhkur" (remember), and you may attach it to ʿālimīna, and al-Zamakhsharī also attached it to ātaynā or to rushdahu, and there is nothing to prevent that. The clause qāla is annexed to the adverb; li-abīhi, the two are attached to qāla, and qawmihi is conjoined to li-abīhi. Mā is an interrogative noun, a mubtadaʾ, and hādhihi the khabar; al-tamāthīlu is a badal from the demonstrative; allatī is an adjective, and the clause antum lahā ʿākifūna is the ṣila of the relative; antum is a mubtadaʾ and ʿākifūna a khabar, and lahā, the two are attached to ʿākifūna. The secret of his turning from saying "ʿalayhā ʿākifūna" to "lahā ʿākifūna" will come in the chapter on Rhetoric. (قالُوا وَجَدْنا آباءَنا لَها عابِدِينَ): qālū is a verb and agent; wajadnā is a verb and agent, and the clause is the content of the saying; ābāʾanā is the first object of wajadnā; lahā, the two are attached to ʿābidīna, and ʿābidīna is the second object of wajadnā. (قالَ: لَقَدْ كُنْتُمْ أَنْتُمْ وَآباؤُكُمْ فِي ضَلالٍ مُبِينٍ): the lām is the response to an omitted oath, qad is a particle of verification, kuntum is kāna and its noun, antum is emphasis for the tāʾ, ābāʾukum is conjoined to the tāʾ, fī ḍalālin is the khabar of kuntum, and mubīn is an adjective of ḍalāl. (قالُوا: أَجِئْتَنا بِالْحَقِّ أَمْ أَنْتَ مِنَ اللَّاعِبِينَ): the hamza is for a question; ji'tanā is a verb, agent and direct object; bil-ḥaqqi, the two are attached to ji'tanā; am is a conjunction equivalent to the hamza; anta is a mubtadaʾ and min al-lāʿibīna is its khabar.

* Rhetoric:
1- Turning from the verbal sentence to the nominal: In His saying, Exalted is He: «وَهُمْ مِنَ السَّاعَةِ مُشْفِقُونَ» there is a turning from address by the verbal sentence, as the context requires, to address by the nominal sentence. One turns from one of the two kinds of address, even if the context requires it, for a kind of emphasis and hyperbole, and it is brought here to single out the particular after the general: fear of Allah is constant with them, but fear of the Hour is more constant and takes stronger hold of their hearts and binds their limbs; they do not leave off remembering it, and avoid every sin out of fear of confronting it in the state they are in. A second matter is the permanence and continuity that the nominal sentence conveys more than the verbal sentence, which is distributed over the tenses.
2- In His saying, Exalted is He: «ما هذِهِ التَّماثِيلُ الَّتِي أَنْتُمْ لَها عاكِفُونَ» there is a turning from ʿalā, with which the verb ʿukūf is made transitive, but he did not intend the transitivity; had he intended it, he would have said "ʿalayhā". He turned from it to lām because he intended by ʿukūf the meaning of worship, so that they would answer him with their words «وَجَدْنا آباءَنا لَها عابِدِينَ», and that they do not part from blind imitation; and in that is a censure of imitation, of speaking without proof, and of being dragged along to what their fathers were on, even with the ropes. It suffices the people of imitation as a disgrace that the worshippers of idols and statues are among them. It was also said that the lām means ʿalā, and the grammarians have stated that it comes with the meaning of ʿalā, but this loses the point we hinted at, so it is better to keep it in its usual sense of specification, which is the principal meaning of the lām.
3- The two clauses in the verse «قالُوا أَجِئْتَنا بِالْحَقِّ أَمْ أَنْتَ مِنَ اللَّاعِبِينَ» differ in form in order to note renewal in one, which appeared in the form of the verbal sentence, and permanence in the other, which appeared in the form of the nominal sentence. The meaning: "Have you newly brought the truth, namely monotheism, in what we hear from you, or are you as you have been in playing since the days of childhood?" By renewal in the first clause they meant that monotheism is a newly invented matter, and by permanence in the second that it is their continuing habit of playing, to belittle him. How ugly is their error in imitating their fathers in worshipping an inanimate thing lower than themselves in rank, as they carve it with their own hands and then rub their faces and foreheads in the dust before it.

dervis-irab:83-88.t:
* I'rab:
(وَأَيُّوبَ إِذْ نادى رَبَّهُ أَنِّي مَسَّنِيَ الضُّرُّ وَأَنْتَ أَرْحَمُ الرَّاحِمِينَ) «وأيوب» is the direct object (mafʿūl bihi) of an omitted verb, its implied form being "remember"; it rests on an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "remember the account of Ayyūb". «وإذ» is a badal (substitute) from "account", that is, from the implied muḍāf, and the clause «نادى ربه» is its genitive complement (muḍāf ilayhi). «وربه» is the direct object of «نادى». «وأني»: «أن» and what is within its scope is accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. "that (bi-annī)"; «أن» and its noun, and the clause «مسني الضر» is the khabar of «أن». «وأنت»: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); «وأنت» is the mubtadaʾ, «وأرحم» the khabar, and «والراحمين» a muḍāf ilayhi; it will be treated in the section on Benefits.
(فَاسْتَجَبْنا لَهُ فَكَشَفْنا ما بِهِ مِنْ ضُرٍّ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; «واستجبنا»: verb and agent; «وله» is attached to «استجبنا». «فكشفنا» is conjoined to «فاستجبنا»; «وما» is the direct object; «وبه» is the ṣila (relative clause) of «ما»; «ومن ضر» is a ḥāl (circumstantial).
(وَآتَيْناهُ أَهْلَهُ وَمِثْلَهُمْ مَعَهُمْ رَحْمَةً مِنْ عِنْدِنا وَذِكْرى لِلْعابِدِينَ) «وآتيناه»: verb, agent and direct object; «وأهله» is the second direct object; «ومثلهم» is conjoined to «أهله», or is an object of accompaniment (mafʿūl maʿahu); «ومعهم» is an adverb of place attached to an omitted element serving as a ḥāl, i.e. "being with them". «ورحمة» is an object of purpose (mafʿūl li-ajlihi); it is also possible that it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) of an implied verb, i.e. "We had mercy on him with a mercy", but the first is preferable. «ومن عندنا» is an adjective (naʿt) of «رحمة»; «وذكرى» is conjoined to «رحمة»; «وللعابدين» is attached to «ذكرى».
(وَإِسْماعِيلَ وَإِدْرِيسَ وَذَا الْكِفْلِ كُلٌّ مِنَ الصَّابِرِينَ) «وإسماعيل» is the direct object of an omitted verb, i.e. "and remember"; it is also possible that it is conjoined as a coordinate to the prophets mentioned before. «وإدريس» is conjoined to «إسماعيل». «وذا الكفل» is likewise conjoined; the reason for his being so named will come in the section on Benefits. «وكل» is the mubtadaʾ and «ومن الصابرين» its khabar.
(وَأَدْخَلْناهُمْ فِي رَحْمَتِنا إِنَّهُمْ مِنَ الصَّالِحِينَ) The clause is conjoined; «وان» and its noun, and «ومن الصالحين» is its khabar.
(وَذَا النُّونِ إِذْ ذَهَبَ مُغاضِباً فَظَنَّ أَنْ لَنْ نَقْدِرَ عَلَيْهِ) «وذا النون» is the direct object of an omitted verb, or is conjoined as a coordinate to those mentioned before; its discussion will come in the section on Benefits. «وإذ» is a badal from the omitted muḍāf as before, and the clause «ذهب» is its genitive complement. «ومغاضبا» is a ḥāl, meaning (angry) at his people, not at his Lord, that is, he was angry with them because of what he had endured from them. «فظن»: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and «ظن» is conjoined to «ذهب», meaning: he left them and went away without being given permission. The agent of «ظن» is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "he (huwa)"; «وأن» is the lightened form of the heavy «أن», and its noun is the pronoun of the situation (ḍamīr al-shaʾn); the clause «لن نقدر عليه» is the khabar. The meaning of «لن» will come in the section on Benefits, as will a summary of his story.
(فَنادى فِي الظُّلُماتِ أَنْ لا إِلهَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ سُبْحانَكَ إِنِّي كُنْتُ مِنَ الظَّالِمِينَ) «فنادى» is conjoined to «ظن»; «وفي الظلمات» is attached to an omitted element serving as a ḥāl; «وأن» is the lightened form of the heavy «أن», its noun being the pronoun of the situation, and the clause «لا إله إلا أنت» is the khabar; it may also be explicative (tafsīriyya), because calling out contains the sense of saying without its letters. «وسبحانك» is an absolute object (mafʿūl muṭlaq) of an omitted verb, and the clause is circumstantial; «واني»: «إن» and its noun, and the clause is causal; the clause «كنت من الظالمين» is the khabar of «إني», and «ومن الظالمين» is the khabar of «كنت».
(فَاسْتَجَبْنا لَهُ وَنَجَّيْناهُ مِنَ الْغَمِّ وَكَذلِكَ نُنْجِي الْمُؤْمِنِينَ) «فاستجبنا» is conjoined to what precedes; «وله» is attached to «استجبنا»; «ونجيناه»: verb, agent and direct object; «ومن الغم» is attached to «نجيناه»; «وكذلك»: the kāf is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar; «وننجي المؤمنين»: imperfect verb, latent agent and direct object.

* Benefits:
1- Summary of the story of Ayyūb:
History relates that Ayyūb was a Roman man, of the descendants of Isḥāq b. Yaʿqūb. Allah made him a prophet and spread the world out for him; his family and wealth were many. He had seven sons and seven daughters, all kinds of livestock, and five hundred fed-an (ploughing-teams) of land followed by five hundred slaves, each slave with a wife and child, and date palms. Then Allah tried him by the loss of his children (the house collapsed on them and they perished), by the loss of his wealth, and by sickness in his body for eighteen years; it was also said thirteen years. One day his wife said to him: "If only you would call upon Allah." He said to her: "How long was the period of ease?" She said: "Eighty years." He said: "I am ashamed before Allah to call upon Him when the period of my affliction has not reached the period of my ease." When Allah removed it from him, He brought his children back to life and gave him the like of them and more besides. The story of Ayyūb is full of inspiring poetic images, and it is a rich dīwān on patience in affliction and not exulting in ease.

2- The difference between al-ḍarr and al-ḍurr:
One says ḍarr with a fatḥa on the ḍād and ḍurr with a ḍamma on it. The difference between them is that al-ḍarr with fatḥa is harm in anything, while al-ḍurr with ḍamma is harm in the person, such as emaciation and illness. The two forms are distinguished because their meanings differ. Some have versified the difference between them, as well as other meanings of both. He said:
وضدّ نفع قيل فيه ضرّ ... وجود ضرّة لعرس ضرّ
وسوء حال المرء ذاك ضرّ ... كذا هزال مرض أو كبر
(The opposite of benefit is said to be ḍarr, and having a co-wife for a wife is ḍarr. / A man's bad condition, that is ḍurr; likewise emaciation, sickness or old age.)
[Translator's note: in the source the end of this poem and the heading "3- Gentleness in asking" are run together on one line; they are separated here.]

3- Gentleness in asking:
Ayyūb was gentle in asking and hinted at the affliction he was suffering without stating what he sought, since he was content to mention the touch of harm; he introduced the generic al to «الضر» so as to include its kinds mentioned above, and described his Lord with utmost mercy after mentioning himself in terms that call for it. It was thus an eloquent lesson for everyone whom misfortunes visit in turn and hardship attacks. It is related that an old woman approached Sulaymān b. ʿAbd al-Malik and said: "O Commander of the Faithful, the mice of my house walk on sticks." He said to her: "You have been gentle in asking; I shall surely make them leap like leopards," and he filled her house with grain. Abū al-Ṭayyib al-Mutanabbī clung to the hem of this eloquence when he addressed Kāfūr with what he hoped for from him, namely that he give him a governorship, though his aim was to be indirect:
أرى لي بقربي منك عينا قريرة ... وإن كان قربا بالبعاد يشاب
وهل نافعي أن ترفع الحجب بيننا ... ودون الذي أملت منك حجاب
أقلّ سلامي حبّ ما خف عنكم ... وأسكت كيما لا يكون جواب
وفي النفس حاجات وفيك فطانة ... سكوتي بيان عندها وخطاب
(I see for myself, in my nearness to you, a cool eye, though it is a nearness mixed with distance. / And what use is it to me that the veils between us be lifted, when beyond what I hoped from you there is a veil? / I keep my greeting brief, for love of what is light upon you, and I fall silent so that there be no reply. / There are needs in the soul and you have shrewdness; my silence to it is explanation and address.)
In the third verse there is a grammatical point, namely the accusative of «حب»: he made it accusative as an object of purpose, being a maṣdar, as if he were saying "for love of what is light", that is, because of my preference for lightness. Ḥabīb b. Aws, Abū Tammām, also was gentle and gathered all his aims in one verse, which is his saying:
وإذا الجود كان عوني على المر ... ء تقاضيته بترك التقاضي
(When generosity is my helper against a man, I demand from him by leaving off demanding.)
As for Abū Bakr al-Khwārizmī, he said, drawing the plan of asking:
وإذا طلبت إلى كريم حاجة ... فلقاؤه يكفيك والتسليم
فإذا رآك مسلما عرف الذي ... حملته فكأنه ملزوم
(When you ask a generous man for a need, meeting him and greeting him suffice you. / When he sees you greeting him, he knows what you have laid on him, and it is as though he were obligated.)
[Translator's note: the source reads «خظة» in «رسم خظة الطلب»; the evident word is «خطة» (plan), and it is so rendered.]
Before them all came Umayya b. Abī al-Ṣalt with his famous saying:
أأذكر حاجتي أم قد كفاني ... حياؤك إن شيمتك الحياء
إذا أثنى عليك المرء يوما ... كفاه من تعرضه الثناء
(Shall I mention my need, or has your modesty sufficed me, since modesty is your nature? / When a man praises you one day, praise suffices him in place of his approaching you.)

4- Dhū al-Kifl:
This is his title, and al-kifl is the share. His name is Bishr; it was also said Ilyās, and it was also said Zakariyyā. It seems he was so named because he was the one who was allotted, the possessor of the fullest share of fortune. It was also said that Dhū al-Kifl was his name, for he had two names and it was not a title.

5- Dhū al-Nūn:
In al-Mukhtār: "Dhū al-Nūn is the fish (al-ḥūt); its plural is anwān and nīnān. Dhū al-Nūn is the title of Yūnus b. Mattā (on the pattern of shattā; the name of his father, as mentioned in al-Qāmūs, or the name of his mother, as Ibn al-Athīr said in al-Nihāya). It was also said he was called Dhū al-Nūn because he saw a handsome boy and said, 'Blacken his nūna, lest the evil eye strike him.' Thaʿlab related that the nūna of a boy is the dimple that is in the chin of a small boy, and the meaning of dassimū is 'blacken it'." Dhū means "possessor". Al-Suhaylī said in Kitāb al-Aʿlām, on the saying of the Exalted «وذا» النون: "He is Yūnus b. Mattā. He annexed dhū to al-nūn, which is the fish, whereas the Exalted said «وَلا تَكُنْ كَصاحِبِ الْحُوتِ», and there is a difference between them. When he was mentioned in the context of praise of him, it was said dhā al-nūn, and not ṣāḥib al-nūn, and annexation with dhū is nobler than annexation with ṣāḥib, because dhū is annexed to the follower, whereas ṣāḥib is annexed to the one followed. You say: Abū Hurayra is the companion (ṣāḥib) of the Prophet, and you do not say: the Prophet is the companion of Abū Hurayra, except in some manner. As for dhū, you say with it dhū al-mulk (possessor of sovereignty), dhū al-jalāl (possessor of majesty), dhū al-ʿarsh (possessor of the throne) and dhū al-qarnayn (the two-horned), and you find the first noun is the one followed, not a follower. For that reason the chieftains of Ḥimyar were called adhwāʾ, among them Dhū Jadan, Dhū Yazan, Dhū Ruʿayn and Dhū Kalāʿ, and in Islam Dhū al-Shahādatayn, Dhū al-Shimālayn and Dhū al-Yadayn. All of that is a magnifying of the one so named, and that is not in the word ṣāḥib, in which there is only identification, accompanied by nothing of this meaning." His story and the fish's swallowing him will come in al-Ṣāffāt.

6- The meaning of «لن نقدر عليه»:
As for the meaning of His saying «فَظَنَّ أَنْ لَنْ نَقْدِرَ عَلَيْهِ»: that We would not decree against him what We decreed, namely his confinement in the belly of the fish, or that We would not straiten him thereby; it is from qadar, not from qudra (power), as in the saying of the Exalted «اللَّهُ يَبْسُطُ الرِّزْقَ لِمَنْ يَشاءُ وَيَقْدِرُ». It is related from Ibn ʿAbbās that he went in to Muʿāwiya and said: "The waves of the Qur'an struck me last night and I drowned in them, and found no deliverance for myself except through you." He said: "What is it, O Ibn ʿAbbās?" He recited this verse to him and said: "Would the Prophet of Allah think that He could not have power over him?" He said: "This is from qadar, not from qudra." Al-Zamakhsharī, after mentioning the view we have given, allowed that it be explained as power (qudra), in the sense that We would not make Our power operate on him, and that it be a case of figurative representation (tamthīl), meaning "his state was likened to the state of one who thought We had no power over him, in his defying his people without waiting for Allah's command".
A majority of scholars held that its meaning is: he thought that We would not straiten him, from "his provision was straitened (qudira) for him", i.e. restricted and scanty.

dervis-irab:106-112.t:
* I'rab:
(إِنَّ فِي هذا لَبَلاغاً لِقَوْمٍ عابِدِينَ) إنّ: a particle resembling the verb (ḥarf mushabbah bi-l-fiʿl); فِي هذا is its predicate, fronted; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); لِقَوْمٍ is an adjective (naʿt) of بَلاغاً, and عابِدِينَ is an adjective.
(وَما أَرْسَلْناكَ إِلَّا رَحْمَةً لِلْعالَمِينَ) The wāw is a conjunction; ما is negative; أَرْسَلْناكَ is a verb, an agent and a direct object (mafʿūl bihi); إِلَّا is a particle of restriction (adāt ḥaṣr); رَحْمَةً is a mafʿūl min ajlihi (object of purpose) or a ḥāl (circumstantial), as an exaggeration in that he is made to be mercy itself, or on the basis of an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "possessor of mercy"; and لِلْعالَمِينَ is an adjective of رَحْمَةً or is attached to the very word "mercy". (قُلْ إِنَّما يُوحى إِلَيَّ أَنَّما إِلهُكُمْ إِلهٌ واحِدٌ فَهَلْ أَنْتُمْ مُسْلِمُونَ) إنّما: a restricting particle (kāffa) and a restricted one (makfūfa); يُوحى is a passive imperfect verb; إِلَيَّ is attached to يُوحى; أنّ and what is within its scope is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of يُوحى; and إِلهُكُمْ is a mubtadaʾ (subject), إِلهٌ the khabar (predicate), and واحِدٌ an adjective. The fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the eloquent fāʾ), i.e. "if you have known this"; هَلْ is a particle of interrogation; أَنْتُمْ is a mubtadaʾ and مُسْلِمُونَ a khabar. The topic of restriction (qaṣr) in both its kinds in this verse will come in the chapter on rhetoric. (فَإِنْ تَوَلَّوْا فَقُلْ آذَنْتُكُمْ عَلى سَواءٍ)
The fāʾ is resumptive; إِنْ is conditional; تَوَلَّوْا is a past verb and it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the wāw is the agent; the fāʾ links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); قُلْ is an imperative verb; آذَنْتُكُمْ is a verb, an agent and a direct object; and the clause is in the position of the jussive, as the apodosis; عَلى سَواءٍ is attached to an omitted ḥāl of the tāʾ, i.e. the agent, or of the kāf, i.e. the object, meaning "being equal in knowledge of the war"; the detailed account of this concision will come in the chapter on rhetoric. (وَإِنْ أَدْرِي أَقَرِيبٌ أَمْ بَعِيدٌ ما تُوعَدُونَ) The wāw is the wāw of ḥāl; إِنْ is negative; أَدْرِي is a nominative imperfect verb whose agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "I"; the hamza is interrogative; قَرِيبٌ is a fronted khabar; أَمْ is a conjunction; بَعِيدٌ is conjoined to it; ما is a delayed mubtadaʾ; and the clause تُوعَدُونَ is a ṣila (relative clause). Abū l-Baqāʾ allowed that ما تُوعَدُونَ be nominative as an agent of قَرِيبٌ, filling the place of its khabar, with قَرِيبٌ being a mubtadaʾ — he said, because it relies on the hamza — or as the agent of بَعِيدٌ, because it is nearer to it, in which case the matter falls under the heading of conflict (tanāzuʿ). The clause أَقَرِيبٌ أَمْ بَعِيدٌ ما تُوعَدُونَ is in the position of the accusative as the object of أَدْرِي, which has been suspended from operating (muʿallaqa). (إِنَّهُ يَعْلَمُ الْجَهْرَ مِنَ الْقَوْلِ وَيَعْلَمُ ما تَكْتُمُونَ) إنّ and its noun; the clause يَعْلَمُ is its khabar, and the agent of يَعْلَمُ is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "He", referring to Allah the Exalted; الْجَهْرَ is a direct object; مِنَ الْقَوْلِ is a ḥāl of الْجَهْرَ; وَيَعْلَمُ is conjoined to the first يَعْلَمُ; ما is a direct object; and the clause تَكْتُمُونَ is a ṣila. (وَإِنْ أَدْرِي لَعَلَّهُ فِتْنَةٌ لَكُمْ وَمَتاعٌ إِلى حِينٍ) The wāw is a conjunction; إِنْ is negative; أَدْرِي is an imperfect verb whose agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "I"; لَعَلَّ and its noun; فِتْنَةٌ is its khabar; لَكُمْ is an adjective; وَمَتاعٌ is conjoined to فِتْنَةٌ; and إِلى حِينٍ is attached to an omitted adjective of مَتاعٌ, or is attached to it directly. The clause لَعَلَّهُ فِتْنَةٌ is in the position of the accusative with أَدْرِي. The Kufans make the particle of hope (tarajjī) behave like the interrogative in suspending the verb from operating, but the grammarians did not list لَعَلَّ among the suspending elements, even though it occurs frequently in the Qur'an, as in this verse and as in His saying: «وما يدريك لعل الساعة قريب، وما يدريك لعله يزكى». It has been said that His saying وَمَتاعٌ does not fall within the scope of the hope, because it is certain, so it is not correct to conjoin it to فِتْنَةٌ; for since it would be conjoined to its khabar, it would be governed by it and would enter its scope and the sphere of the hope that it indicates. It is therefore preferable to say that وَمَتاعٌ is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "and this is an enjoyment for a while", i.e. the postponement of your punishment is an enjoyment for you, and the clause is resumptive. This is not far-fetched. (قالَ رَبِّ احْكُمْ بِالْحَقِّ وَرَبُّنَا الرَّحْمنُ الْمُسْتَعانُ عَلى ما تَصِفُونَ) رَبِّ is a vocative (munādā) annexed to the omitted first-person yāʾ; احْكُمْ is a verb of supplication whose agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "you"; بِالْحَقِّ is a ḥāl; وَرَبُّنَا: the wāw is resumptive and رَبُّنَا is a mubtadaʾ; الرَّحْمنُ may be a khabar and الْمُسْتَعانُ a second khabar, or it may be an adjective of رَبُّنَا with الْمُسْتَعانُ as the khabar, since it is what is being reported; عَلى ما is attached to الْمُسْتَعانُ; the clause تَصِفُونَ is a ṣila, and the returning pronoun is omitted, i.e. "you describe Him contrary to reality".

* Rhetoric:
1- Restriction (al-qaṣr):
In His saying «قُلْ إِنَّما يُوحى إِلَيَّ أَنَّما إِلهُكُمْ إِلهٌ واحِدٌ». The discussion of restriction has already been given in detail, and we say that in this verse there are two restrictions. The first is the restriction of the attribute to the thing described, which is the restriction of revelation to oneness, the meaning being: nothing is revealed to me except the singling out of the deity for oneness — not because nothing else has been revealed to him, but because it is the principal root of all worship and action, and is what is required first and before everything, so that what is other than it is as though not looked at, or not worthy of mention. The second is the restriction of the thing described to the attribute, which is the restriction of Allah to oneness, and this is plain.

2- Concision (al-ījāz):
This is in His saying «فَإِنْ تَوَلَّوْا فَقُلْ آذَنْتُكُمْ عَلى سَواءٍ». Much has been said before about concision. In this verse there is a concision of brevity (ījāz qaṣr), because in three words — «آذنتكم على سواء» — it speaks of what would otherwise be lengthy discourse, namely: "If they turn away after these signs and proofs, and turn aside and fold up their flanks [in aversion], then say to them: We have informed you, on equal terms, that you and I are in a war with no truce and no peace between us, but I do not know when Allah will give permission." The verb آذنتكم is derived from أَذِنَ when it means "he knew". al-Ḥārith ibn Ḥilliza said:
آذنتنا ببنيها أسماء ... رب ثاو يمل منه الثواء
(Asmāʾ announced her departure to us with her sons; many a lodger is wearied by the lodging.)
al-Zamakhsharī was eloquent in explaining this concision, and this is a portion of his words:
«The meaning is that I, after your turning away and your refusal to accept what has been offered to you of the obligation of affirming the oneness of Allah and exalting Him above rivals and partners, am like a man between whom and his enemies there is a truce, who senses treachery from them, so he casts the covenant back to them, proclaims the repudiation and spreads it, and notifies them all of it «على سواء», that is, on equal terms in the notification of it, concealing it from none of them, and being open with all of them, and peeling the staff from its bark [i.e. leaving nothing hidden].»

3- Generation (al-tawlīd):
In His saying: «قل رب احكم بالحق» is the art of tawlīd, which Ibn Munqidh called the art of delicacy (fann al-talṭīf). It is of two kinds: from words and from meanings:
1- Tawlīd from words is also of two kinds:
a- The speaker generates a form of speech from his own wording and the wording of another.
b- The speaker generates a form from two places in his own wording.
The first is that he pairs a word with another word, for a word of someone else's wording, and there is generated between them a speech that contradicts the purpose of the owner of the foreign word; this applies to single words, not to combined sentences. An example is what is related of Muṣʿab ibn al-Zubayr, that he had branded his horses with the word «ʿudda» (equipment), intending equipment for war. When he was killed and his horses came to al-Ḥajjāj, and he saw that brand, he ordered that beside «ʿudda» be branded the word «al-firār» (flight). Between the two words there came to be generated a meaning other than the one Muṣʿab had intended, and the praise turned into disparagement.
2- Tawlīd from meanings: its examples will come. As for the verse we are dealing with, He has paired one art of the badīʿ with another art within it, and a third art, other than the two, was generated. This is because an apparent difficulty arises, namely that it may be said: What is the wisdom in His, glory be to Him, commanding His Prophet to ask Him to judge with the truth, when He, the Mighty and Majestic, knows that His Prophet is certain that He judges only with the truth? Had it been limited to the saying "judge" alone, that would have sufficed. Why, then, was the more concise wording that fulfils the intended meaning and is free from apparent difficulty abandoned for the longer one that gives rise to difficulty? The answer:
The prophets, peace be upon them, do not invoke against those who oppose them until they are given leave to do so, because they were sent to reconcile hearts, not to repel them, and they know of the unseen only what Allah has made them know. So when He informs them of those among their people who cannot possibly believe, it becomes permissible for them to invoke against them. Do you not see that Noah, peace be upon him, did not venture to say: «رَبِّ لا تَذَرْ عَلَى الْأَرْضِ مِنَ الْكافِرِينَ دَيَّاراً» until after His saying to him: «أَنَّهُ لَنْ يُؤْمِنَ مِنْ قَوْمِكَ إِلَّا مَنْ قَدْ آمَنَ»; and for that reason he was cautious in the supplication with his saying «على الأرض» ("upon the earth"), since those who believed with him were in the ark, and none remained on the earth except those against whom the punishment was due. And when He, glory be to Him, knew that those who were hostile to His Prophet Muḥammad ﷺ could not be hoped to succeed, He commanded him to invoke against them, yet He taught him how to invoke against them in a manner that would not repel others. So He wished to say: "Say: My Lord, destroy the wrongdoers", but He turned from this specific wording, because of the repulsion in it, to the wording of consequence (irdāf), and said: «قل رب احكم بالحق». For when He judges with the truth, which is justice, He punishes whoever deserves punishment. As for the saying of the one raising the difficulty — "Why was the more concise abandoned for the longer? Had he said 'My Lord, judge', it would have sufficed" — the matter is not as he claims, because the free-choosing judge, who has no partner, may judge with grace, thereby yielding his own right, and he may judge with justice, thereby fulfilling his right and the right of others; and asking for judgement in general does not fulfil this. For this reason the more concise was abandoned for the longer, so as to fulfil the intended meaning.
Fourteen kinds of the badīʿ have been distilled from this answer, which coincide in these three words, and they are:
1- Al-irdāf (consequence), which we mentioned above.
2- Al-īḍāḥ (clarification), because the clarification of the difficulty arising from the apparent wording came embedded within the irdāf.
3- Al-tatmīm (completion), for had it been limited to the saying "My Lord, judge", the intended meaning would have been deficient, because mere judgement does not fulfil the aim, as we have shown.
4- Al-muqārana (conjunction), because the idmāj (embedding) and the īḍāḥ were joined in the tatmīm.
5 and 6- Al-iftinān (diversification), because these three words combine two of the arts that speakers aim at, and they are:
a- The art of courtesy (adab), in the Real, glory be to Him, teaching His Prophet ﷺ how to invoke against those who oppose him in a manner that does not repel others from him.
b- The art of satire (hijāʾ), because the justice of Allah, glory be to Him, does not allow Him to command His Prophet to invoke except against those whom He knew to be determined upon disobedience and clear of faith; and whoever is such deserves blame. So He embedded, in commanding the Messenger to invoke against them, their satirising, by virtue of what the speech implies of their deserving reproach.
7- Al-ījāz (concision) of the intended meaning in the fewest possible letters.
8- Al-suhūla (ease), for the words are composed soundly, free of ill neighbourliness, with easy points of articulation, and because the words come in their proper places, no word is advanced ahead of another or delayed behind it.
9- Al-tahdhīb (refinement), in that the composition of the sentence is set in the soundest order and easiest refinement, since the one invoked is mentioned first, the request second, and the thing requested third.
10- Ḥusn al-bayān (beauty of exposition), because the mind races to understand the meaning of the speech without pausing, merely on hearing it the first time, owing to the absence of complexity in the wording and its freedom from the causes of obscurity — such as fronting and delaying, taking the more roundabout route, and using a homonym.
11- Al-tamzīj (blending), because of the blending of the arts with the meanings of the badīʿ; for the two arts of courtesy and satire blended with the meaning of irdāf and tatmīm, and in the wording only one form appeared for each pair of meanings: the art of courtesy appeared and the art of satire was embedded in it, and the irdāf appeared and the tatmīm was embedded in it.
12- Al-ibdāʿ (innovation), because each word in the sentence contains one kind or two or more of the badīʿ.
13- Al-tamthīl (proverb-making), because the strength of the eloquence and the lustre of the fluency brought these words out in the form of a current proverb, fit to be cited in every event resembling its event.
14- Al-tawlīd, because when the irdāf was paired with the tatmīm, the īḍāḥ was generated from them, and from the īḍāḥ and the irdāf the idmāj was generated; and when the benefit of bringing the preposition and its genitive noun became apparent, and the tatmīm was established, and the reason for turning away from the specific wording of supplication to the wording of irdāf became clear, there was generated from that the art of courtesy, and from the art of courtesy the art of satire; and when harmony and refinement were established, together with the fine arrangement that occurred in the composition, the current proverb was generated from that. For this reason tawlīd prevailed over all the thirteen kinds in it, and it was placed in its own chapter rather than in theirs.

Tawlīd in poetry:
In poetry, only tawlīd of meanings is admired. As for tawlīd of words, it comes below it in rank, and some have even gone so far as to deem it unacceptable because of its resemblance to plagiarism. This is when a poet finds a word of another's poetry pleasing, takes it and loads it with a meaning other than its first meaning, such as the saying of Abū Tammām:
لها منظر قيد الأوابد لم يزل ... يروح ويغدو في خفارته الحب
(She has an appearance that is a fetter of the wild creatures; love has never ceased to come and go under her protection.)
He took the phrase قيد الأوابد ("fetter of the wild creatures") from the verse of Imruʾ al-Qays in describing a horse and moved it to love poetry. The verse of Imruʾ al-Qays is:
وقد اغتدي والطير في وكناتها ... بمنجرد قيد الأوابد هيكل
(I set out early, while the birds were still in their nests, on a sleek-coated, huge-framed horse, a fetter of the wild creatures.)
though it may be pleasing, as ʿAlī ibn Zurayq al-Baghdādī did in his saying:
استودع الله في بغداد لي قمرا ... بالكرخ من فلك الأزرار مطلعه
(I entrust to Allah a moon of mine in Baghdad; in al-Karkh, from the sphere of buttons, is its rising-place.)
He took «al-azrār» (buttons) from the saying of ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Muʿtazz:
يا حسن أحمد إذ بدا متشمرا ... في قرطق يسعى بكأس عقاره
والغصن في أثوابه والدر في ... فمه وجيد الظبي في أزراره
(How fair is Aḥmad when he appeared, girded up, in a short tunic, going about with a cup of his wine; a branch in his garments, pearls in his mouth, and the neck of a gazelle in his buttons.)
They also faulted ʿUmāra al-Yamanī for his verse praising the Fatimid Egyptian caliph on his arrival to him from Yemen, which is:
فهل درى البيت أني بعد فرقته ... ماسرت من حرم إلا إلى حرم
(Did the House know that, since parting from it, I have travelled from no sanctuary except to a sanctuary?)
because it is taken word for word from the poetry of Abū Tammām in praise:
يا من رأى حرما يسري إلى حرم ... طوبى لمستلم يأتي وملتزم
(O you who have seen a sanctuary travelling to a sanctuary: blessed is he who touches [the Stone] and comes, and who clings [to the Multazam].)
Here the critic is bewildered by how often great poets fall into these slips. Ibn al-Athīr said: «Among what I used to admire of the poetry of Abū Nuwās is his saying from his ode that begins:
دع عنك لومي فإن اللوم إغراء ... وداوني بالتي كانت هي الداء
(Leave off blaming me, for blame is incitement; and cure me with that which was itself the disease.)
دارت على فتية ذل الزمان لهم ... فما يصيبهم إلا بما شاءوا
(It [the cup] went round among youths to whom time submitted; it strikes them only with what they wish.)
and this is of lofty poetry. Then I came upon this verse in the Kitāb al-Aghānī of Abū l-Faraj, among the songs of Maʿbad, and it is:
لهفي على فتية ذل الزمان لهم ... فما أصابهم إلا بما شاءوا
(Alas for youths to whom time submitted; it afflicted them only with what they wished.)
and I do not know how this is.»
As for tawlīd of meanings, it is admirable without qualification, as in the saying of Abū l-Ṭayyib al-Mutanabbī:
همام إذا ما فارق الغمد سيفه ... وعاينته لم تدر أيهما النصل
(A chieftain: when his sword leaves its sheath and you look at him, you cannot tell which of the two is the blade.)
He took it from the saying of Abū Tammām:
يمدون بالبيض القواطع أيديا ... فهن سواء والسيوف القواطع
(They stretch out hands with the cutting white swords; the hands and the cutting swords are alike.)
al-Mutanabbī also said:
وما هي إلا لحظة بعد لحظة ... إذا نزلت في قلبه رحل العقل
(It is but a glance after a glance; when it settles in his heart, reason departs.)
He took it from the saying of Abū Nuwās in describing wine:
إذا ما أتت دون اللهاة من الفتى ... دعا همه من صدره برحيل
(When it reaches below the uvula of the youth, it calls his worry to depart from his breast.)
It is fine how al-Mutanabbī took from Abū Tammām his saying:
ومن الخير بطء سيبك عني ... أسرع السحب في المسير الجهام
(Part of the good is the slowness of your bounty to me; the swiftest clouds in their course are the rainless ones.)
and the verse of Abū Tammām:
هو الصنع إن تعجل فخير وإن ترث ... فللريث في بعض المواضع أنفع
(It is a favour: if you hasten, that is good, and if you delay, then delay in some places is more beneficial.)
while the verse of al-Mutanabbī is more beautiful and more elegant, and in it is the added feature of proverb-making.
One of the later poets generated a Persian verse and said:
كأن عذاره في الخد لام ... ومبسمه الشهيّ العذب صاد
وطرة شعره ليل بهيم ... فلا عجب إذا سرق الرقاد
(As though the down on his cheek were a lām, and his sweet, delicious smile a ṣād; and the fringe of his hair a pitch-black night — so no wonder if sleep is stolen.)
This poet generated, from the likening of the down to a lām and the mouth to a ṣād, the word «liṣṣ» (thief), and generated from its meaning and from the meaning of likening the forelock to night the mention of stealing the stars. So the verse achieved tawlīd, novelty (ighrāb) and embedding (idmāj).
We have given free rein to the discussion, but what is beautiful is never wearisome.

* Benefits:
Suspension (al-taʿlīq):
The verbs that govern two objects, whose origin is a mubtadaʾ and a khabar, have many rulings, among them suspension, which is the nullification of the operation in wording but not in position, because there follows something that has the right to the beginning of the sentence. The suspending elements (al-muʿallaqāt) are:
1- The lām of commencement (lām al-ibtidāʾ), as in «لَقَدْ عَلِمُوا لَمَنِ اشْتَراهُ ما لَهُ فِي الْآخِرَةِ مِنْ خَلاقٍ». Here مَنِ is a mubtadaʾ, a relative noun; the clause اشْتَراهُ is the ṣila of مَنِ, and its returning pronoun is the latent agent of اشْتَراهُ; ما is negative; لَهُ and فِي are attached to the existence that is the khabar of خَلاقٍ; مِنْ is redundant; and the clause ماله في الآخرة من خلاق is the khabar of مَنِ, the link between them being the pronoun governed by the lām. The clause of مَنِ and its khabar is in the position of the accusative, the operating verb being suspended from it by the lām of commencement, because it has the right to the beginning of the sentence, so no operator passes over it. It is passed over only in the chapter of inna, where the khabar is made nominative, because it is delayed from a fronted position in order to improve the wording, its origin being to precede inna.
2- The lām of oath (lām al-qasam), as in the verse of Labīd:
ولقد علمت لتأتين منيتي ... إن المنايا لا تطيش سهامها
(I have indeed known that my death will surely come; the deaths' arrows never miss.)
The lām in لتأتين is the lām of oath and is called the answer of the oath. The oath and its answer are in the position of the accusative, the operating verb being suspended from it by the lām of oath — not only the answer clause. So what has been said falls away, that the oath-answer clause has no position, while the clause from which the operator is suspended has a position, and so the two are incompatible. For this reason Abū Ḥayyān said: «Most of our fellow grammarians do not mention the lām of oath among the suspending elements, and in al-ʿIzza [?]: the lām of oath does not suspend, as in:
لقد علمت أسد أننا ... لهم يوم نصر لنعم النصير
(Asad have indeed known that we, on a day of victory, are for them an excellent helper)
with the fatḥa on anna; this is the lām of oath and it has not suspended; and you say 'I knew that Zayd will surely stand', with the fatḥa on anna.»» End of quotation. [Translator's note: the words «وفي العزة» appear in the source in this form and their sense is unclear; they are translated literally.] And in al-Mughnī: «Verbs of the heart, because they convey certainty, are answered with what an oath is answered with, as in his saying: ولقد علمت لتأتين منيتي etc.»» End of quotation. So he took the lām of لتأتين out of being a lām of oath.
3- The negative mā, as in «لقد علمت ما هؤلاء ينطقون»: here mā is negative, هؤلاء is a mubtadaʾ, and the clause ينطقون is its khabar; the nominal clause is in the position of the accusative with علمت, and the operator is suspended from it in wording by the negative mā.
4- The negative lā and in, occurring in the answer to an oath, either uttered or implied. The uttered, as in "I knew, by Allah, lā Zayd is in the house and lā ʿAmr" and "I knew, by Allah, in Zayd is in the house"; the implied, as in "I knew lā Zayd is in the house and lā ʿAmr".
5- The interrogative, like the verse we are dealing with, «وإن أدري أقريب إلخ», and the saying of Kuthayyir:
وما كنت أدري قبل عزة ما البكا ... ولا موجعات القلب حتى تولت
(Before ʿAzza I did not know what weeping is, nor the heart's sorrows, until she turned away.)
Here موجعات is conjoined in the accusative, with the kasra [on the plural] as its sign, to the position of his saying ما البكا, from which his saying أدري was suspended.

dervis-irab:89-93.t:
* Vocabulary:
(زَكَرِيَّا): with a long final vowel (madd), the name of a prophet; its alif is the feminine alif, and for that reason it is a diptote (mamnūʿ min al-ṣarf); it is also a diptote because of being foreign and a proper name. It was also said that it is Arabic, derived from zakara, meaning "it was full" or "it was crammed".

* I'rab:
(وَزَكَرِيَّا إِذْ نادى رَبَّهُ رَبِّ لا تَذَرْنِي فَرْداً وَأَنْتَ خَيْرُ الْوارِثِينَ) The parsing of «وزكريا إذ نادى ربه» has already been given. «ورب» is the one addressed (munādā), annexed to the omitted first-person yāʾ; «ولا» is a prohibitive lā used for supplication; «وتذرني» is an imperfect verb made jussive by «لا»; the nūn is the protective nūn (nūn al-wiqāya); the agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "you (anta)"; the yāʾ is the direct object; «وفردا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial). «وأنت»: the wāw is a conjunction on an omitted element, i.e. "so grant me an heir, and You..."; «وأنت» is the mubtadaʾ and «وخير الوارثين» is the khabar.
(فَاسْتَجَبْنا لَهُ وَوَهَبْنا لَهُ يَحْيى وَأَصْلَحْنا لَهُ زَوْجَهُ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; «واستجبنا»: verb and agent; «وله» is attached to «استجبنا»; the object is omitted, i.e. "his call". «وأصلحنا»: verb and agent; «وله» is attached to «أصلحنا»; «وزوجه» is the direct object.
