What is meant by making her right is that We made her fit for childbearing after her barrenness and sterility; sterility (ʿuqm) is the blocking of the womb, as in al-Mukhtār.
(إِنَّهُمْ كانُوا يُسارِعُونَ فِي الْخَيْراتِ) The clause gives the reason for the making right. «إن» and its noun; the clause «كانوا» is its khabar; kāna and its noun; the clause «يسارعون في الخيرات» is the khabar of kāna. [Translator's note: the source text reads «وجملة كانوا كانوا خبرها», with «كانوا» repeated; the repetition is evidently a slip.] He used «في» rather than «إلى» to signal their constancy in hastening, as though they were settled in it.
(وَيَدْعُونَنا رَغَباً وَرَهَباً وَكانُوا لَنا خاشِعِينَ) «ويدعوننا» is conjoined to «يسارعون»; «ويدعوننا»: verb, agent and direct object; «ورغبا ورهبا» are two maṣdars (verbal nouns) made accusative as ḥāl, or as maṣdars meeting their governing verb in meaning but not in form, or as objects of purpose; «وكانوا»: kāna and its noun; «وخاشعين» is its khabar; «ولنا» is attached to «خاشعين».
(وَالَّتِي أَحْصَنَتْ فَرْجَها فَنَفَخْنا فِيها مِنْ رُوحِنا وَجَعَلْناها وَابْنَها آيَةً لِلْعالَمِينَ) «والتي», i.e. "and remember Maryam, who ..."; the clause «أحصنت فرجها» is the ṣila (relative clause). «فنفخنا» is conjoined to «أحصنت»; «وفيها» is attached to «نفخنا»; «ومن روحنا» is also attached to «نفخنا». You may also parse «التي» as a mubtadaʾ with an omitted khabar, i.e. "(is mentioned) in what is recited to them". «وجعلناها»: verb, agent and direct object; «وابنها» is conjoined to the hāʾ, or is an object of accompaniment; «وآية» is the second direct object. It does not agree with the first object (so as to be dual) because each of Maryam and her son is a sign by being joined to the other, so they became one sign; or you may say that it was omitted from one because the other indicates it, i.e. "We made Maryam a sign and her son likewise", or the reverse. «وللعالمين» is an adjective (naʿt) of «آية».
(إِنَّ هذِهِ أُمَّتُكُمْ أُمَّةً واحِدَةً وَأَنَا رَبُّكُمْ فَاعْبُدُونِ) «إن», its noun and its khabar; «وأمة» is a necessary ḥāl; it was also said to be a badal from «هذه»; «وواحدة» is an adjective. «وأنا»: the wāw is a conjunction; «وأنا» is the mubtadaʾ and «وربكم» the khabar; the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (eloquent fāʾ); «واعبدوني»: imperative verb and agent; the first-person yāʾ, omitted in keeping with the orthography of the muṣḥaf, is the direct object.
(وَتَقَطَّعُوا أَمْرَهُمْ بَيْنَهُمْ كُلٌّ إِلَيْنا راجِعُونَ) The wāw is a conjunction; «وتقطعوا» is a past verb with its agent; the original is «وتقطعتم», except that the speech was turned to the third person in the manner of iltifāt (turning), as will come in the section on Rhetoric. As for «وأمرهم», there are several views on its being accusative, the preferable of which is that it is accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. "they became divided in their affair". It is also possible that «تقطعوا» means "they cut up", in which case «أمرهم» is a direct object. Abū al-Baqāʾ held that it is a tamyīz (specification), and I do not know how that holds up with him.

* Rhetoric:
1- Iltifāt: in His saying «إِنَّ هذِهِ أُمَّتُكُمْ أُمَّةً واحِدَةً وَأَنَا رَبُّكُمْ فَاعْبُدُونِ، وَتَقَطَّعُوا أَمْرَهُمْ بَيْنَهُمْ كُلٌّ إِلَيْنا راجِعُونَ» there is iltifāt. The original of «تقطعوا» is «تقطعتم», following the first part, except that the speech was turned from address to the third person in the manner of iltifāt, as though He were lamenting what they had corrupted and making ugly in their eyes what they had done, saying to them: "Do you not see the enormity of what these people committed in the religion of Allah? They made the matter of their religion pieces among themselves." That is a figurative representation (tamthīl) of their disagreement in it and their dissension. Then He threatened them after that, that these differing groups return to Him, and He will requite them for what they did.
2- The meaning of blowing in Maryam: The apparent sense of the speech suggests that Maryam is the one who was given life, because the meaning of blowing is giving life; but Allah the Exalted treated the blowing of the spirit into ʿĪsā, because he was in Maryam's womb, as the blowing of the spirit into Maryam. Similar to that is a piper saying: "I blew in the house of so-and-so", meaning: I blew the pipe in his house.

dervis-irab:56-61.t:
* Vocabulary:
(جُذاذاً): In al-Qāmūs: al-judhādh, with the jīm taking three vowels, is what is broken off from a thing, and its verb is jadha yajidhdhu, of the pattern naṣara. The characteristics of the co-occurrence of jīm and dhāl as the fāʾ and ʿayn of a word have already been mentioned.

* I'rab:
(قالَ: بَلْ رَبُّكُمْ رَبُّ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ الَّذِي فَطَرَهُنَّ وَأَنَا عَلى ذلِكُمْ مِنَ الشَّاهِدِينَ): bal is a particle of retraction; rabbukum is a mubtadaʾ and rabbu al-samāwāti wa-al-arḍi is the khabar; alladhī is an adjective of rabb and the clause faṭarahunna is the ṣila; the pronoun refers to the heavens and the earth or to the statues, and al-Zamakhsharī preferred the second as being "more telling in showing their error and firmer in arguing against them". That is also indicated by His saying «وَأَنَا عَلى ذلِكُمْ مِنَ الشَّاهِدِينَ», as if he had said: "and I shall make that clear to you and prove it". Wa-anā is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is min al-shāhidīna, and ʿalā dhālikum, the two are attached to al-shāhidīna. (وَتَاللَّهِ لَأَكِيدَنَّ أَصْنامَكُمْ بَعْدَ أَنْ تُوَلُّوا مُدْبِرِينَ): this is the start of confirming the practical way, or the practical proof as it is said. The wāw is a conjunction, the tāʾ is the tāʾ of the oath, and an important discussion of the prepositional particles of the oath will come in the chapter on Benefits; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being "uqsimu"; the lām is the response to the oath; la-akīdanna is an imperfect verb indeclinable on fatḥa because emphasis with the heavy nūn is obligatory, and its agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "anā"; aṣnāmakum is the direct object; baʿda is an adverb attached to akīdanna; an and what is in its scope are an interpreted maṣdar annexed to the adverb; and mudbirīna is a ḥāl, that is, "you return to your gatherings". (فَجَعَلَهُمْ جُذاذاً إِلَّا كَبِيراً لَهُمْ لَعَلَّهُمْ إِلَيْهِ يَرْجِعُونَ): the fāʾ is conjoined to an omitted element, its implied form being: they turned away and returned to their gatherings, and Ibrāhīm went with them; when he was part way along the road he threw himself down and said "I am sick", complaining of his foot, so they left him and went on. Ibrāhīm returned to the house of the idols; opposite the door was a great idol, and beside it one smaller than it, and so on in succession. Ibrāhīm said to them: "Will you not eat?" and none uttered a word, so he fell upon them, smashing, and made them... The whole story is narrated in al-Khāzin and elsewhere.
Wa-jaʿalahum is a verb, a latent agent and a first direct object; judhādhan is a second direct object; illā is a particle of exception because the speech is complete and affirmative; and kabīran is excepted from the hāʾ, that is, he did not break it and left it, to perfect the point and complete the mockery of them. Laʿalla and its noun; ilayhi, the two are attached to yarjiʿūna, and the clause yarjiʿūna is the khabar of laʿalla; in this there is mockery indeed.
(قالُوا مَنْ فَعَلَ هذا بِآلِهَتِنا إِنَّهُ لَمِنَ الظَّالِمِينَ): qālū is a verb and agent; man is an interrogative noun intended for denial, a mubtadaʾ, and the clause faʿala is the khabar; hādhā is the object of faʿala; bi-ālihatinā, the two are attached to faʿala; they did not point to them with "hā'ulāʾi" though they were before them, because of putting the overt noun in the place of the pronoun, the discussion of which has preceded. The clause innahu la-min al-ẓālimīna is resumptive, introduced to affirm what preceded and confirm their rejection of what had happened; inna and its noun, the shifted lām, and min al-ẓālimīna are the khabar of both [inna and its noun]. [Translator's note: the source says "خبران" (two khabars); the sense is that min al-ẓālimīna is the khabar of inna, with the lām attached to it.] (قالُوا سَمِعْنا فَتًى يَذْكُرُهُمْ يُقالُ لَهُ إِبْراهِيمُ): the clause samiʿnā is the content of the saying; fatan is the object of samiʿnā; the clause yadhkuruhum is a second direct object; the special feature of the verb samiʿa will come in the chapter on Benefits; the clause yuqālu is an adjective of fatan; lahu, the two are attached to yuqālu; and Ibrāhīmu: there are several grounds for its nominative case, of equal preference. First, it is a nāʾib fāʿil of yuqālu, i.e. "this word is said of him"; al-Zamakhsharī said: and this is the sound one, because what is meant is the name, not the one named. Second, it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "he is Ibrāhīm" or "this is Ibrāhīm". Third, it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, i.e. "Ibrāhīm is the one who did that". Fourth, it is a vocative whose particle is omitted, i.e. "yā Ibrāhīmu". (قالُوا فَأْتُوا بِهِ عَلى أَعْيُنِ النَّاسِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَشْهَدُونَ): fa-ʾtū: the fāʾ is the fāʾ faṣīḥa; ʾtū is an imperative verb indeclinable by the omission of the nūn, and the wāw is the agent; bihi, the two are attached to His saying «فأتوا»; and ʿalā aʿyuni al-nāsi is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from the pronoun governed by the bāʾ, i.e. "bring him while he is seen and witnessed". The secret of istiʿlāʾ (the use of "on") in this expression will come. Laʿallahum: laʿalla and its noun, and the clause yashhadūna is its khabar, that is, "they will testify against him that he is the doer".

* Benefits:
In these verses there are many benefits, of which we cite the most important as follows:

1- The particles of the oath:
The original particles of the oath are the bāʾ, with the wāw being a substitute for it. We say that because it is the preposition by which the verb of swearing is connected to the one sworn by, and that verb is aḥlifu or uqsimu or the like; but since the verb is intransitive, they linked it with the transitivizing bāʾ, so it became aḥlifu billāh or uqsimu billāh. Allah the Exalted said: «وَأَقْسَمُوا بِاللَّهِ جَهْدَ أَيْمانِهِمْ» and the poet said:
أقسم بالله وآلائه ... والمرء عما قال مسئول
(I swear by Allah and His bounties; and a man is accountable for what he said)
And Zuhayr ibn Abī Sulmā said:
فأقست بالبيت الذي طاف حوله ... رجال بنوه من قريش وجرهم
(I swore by the House around which circled men who built it, of Quraysh and Jurhum)
[Translator's note: the source reads «فأقست»; presumably «فأقسمت».]
They singled out the bāʾ for that, rather than other prepositions, for several reasons:
(a) It is permissible to mention the verb of swearing with it, as you saw in the preceding examples, and that is not permissible with the wāw and the tāʾ, so you do not say "uqsimu wallāh" nor "uqsimu tallāh".
(b) It is permissible for it to enter on a pronoun, unlike the other particles; you say "bika la-afʿalanna", and do not say "taka" or "waka"; and it is known that the pronoun returns a thing to its origin.
(c) Its use in the entreating oath (al-qasam al-istiʿṭāfī): the oath is a performative sentence intended to confirm another sentence; if that other sentence is also performative, then that is the entreating oath, such as "billāhi hal qāma Zaydun?", i.e. "I ask you by Allah, adjuring you". An example of the entreating oath with the bāʾ is the saying of al-Majnūn:
بربك هل ضممت إليك ليلى ... قبيل الصبح أو قبلت فاها
(By your Lord, did you embrace Laylā shortly before dawn, or kiss her mouth?)
(d) The bāʾ, unlike the wāw and the tāʾ, is distinguished by occurring for things other than the oath, which is obvious.
Since this became frequent in swearing, they preferred lightness and omitted the verb from the wording, while it remained intended so that the preposition would be attached to it; then they substituted the wāw for the bāʾ as a broadening in the language, and because it is lighter, since the wāw is lighter than the bāʾ and its vowel lighter than the vowel of the bāʾ. They singled out the wāw for this for two reasons:
(a) It is from the same place of articulation as the bāʾ, that is, the lips.
(b) From the side of meaning: the bāʾ means attachment and the wāw means togetherness, and when a thing is attached to a thing, it has come along with it.
As for the tāʾ, it is a substitute for the wāw, because its substitution is frequent in words such as tukaʾa, turāth and tukhma, because of its resemblance in the breadth of its point of articulation; and it is among the whispered letters, so its whisper suits the softness of the letters of softness. Since the wāw is a substitute for the bāʾ, and a substitute falls below the rank of the original, it enters only on an overt noun and does not enter on a pronoun, due to the lowering of the branch below the rank of the origin, as it is of the second rank; and the tāʾ, since it is a substitute for the wāw and of the third rank, fell below the rank of the wāw, so it was specified for the name of Allah the Exalted because of the frequency of swearing by Him. It may carry the sense of wonder; Allah the Exalted said: «تَاللَّهِ تَفْتَؤُا تَذْكُرُ يُوسُفَ» by way of wonder, and like the verse before us, as though he marvelled at the ease of the stratagem at his hand and its becoming available, because that was a matter of despair or at least in doubt for its difficulty and hardness.

2- The characteristics of the verb samiʿa:
This verb has wonderful characteristics, namely that when it enters on what is not heard, it takes two objects, as in the noble verse: the first object is fatan and the second is yadhkuruhum; unlike when it enters on what is heard, for instance if you say "samiʿtu kalāma Zaydin", in which case it takes one object.

3- The meaning of istiʿlāʾ:
The meaning of istiʿlāʾ is height, so the sīn and tāʾ are for height, not for request. Istiʿlāʾ is of two kinds: real, such as «وَعَلَيْها وَعَلَى الْفُلْكِ تُحْمَلُونَ» [Translator's note: the source text is garbled here, reading «نحوَلَيْها وَعَلَى الْفُلْكِ تُحْمَلُونَ» with the opening of the quotation missing]; and figurative, such as «أُولئِكَ عَلى هُدىً مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ» and «وَإِنَّكَ لَعَلى خُلُقٍ عَظِيمٍ», where mastery of guidance and of great, noble character, and steadfastness in them, is likened to one on a mount that he steers as he wishes. Likewise their saying "ʿalayhi dayn" (he has a debt upon him), as if something had risen above him; and as in His saying «عَلى أَعْيُنِ النَّاسِ», that is, his coming is established in the eyes and takes hold of them, as a rider is firm on the ridden animal and in possession of it.

dervis-irab:62-70.t:
* I'rab:
(قالُوا: أَأَنْتَ فَعَلْتَ هذا بِآلِهَتِنا يا إِبْراهِيمُ؟): the hamza is for a question; anta is a mubtadaʾ and the clause faʿalta is its khabar; hādhā is the direct object; bi-ālihatinā, the two are attached to faʿalta; yā is a vocative particle and Ibrāhīmu is a vocative, a singular proper noun indeclinable on ḍamma in the position of accusative. (قالَ: بَلْ فَعَلَهُ كَبِيرُهُمْ هذا فَسْئَلُوهُمْ إِنْ كانُوا يَنْطِقُونَ): bal is a particle of retraction; faʿalahu kabīruhum is a verb, direct object and postponed agent; hādhā is an adjective of kabīruhum or a badal from it; the fāʾ is the fāʾ faṣīḥa; isʾalūhum is an imperative verb, agent and direct object; in is conditional; kānū is a defective past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis, and the wāw is its noun and the clause yanṭiqūna is its khabar; the apodosis is omitted, indicated by what precedes, i.e. "fa-isʾalūhum". (فَرَجَعُوا إِلى أَنْفُسِهِمْ فَقالُوا إِنَّكُمْ أَنْتُمُ الظَّالِمُونَ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; rajaʿū is a past verb and agent; ilā anfusihim, the two are attached to rajaʿū; fa-qālū is conjoined to fa-rajaʿū; innakum is inna and its noun, and the clause antum al-ẓālimūna is its khabar; you may make antum a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl) and al-ẓālimūna the khabar of inna. (ثُمَّ نُكِسُوا عَلى رُؤُسِهِمْ لَقَدْ عَلِمْتَ ما هؤُلاءِ يَنْطِقُونَ)
thumma is a conjunction of delay; the meaning of tankīs will come in the chapter on Rhetoric; nukisū is a verb and nāʾib fāʿil; ʿalā ruʾūsihim is a ḥāl, i.e. "being upon their heads", and you may attach it to the verb itself. The meaning of tankīs is reversal; one says nakasa raʾsahu and nakkasahu, lightened or doubled, i.e. he lowered it until its top became its bottom. The lām is the response to an omitted oath, qad is a particle of verification, and ʿalimta is a verb and agent, the address being to Ibrāhīm, and the clause is the object of an omitted saying in the position of ḥāl; mā is a Ḥijāzī negative, hā'ulāʾi is its noun and the clause yanṭiqūna is its khabar. The clause mā hā'ulāʾi yanṭiqūna is in the position of the two objects of ʿalimta, or the position of a single object if ʿalimta means ʿarafta. (قالَ: أَفَتَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ ما لا يَنْفَعُكُمْ شَيْئاً وَلا يَضُرُّكُمْ): the hamza is for a question of denial and the fāʾ is conjoined to an omitted element; taʿbudūna is a nominative imperfect verb and the wāw is the agent; min dūni Allāhi is a ḥāl; mā is the direct object and the clause lā yanfaʿukum is the ṣila; shayʾan is a mafʿūl muṭlaq; wa-lā yaḍurrukum is conjoined to «لا ينفعكم». (أُفٍّ لَكُمْ وَلِما تَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ أَفَلا تَعْقِلُونَ): uffin is an imperfect-tense verbal noun (ism fiʿl), the dialects of which have already been mentioned, and its meaning is "I am vexed"; lakum, the two are attached to an omitted ḥāl, since the lām is for explaining the one expressing vexation; wa-li-mā taʿbudūna is conjoined to lakum, and the clause taʿbudūna is the ṣila; min dūni Allāhi is a ḥāl. A-fa-lā: the hamza is for a question of denial, the fāʾ is conjoined to an omitted element, lā is negative, taʿqilūna is an imperfect verb and the wāw is the agent. (قالُوا: حَرِّقُوهُ وَانْصُرُوا آلِهَتَكُمْ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ فاعِلِينَ): ḥarriqūhu is an imperative verb, agent and direct object, and the clause is the content of the saying; unṣurū is an imperative verb and agent, ālihatakum is the direct object; in is conditional and kuntum is the protasis, the tāʾ being the noun of kāna and fāʿilīna its khabar; the apodosis of in is omitted, indicated by what precedes, i.e. "fa-ḥarriqūhu wa-unṣurū ālihatakum". (قُلْنا يا نارُ كُونِي بَرْداً وَسَلاماً عَلى إِبْراهِيمَ): omitted clauses must be implied, i.e. they resolved on burning him, so they collected much firewood, kindled the fire, bound Ibrāhīm, put him in a catapult and threw him into the fire. Qulnā is a verb and agent; yā is a vocative particle and nāru is an indefinite specific vocative indeclinable on ḍamma in the position of accusative; kūnī is a defective imperative verb, the yāʾ its noun and bardan its khabar; salāman is conjoined to bardan; and ʿalā Ibrāhīma is an adjective of salāman. (وَأَرادُوا بِهِ كَيْداً فَجَعَلْناهُمُ الْأَخْسَرِينَ): the wāw is a conjunction; arādū is a past verb and agent; bihi, the two are attached to arādū; kaydan is the direct object; fa-jaʿalnāhum: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and jaʿalnāhum is conjoined to arādū, and al-akhsarīna is a second direct object.

* Rhetoric:
1- Tajāhul al-ʿārif (feigned ignorance): In His saying: «أَأَنْتَ فَعَلْتَ هذا بِآلِهَتِنا يا إِبْراهِيمُ» is a delightful art of theirs called tajāhul al-ʿārif, which is the speaker's asking about what he truly knows, feigning ignorance, so that the speech comes out in the manner of praise or censure, or to indicate the intensity of passion in love, or with the aim of wonder, reproach or affirmation. It is of two kinds, positive and negative, and the verse before us is of the positive feigned ignorance running in the manner of affirmation.
2- Taʿrīḍ (allusion): In His saying «فَسْئَلُوهُمْ إِنْ كانُوا يَنْطِقُونَ» is the art of taʿrīḍ, to which reference has been made more than once. He, upon him be peace, wished to show them that whoever does not speak and does not know is not deserving of worship, and that it is not sound in reason to call him a god. So he brought the speech out as an allusion to them, leading them to admit that the inanimate things they worshipped are not gods; for if they said "they do not speak", he would say to them: "Then how do you worship what is unable to speak and falls short of knowing what happens in the place where it is?" This speech is a supposition of falsehood with the opponent until the proof binds him and he admits the truth, for that is more decisive against his doubt and more repelling of his obstinacy.

dervis-irab:71-75.t:
* I'rab:
(وَنَجَّيْناهُ وَلُوطاً إِلَى الْأَرْضِ الَّتِي بارَكْنا فِيها لِلْعالَمِينَ): the wāw is a conjunction; najjaynāhu is a verb, agent and direct object; Lūṭan is conjoined to the hāʾ or is a mafʿūl maʿahu, the wāw being the wāw of accompaniment, and he was his brother's son, so We moved him from the land of Nimrūd in Iraq. Ilā al-arḍi, the two are attached to najjaynāhu or to an omitted ḥāl; allatī is an adjective of al-arḍ, and the clause bārakna fīhā lil-ʿālamīna is the ṣila; fīhā is a ḥāl and lil-ʿālamīna, the two are attached to bārakna. It is the villages of Bayt al-Maqdis in Palestine, and an important discussion of Filasṭīn as a word will come in the chapter on Benefits.
(وَوَهَبْنا لَهُ إِسْحاقَ وَيَعْقُوبَ نافِلَةً وَكُلًّا جَعَلْنا صالِحِينَ): the wāw is a conjunction; wahabnā is a verb and agent; lahu, the two are attached to wahabnā; Isḥāq is the direct object and Yaʿqūb is conjoined to Isḥāq; nāfilatan is a ḥāl from Yaʿqūb, i.e. Yaʿqūb was given as an addition without being asked; and if you take nāfila to mean "gift", then its accusative is as a mafʿūl muṭlaq from the meaning of the governor, which is wahabnā, since the gift (hiba) and the grant (ʿaṭiyya) are close in meaning. Kullan is the first object of jaʿalnā, put forward; jaʿalnā is a verb and agent; ṣāliḥīna is the second direct object. (وَجَعَلْناهُمْ أَئِمَّةً يَهْدُونَ بِأَمْرِنا): wa-jaʿalnāhum is a verb, agent and direct object; a'immatan is a second direct object; the clause yahdūna bi-amrinā is an adjective of a'imma, and bi-amrinā is a ḥāl, i.e. "they guide to Our religion, bearing Our command". (وَأَوْحَيْنا إِلَيْهِمْ فِعْلَ الْخَيْراتِ وَإِقامَ الصَّلاةِ وَإِيتاءَ الزَّكاةِ وَكانُوا لَنا عابِدِينَ): wa-awḥaynā is conjoined to what preceded; ilayhim, the two are attached to awḥaynā; fiʿla al-khayrāti is the direct object; iqāma al-ṣalāti is conjoined to fiʿla al-khayrāti, and likewise ītāʾa al-zakāti; wa-kānū: the wāw is a conjunction, kānū is kāna and its noun, and ʿābidīna is its khabar; lanā, the two are attached to ʿābidīna. (وَلُوطاً آتَيْناهُ حُكْماً وَعِلْماً): Lūṭan is accusative by an omitted verb explained by what follows, i.e. "ātaynā Lūṭan", and so it is a case of ishtighāl; the clause ātaynāhu is explicative, with no grammatical position; ḥukman is a second object of ātaynāhu and ʿilman is conjoined to ḥukman.
(وَنَجَّيْناهُ مِنَ الْقَرْيَةِ الَّتِي كانَتْ تَعْمَلُ الْخَبائِثَ إِنَّهُمْ كانُوا قَوْمَ سَوْءٍ فاسِقِينَ): wa-najjaynāhu is a verb, agent and direct object; min al-qaryati, the two are attached to najjaynāhu; allatī is an adjective of al-qarya, the clause kānat is the ṣila, the noun of kānat is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "hiya", and the clause taʿmalu al-khabā'itha is the khabar of kānat; the clause innahum is causal with no grammatical position; inna and its noun, the clause kānū is its khabar, qawma is the khabar of kānū, sū'in is annexed to qawm, and fāsiqīna is an adjective of qawm. (وَأَدْخَلْناهُ فِي رَحْمَتِنا إِنَّهُ مِنَ الصَّالِحِينَ): fī raḥmatinā, the two are attached to adkhalnāhu; the clause innahu min al-ṣāliḥīna is causal; inna and its noun, and the preposition and its genitive noun are the khabar.

* Rhetoric:
In these verses there are two majāz (figurative usages). The first is in His saying «وَنَجَّيْناهُ مِنَ الْقَرْيَةِ الَّتِي كانَتْ تَعْمَلُ الْخَبائِثَ», and what is meant is its people, because they practised the khabāʾith, that is, the vile deeds, such as sodomy, shooting with pellet-bows, playing with birds and other things.
The second is in His saying «وَأَدْخَلْناهُ فِي رَحْمَتِنا», that is, in Our Paradise, because it is the place of mercy; so it is a majāz mursal whose relation is locality.

* Benefits:
1- Filasṭīn (Palestine):
Filasṭīn, with fatḥa or kasra on the fāʾ and with fatḥa on the lām only, is the villages of Bayt al-Maqdis. In al-Qāmūs: "Filasṭūn and Filasṭīn, and their fāʾ may take fatḥa: a district of Syria and a village in Iraq; you say it with wāw in the nominative and with yāʾ in the accusative and genitive, or the yāʾ is invariable in every case, and the relative adjective is Filasṭī." Moreover, in this kind, that is, what is called the sound masculine plural, it is permissible to be declined with the three vowels overt on the nūn when it is not foreign; and if it is foreign it is declined as a diptote, that is, it is not given tanwīn and is genitive with fatḥa, and it is also permissible for it to be declined like the sound masculine plural.

2- Iqām al-ṣalāt and ītāʾ al-zakāt:
(إِقامَ الصَّلاةِ وَإِيتاءَ الزَّكاةِ): the rule for the maṣdar of the quadriliteral verb on the pattern afʿala is that it comes on ifʿāl if its ʿayn is sound, such as akrama ikrāman and awjada ījādan; if its ʿayn is weak, such as aqāma, aʿāna and abāna, its maṣdar comes on ifāla, like iqāma, iʿāna and ibāna: the ʿayn of the maṣdar is omitted and the tāʾ of feminine gender compensates for it. The original is iqwām, iʿwān and ibyān; the vowel of the wāw and yāʾ, which is fatḥa, was moved to the silent letter before them, then they were dropped to avoid two silent letters meeting, and the tāʾ compensates for them. This tāʾ may be dropped from the maṣdar when it is annexed, as in His saying, Exalted is He: «وَإِقامَ الصَّلاةِ وَإِيتاءَ الزَّكاةِ». And of those whose lām is weak, such as aʿṭā, ahdā and awlā, the lām is turned into a hamza in the maṣdar, such as iʿṭāʾ, ihdāʾ and īlāʾ; the original is iʿṭāw, ihdāy and īlāy. In Sharḥ al-Qāmūs it says: "The Arabs hamzate the wāw and yāʾ when they come after an alif, because the hamza bears the vowel better than the two, and because they find stopping on the wāw heavy, and likewise the yāʾ, as in al-ridāʾ, whose origin is ridāy." Refer for this to the discussion of ibdāl in the larger grammar books.

dervis-irab:94-100.t:
* Vocabulary:
(كُفْرانَ): al-kufrān is a maṣdar (verbal noun) of al-kufr. He said in al-Qāmūs: "kafara yakfuru, of the pattern naṣara, kufran, kufran, kufūran and kufrānan, the opposite of believing; kafara bi-l-khāliq means he denied Him and rendered (belief) void; and kafara kufran, kufūran and kufrānan bi-niʿam Allāh means he rejected Allah's favours and pretended to forget them."
(حَدَبٍ): with two fatḥas, a raised piece of land; from it comes al-ḥadab in the back (hunchback); every rise or hillock is a ḥadba.
(يَنْسِلُونَ): they hasten; al-nasalān is taking steps close together while hurrying. In al-Miṣbāḥ: "nasala in his walking, nasalānan: he hurried, and its pattern is ḍaraba"; and in al-Qāmūs it is of the pattern ḍaraba and qatala.
(حَصَبُ جَهَنَّمَ): al-ḥaṣab is "that with which one is pelted", i.e. they will be thrown into the Fire; al-ḥaṣb is throwing. In al-Mukhtār: "al-ḥaṣab with two fatḥas is that with which the fire is pelted, that is, thrown; whatever you threw into the fire, you have 'ḥaṣabtu' the fire with it; its pattern is ḍaraba," and the same is in al-Qāmūs.

* I'rab:
(فَمَنْ يَعْمَلْ مِنَ الصَّالِحاتِ وَهُوَ مُؤْمِنٌ فَلا كُفْرانَ لِسَعْيِهِ وَإِنَّا لَهُ كاتِبُونَ) The fāʾ is resumptive; «ومن» is a jussive-governing conditional noun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ; «ويعمل» is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); «ومن الصالحات» is an adjective of an omitted direct object, i.e. "some deed of the righteous deeds"; the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); «وهو» is the mubtadaʾ and «ومؤمن» the khabar; the fāʾ is the linking fāʾ (rābiṭa); «ولا» is the lā of generic negation; «وكفران» is its noun and «ولسعيه» its khabar. The wāw is resumptive or circumstantial; «وان» and its noun, and «وكاتبون» is its khabar; «وله» is attached to «كاتبون».
(وَحَرامٌ عَلى قَرْيَةٍ أَهْلَكْناها أَنَّهُمْ لا يَرْجِعُونَ) The wāw is a conjunction, of the type that conjoins sentences, or resumptive. «وحرام» is a fronted khabar; «وعلى قرية» is attached to «حرام»; the clause «أهلكناها» is an adjective of «قرية»; «وان» and what is within its scope is a postponed mubtadaʾ: «إن» and its noun, and the clause «لا يرجعون» its khabar. It was said that «لا» is redundant (zāʾida), which is the view of Abū ʿUbayda, like His saying «ما منعك أن لا تسجد», meaning "that they return to faith". The sense is: it is impossible for the people of a town whose destruction We have decreed because of their unbelief, that they return in the world to faith before the Resurrection arises; then they return. It is also valid that it is a negative in its usual sense, the implied meaning being "because they do not return". Al-Zajjāj said: «وحرام على قرية أهلكناها» means We have decreed the destruction of the town, so that We do not accept their deeds, because they will not return, i.e. they will not repent. What indicates this meaning is His saying before it «فَلا كُفْرانَ لِسَعْيِهِ», i.e. his deed is accepted; then He mentioned this immediately after it and made clear that the deed of the unbeliever is not accepted.
The words of Ibn Hishām in al-Mughnī: «وحرام على قرية أهلكناها أنهم لا يرجعون». It was said that «لا» is redundant, and the meaning is: it is impossible for the people of a town whose destruction We decreed because of their unbelief that they return from unbelief until the Hour arises. On this view «حرام» is a fronted khabar of necessity, because the subject of the predication is «أن» with its complement, like «وآية لهم أنا حملنا ذريتهم»; it is not a mubtadaʾ with «أن» and its complement as a fāʿil that dispenses with a khabar, as Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed, because it is not an explicit adjective, and because it does not rest on a negation or a question. It was also said that «لا» is negative, and the parsing is either as above, with the meaning "it is impossible for them that they not return to the Hereafter"; or on the view that «حرام» is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, i.e. "the acceptance of their deeds" (it begins with an indefinite noun because it is restricted by its complement); or that it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "and righteous deed is forbidden to them". On both views «فانهم لا يرجعون» is a reason with an implied lām, the meaning being: "their deeds are not returned in it". The evidence for what is omitted is the preceding saying of the Exalted: «فَمَنْ يَعْمَلْ مِنَ الصَّالِحاتِ وَهُوَ مُؤْمِنٌ فَلا كُفْرانَ لِسَعْيِهِ».
(حَتَّى إِذا فُتِحَتْ يَأْجُوجُ وَمَأْجُوجُ وَهُمْ مِنْ كُلِّ حَدَبٍ يَنْسِلُونَ) «حتى» is a particle of limit and genitive; it is the limit of the impossibility of returning, so it is attached to «حرام», in the sense that it is a particle of limit and genitive. It may also be inceptive (ibtidāʾiyya), which is the one after which speech is reported; the reported speech here is the conditional clause and its apodosis. «وإذا» is an adverb for the future, and the apodosis to which «إذا» is attached is omitted, its implied form being "they said: O woe to us!". Al-Zamakhsharī and others preferred that the apodosis be the fāʾ that enters «إذا» of surprise (idhā al-fujāʾiyya), for when the fāʾ comes with it the two support and help each other in linking the apodosis to the condition, so it is strengthened; and had it been said "idhā hiya shākhiṣa" or "fa-hiya shākhiṣa", it would have been sound. [Translator's note: the sentence is somewhat compressed in the source; this is a literal rendering.] Abū Ḥayyān preferred that «حتى» be a preposition attached to «تقطعوا», despite the distance involved. He said: "That «حتى» is a preposition attached to «تقطعوا» involves, in terms of the great separation, some remoteness, but in terms of meaning it is good, namely that they continue to differ over the religion of truth until close to the coming of the Hour; when the Hour comes, that ceases." «وفتحت» is a past passive verb; «ويأجوج ومأجوج» is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); an omitted muḍāf must be implied, namely "their barrier". The wāw is circumstantial; «وهم» is the mubtadaʾ and its khabar is the clause «ينسلون»; «ومن كل حدب» is attached to «ينسلون».
(وَاقْتَرَبَ الْوَعْدُ الْحَقُّ فَإِذا هِيَ شاخِصَةٌ أَبْصارُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا) The wāw is a conjunction; «واقترب الوعد»: verb and agent; «والحق» is an adjective of «الوعد»; the fāʾ is the linking fāʾ; «وإذا» is the idhā of surprise, whose discussion has already been given; «وهي» is the mubtadaʾ and «وشاخصة» the khabar; «وأبصار الذين كفروا» is the agent of «شاخصة».
(يا وَيْلَنا قَدْ كُنَّا فِي غَفْلَةٍ مِنْ هذا بَلْ كُنَّا ظالِمِينَ) The vocative is attached to an omitted saying, in the position of accusative as ḥāl, i.e. "saying, 'O woe to us! Come, for this is your time'". «وقد» is a particle of affirmation; kāna and its noun, and «وفي غفلة» is its khabar; «ومن هذا» is attached to «غفلة». «بل» is a particle of rectification (iḍrāb); kāna, its noun and its khabar. All these clauses are the content of their omitted saying.
(إِنَّكُمْ وَما تَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ حَصَبُ جَهَنَّمَ أَنْتُمْ لَها وارِدُونَ) «إن» and its noun; the clause is inceptive; «وما» is conjoined to the kāf; the clause «تعبدون» is the ṣila; «ومن دون الله» is a ḥāl; «وحصب جهنم» is the khabar of «إنكم»; the clause «أنتم لها واردون» is a nominal clause of mubtadaʾ and khabar in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from «جهنم». But there is the objection that a ḥāl from the muḍāf ilayhi has not occurred in their speech except conditionally. It may also be a badal from «حصب جهنم», or a second khabar of «إن»; others allowed it to be resumptive.
(لَوْ كانَ هؤُلاءِ آلِهَةً ما وَرَدُوها وَكُلٌّ فِيها خالِدُونَ) «لو» is a conditional of impossibility (shartiyya imtināʿiyya); «وكان» is a defective past verb; «وهؤلاء» is its noun and «وآلهة» its khabar; the clause «ما وردوها» has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of «لو»; the wāw is circumstantial; «وكل» is the mubtadaʾ; «وفيها» is attached to «خالدون»; and «وخالدون» is the khabar.
(لَهُمْ فِيها زَفِيرٌ وَهُمْ فِيها لا يَسْمَعُونَ) «لهم» is a fronted khabar; «وفيها» is a ḥāl; «وزفير» is a postponed mubtadaʾ; the wāw is a conjunction; «وهم» is the mubtadaʾ; «وفيها» is attached to «يسمعون»; and the clause «لا يسمعون» is their khabar.

* Rhetoric:
The kalāmī method (al-madhhab al-kalāmī): in His saying «إِنَّكُمْ وَما تَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ حَصَبُ جَهَنَّمَ أَنْتُمْ لَها وارِدُونَ لَوْ كانَ هؤُلاءِ آلِهَةً ما وَرَدُوها وَكُلٌّ فِيها خالِدُونَ» is the kalāmī method, to which reference has already been made; we shall expand on it here, and say:
When it is established that the kalāmī method is the speaker's arguing for what he wishes to prove by an argument that cuts off the obstinate opponent, in the manner of the masters of kalām, or the drawing of sound conclusions from true premises, as will come in Sūrat al-Ḥajj, then the verse we are dealing with entails that these idols and images are not gods: for were they gods, they would not be fuel of Hell, as was said before that the corollary of His saying «لَوْ كانَ فِيهِما آلِهَةٌ إِلَّا اللَّهُ لَفَسَدَتا» is, in implied form: "but the two did not go to ruin, so there are no gods in them but Allah." Of the second type, the saying of the Exalted was discussed in Sūrat al-Aʿrāf: «وَلا يَدْخُلُونَ الْجَنَّةَ حَتَّى يَلِجَ الْجَمَلُ فِي سَمِّ الْخِياطِ». The way of drawing the conclusion in this sentence from the two premises is to say: the unbelievers will never enter Paradise until the camel passes through the eye of the needle; the camel never passes through the eye of the needle; so they will never enter Paradise, because making a condition depend on something impossible entails the impossibility of the conditioned thing's occurrence.
Of the kalāmī method is the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "If you knew what I know, you would laugh little and weep much." The completion of the proof is to say: "But you laugh much and weep little, so you do not know what I know." Similar is the saying of Mālik b. al-Murajjal al-Andalusī:
لو يكون الحب وصلا كله ... لم تكن غايته إلا الملل
أو يكون الحب هجرا كله ... لم تكن غايته إلا الأجل
إنما الوصل كمثل الماء لا ... يستطاب الماء إلا بالغلل
(If love were all union, its end would be nothing but weariness. / Or if love were all desertion, its end would be nothing but death. / Union is only like water: water is not found sweet except after thirst.)
The first two verses are a conditional syllogism and the third a juristic analogy: he drew an analogy of union with water; as water is not found sweet except after thirst, so union is likewise not found sweet except after the heat of desertion. As for categorical syllogisms, they derived them in various forms; among them what is related that a Tamīmī poet came to Abū Dulaf, who said to him: "Where are you from?" He said: "From Tamīm," and Abū Dulaf said:
تميم بطرق اللؤم اهدى من القطا ... ولو سلكت سبل الهداية ضلت
(Tamīm, in the ways of meanness, is better guided than the sandgrouse, and were it to take the paths of guidance, it would go astray.)
The Tamīmī said: "Yes, it was by that guidance that I came to you." So he silenced him with a categorical proof by which he obliged him to admit that coming to him is misguidance. By my life, the conditional syllogism is clearer in indication in this field than others, sweeter to the taste and easier in composition, for it is a sentence occurring after «لو» with its apodosis, and this sentence, in their terminology, is a connected conditional premise by which the preceding ruling is argued.
Ibn Rashīq said in Kitāb al-ʿUmda: "Ibn al-Muʿtazz mentioned that al-Jāḥiẓ called this type the kalāmī method. Ibn al-Muʿtazz said: 'This is a chapter of which I do not know that I have found anything in the Qur'an, and it is attributed to artificiality, exalted is Allah far above that.'" Both Ibn Rashīq and Ibn al-Muʿtazz overlooked that the Qur'an is full of this type, as you have seen and as will come later. Ibn Rashīq, however, observed another point about Ibn al-Muʿtazz, saying: "Ibn al-Muʿtazz concluded with this chapter the five chapters of badīʿ that he singled out with this name and put before the others, and he cited for al-Farazdaq:
لكل امرئ نفسان: نفس كريمة ... وأخرى يعاصيها الفتى ويطيعها
ونفسك من نفسيك تشفع للندى ... إذا قل من احرارهن شفيعها
(Every man has two selves: a noble self, and another that the man disobeys and obeys. / Your self, of your two selves, intercedes for generosity, when the intercessor from among their free ones is few.)
and he cited for another, and I think it is none other than Ibrāhīm b. al-ʿAbbās:
وعلمتني كيف الهوى وجهلته ... وعلمكم صبري على ظلمكم ظلمي
فأعلم ما لي عندكم فيميل بي ... هواي إلى جهلي وأعرض عن ظلمي
(You taught me how to love, and I was ignorant of it, and you know my patience under your wronging me, my wronging.)
(So I know what I have with you, and my passion inclines me to my ignorance and I turn away from my wronging.)
and he faulted Abū Tammām for his saying:
فالمجد لا يرضى بأن ترضى بأن ... يرضى المؤمل منك إلا بالرضا
(Glory is not content that you be content that the one who hopes of you be content except with contentment.)
[Translator's note: the verse is quoted in the source without continuing punctuation and the following narrative is run directly into it; the line is translated as it stands, and its sense is deliberately tangled, which is the very fault under discussion.]
It is related that Isḥāq al-Mawṣilī heard al-Ṭāʾī recite and use much of this type and its like in the presence of al-Ḥasan b. Wahb, and he said: "O you, you have scattered (shadhdhartā) against yourself." In my view the criticism is directed at Abū Tammām in his verse not from the side of the kalāmī method which he followed but from the side of the verbal convolution in it.
Of the charming examples of this method is what Ibn Rashīq cited for Ibn al-Muʿtazz, namely his saying:
أسرفت في الكتمان ... وذاك مني دهاني
كتمت حبّك حتى ... كتمته كتماني
ولم يكن لي بد ... من ذكره بلساني
(I went to excess in concealment, and that of me afflicted me. / I concealed your love until I concealed my very concealing of it. / And I had no choice but to mention it with my tongue.)
He said: "This is charm itself, and elegance itself."
Abū Nuwās said:
سخنت من شدة البرودة حتى ... صرت عندي كأنك النار
لا يعجب السامعون صفتي ... كذلك الثلج بارد حار
(You were so intensely cold that you became hot, to my mind, as if you were fire. / Let not listeners wonder at my description: so too ice is cold and hot.)
This is a philosophical kalāmī method, and also his saying:
فيك خلاف لخلاف الذي ... فيه خلاف لخلاف الجميل
(In you is a disagreement with the disagreement of the one in whom is a disagreement with the disagreement of the beautiful.)
Abū Tammām can be considered the master of a special way in the kalāmī method. Listen to his saying on envy:
وإذا أراد الله نشر فضيلة ... طويت أتاح لها لسان حسود
لولا اشتعال النار فيما جاورت ... ما كان يعرف طيب عرف العود
(When Allah wills to spread a virtue that has been folded away, He provides for it the tongue of an envier. / Were it not for the fire's blazing in what lies next to it, the sweetness of the scent of aloes-wood would not be known.)
And among the flowers of Bahāʾ al-Dīn Zuhayr is his saying:
يا من أكابد فيه ما أكابده ... مولاي أصبر حتى يحكم الله
سميت غيرك محبوبي مغالطة ... لمعشر فيك قد فاهوا بما فاهوا
أقول زيد وزيد لست أعرفه ... وإنما هو لفظ أنت معناه
وكم ذكرت مسمّى لا اكتراث به ... حتى يجر إلى ذكراك ذكراه
أتيه فيك على العشاق كلهم ... قد عز من أنت، يا مولاي، مولاه
كادت عيونهم بالبغض تنطق لي ... حتى كأن عيون الناس أفواه
(O you for whom I suffer what I suffer, my lord, I shall be patient until Allah decides. / I called someone other than you my beloved, to mislead a company who have blurted out what they blurted about you. / I say "Zayd, and Zayd", whom I do not know, but it is only a word of which you are the meaning. / How many a named one I have mentioned of no concern to me, until its mention drew on the mention of you. / I am proud over all lovers on your account; he is mighty whose master, my lord, you are. / Their eyes almost spoke to me with hatred, until the eyes of people seemed to be mouths.)

dervis-irab:101-105.t:
* Vocabulary:
(السِّجِلِّ): the book of covenants and the book of judgments; a book in which the judge writes down the form of claims and the ruling in them, and deeds of sale and the like, so that they remain preserved with him. Its plural is sijillāt. One says sajjala al-rajul: he wrote the sijill; sajjala al-awrāq: he registered the papers in the courts; sajjala al-qāḍī ʿalayhi: the judge pronounced judgment on him; sajjala ʿalayhi bi-kadhā: he made him notorious for it and branded him; and sajjala lahu bi-mālihi: he confirmed it and established it for him.

* I'rab:
(إِنَّ الَّذِينَ سَبَقَتْ لَهُمْ مِنَّا الْحُسْنى أُولئِكَ عَنْها مُبْعَدُونَ) «إن» and its noun; the clause «سبقت» is the ṣila (relative clause); «ولهم» is attached to «سبقت»; «ومنّا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial); «والحسنى» is the fāʿil (agent); «وأولئك» is the mubtadaʾ; «وعنها» is attached to «مبعدون»; «ومبعدون» is the khabar of «أولئك»; the clause «أولئك عنها مبعدون» is the khabar of «إن»; and the clause «إن» etc. is inceptive.
(لا يَسْمَعُونَ حَسِيسَها وَهُمْ فِي مَا اشْتَهَتْ أَنْفُسُهُمْ خالِدُونَ) The clause «لا يسمعون حسيسها» admits several analyses: it may be a badal (substitute) for «مبعدون» because it takes its place and dispenses with it; it may be a second khabar of «أولئك»; and it may be a ḥāl from the pronoun of «مبعدون». «لا» is negative; «ويسمعون حسيسها» is an imperfect verb, nominative, with its agent and direct object. The wāw is circumstantial or resumptive; «وهم» is the mubtadaʾ; «وفيما» is attached to «خالدون»; the clause «اشتهت أنفسهم» is the ṣila; and «وخالدون» is their khabar.
(لا يَحْزُنُهُمُ الْفَزَعُ الْأَكْبَرُ وَتَتَلَقَّاهُمُ الْمَلائِكَةُ هذا يَوْمُكُمُ الَّذِي كُنْتُمْ تُوعَدُونَ) The clause is circumstantial, or a badal for the preceding clause. «لا» is negative; «ويحزنهم»: verb and direct object; «والفزع» is the agent; «والأكبر» is an adjective of «الفزع»; «وتتلقاهم الملائكة»: verb, direct object and agent. The clause «هذا يومكم» is the content of an omitted saying occupying the position of a ḥāl, i.e. "saying: This is your day"; «وهذا» is the mubtadaʾ and «ويومكم» the khabar; «والذي» is an adjective of «يومكم»; the clause «كنتم» is the ṣila; kāna and its noun; and the clause «توعدون» is the khabar of «كنتم».
(يَوْمَ نَطْوِي السَّماءَ كَطَيِّ السِّجِلِّ لِلْكُتُبِ) The adverb is attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being "remember"; you may attach it to «لا يحزنهم», or to «الفزع», or to «تتلقاهم الملائكة». The clause «نطوي» is in the position of genitive, the adverb being annexed to it; the agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "we (naḥnu)"; «والسماء» is the direct object; «وكطي»: the kāf is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "as a man folds his page in order to write in it"; so al-ṭayy is a maṣdar annexed to its object, and omission of the agent with the maṣdar is regular and continual. «وللكتب» is attached to «طي», the lām serving to strengthen transitivity, i.e. "for the writings, all of them", that is, for the many things of meaning that are written in it.
(كَما بَدَأْنا أَوَّلَ خَلْقٍ نُعِيدُهُ وَعْداً عَلَيْنا إِنَّا كُنَّا فاعِلِينَ) The kāf is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar; «وما» is maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun); «وبدأنا»: verb and agent; «وأول خلق» is the direct object of «بدأنا», i.e. "We shall restore the first creation in a restoring like Our beginning of it"; al-Zamakhsharī always makes «ما» a restraining particle (kāffa) for the kāf. «ووعدا» is a maṣdar made accusative by an implied «وعدنا» before it, and is an absolute object (mafʿūl muṭlaq) confirming the content of what precedes; «وعلينا» is attached to «وعدا»; «وإن» and its noun; the clause «كنا» is the khabar of «إنا»; kāna and its noun; «وفاعلين» is its khabar. The clause «إنا» is causal, serving as emphasis on the power to do that; Abū Ḥayyān in al-Baḥr implied it as "that is, we are able to do that"; al-ʿImādī preferred that it be circumstantial and implied it as "that is, making this promise come true, so prepare for it". Important benefits on this verse will come in the sections on Benefits and Rhetoric. [Translator's note: this entry in the data contains no separate Benefits section; the author's cross-reference is translated as written.]
(وَلَقَدْ كَتَبْنا فِي الزَّبُورِ مِنْ بَعْدِ الذِّكْرِ أَنَّ الْأَرْضَ يَرِثُها عِبادِيَ الصَّالِحُونَ) The wāw is resumptive, and the clause is resumptive, brought to establish that the earth belongs to the righteous, for them to exploit its resources and the energies stored within it. The lām is the answer to an omitted oath; «وقد» is a particle of affirmation; «وكتبنا»: verb and agent; «وفي الزبور» is attached to «كتبنا»; «ومن بعد» is attached to an omitted element serving as a ḥāl from «الزبور»; «وأن» and what is in its scope is the object of «كتبنا», i.e. "We wrote the inheritance of the earth"; «وإن» and its noun, and the clause «يرثها» its khabar; «وعبادي» is the agent and «والصالحون» an adjective.

* Rhetoric:
1- Exaggeration (mubālagha): in His saying «لا يَسْمَعُونَ حَسِيسَها» there is the art of exaggeration, because someone might say: "When the people of Paradise have settled in their abodes there, what glad tidings is there for them in that they do not hear its faintest sound?" The answer is that it is an emphatic exaggeration, and that it (Hell) will never come near them; for whoever is close to it hears, without doubt, its faintest sound, because the people of the Fire are in levels (darakāt) arranged in accordance with the number of its inhabitants and of those who enter it, and in accordance with the number of their objects of worship. For that reason the Exalted said in another verse «لَها سَبْعَةُ أَبْوابٍ لِكُلِّ بابٍ مِنْهُمْ جُزْءٌ مَقْسُومٌ», and the detail of that will come in Sūrat al-Ḥijr. It is related that ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, recited this verse, «إِنَّ الَّذِينَ سَبَقَتْ لَهُمْ مِنَّا الْحُسْنى أُولئِكَ عَنْها مُبْعَدُونَ», and then said: "I am one of them, and Abū Bakr and ʿUmar and ʿUthmān and Ṭalḥa and al-Zubayr and Saʿd and Saʿīd and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. ʿAwf." Then the prayer was called and he stood up dragging his cloak, saying: «لا يَسْمَعُونَ حَسِيسَها».
2- Simile (tashbīh): in His saying «كَما بَدَأْنا أَوَّلَ خَلْقٍ نُعِيدُهُ» there is a likening of the restoration to the beginning, in that power reaches both equally. Al-Zamakhsharī said:
"If you say: What is the first creation that He should restore it as He began it? I say: Its first is bringing it into being from nothing, so as He brought it into being first from nothing, He restores it a second time from nothing. If you say: Why is «خلق» indefinite? I say: It is like your saying 'he is the first man who came to me', meaning the first of the men, but you made it singular and indefinite, wishing to itemise them man by man; so likewise the meaning of 'first creation' is the first of creation, in the sense of the first of created things, because khalq is a maṣdar that is not pluralised. There is another aspect, that the kāf is made accusative by an implied verb that «نعيده» explains, and «ما» is a relative: 'We restore the like of that which We began, We restore it'; and «أول خلق» is an adverbial expression attached to «بدأناه», i.e. 'the first of what He created', or a ḥāl from the pronoun of the relative, which has dropped out of the wording but is established in the meaning."
